name: _woa-pr-build-test

# The WoA pipeline for an approved upstream PR, called by `upstream-pull.yml`
# pinned to the head SHA a maintainer approved. It is `windows-woa-build-test.yml`
# minus everything a pull request must not reach:
#
#   * No publication. GitHub makes a caller grant every permission any nested
#     job requests - before `if:` is evaluated - and the nightly's `publication`
#     job requests `contents: write`. Calling this file instead, the PR path
#     grants read only, so it never holds publication scope.
#   * No HUD reporting. A PR head is not a nightly of upstream main, so it has
#     no row to file against.
#   * No ref resolution for pytorch: the ref must already be a full SHA.
#
# The build and test jobs are the nightly's own - same matrix, names and
# inputs - so a PR is validated the way a nightly is built, and HUD-style job
# names read the same in both. `scripts/pr-gate/tests/test_woa_pr_pipeline.py`
# keeps the two files in step.
#
#   prep -> build matrix -> test matrix -> test-summary

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      pytorch-ref:
        description: "Full 40-hex commit SHA to build: the PR's approved head."
        type: string
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read

jobs:
  prep:
    name: resolve pytorch ref
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      pytorch-ref: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.pytorch-ref }}
      torchaudio-ref: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.torchaudio-ref }}
      torchvision-ref: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.torchvision-ref }}
      nightly-date: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.nightly-date }}
      num-shards: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.num-shards }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository (for prep scripts)
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      - name: Resolve source refs to commit SHAs
        id: ref
        shell: bash
        env:
          REF: ${{ inputs.pytorch-ref }}
          AUDIO_REF: "main"
          VISION_REF: "main"
          NUM_SHARDS: "4"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/source-refs/resolve_ref.sh
          # The gate pinned the approved head; anything else is refused rather
          # than resolved, so what builds is exactly what was approved.
          require_sha pytorch "${REF}" "${REF}"
          # No nightly release to take a date from; the wheel is dated today.
          nightly_date="$(date -u +%Y%m%d)"
          audio_sha="$(resolve_ref "https://github.com/pytorch/audio" "${AUDIO_REF}")";   require_sha torchaudio  "${audio_sha}"  "${AUDIO_REF}"
          vision_sha="$(resolve_ref "https://github.com/pytorch/vision" "${VISION_REF}")"; require_sha torchvision "${vision_sha}" "${VISION_REF}"
          echo "pytorch ${REF}, torchaudio '${AUDIO_REF}' -> ${audio_sha}, torchvision '${VISION_REF}' -> ${vision_sha}"
          {
            echo "pytorch-ref=${REF}"
            echo "torchaudio-ref=${audio_sha}"
            echo "torchvision-ref=${vision_sha}"
            echo "nightly-date=${nightly_date}"
            echo "num-shards=${NUM_SHARDS}"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          {
            echo "## WoA PR build-test config"
            echo ""
            echo "| field | value |"
            echo "| --- | --- |"
            echo "| pytorch-ref (approved head) | \`${REF}\` |"
            echo "| torchaudio-ref (resolved SHA) | \`${audio_sha}\` |"
            echo "| torchvision-ref (resolved SHA) | \`${vision_sha}\` |"
            echo "| wheel date | \`${nightly_date}\` |"
            echo "| shards | \`${NUM_SHARDS}\` |"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  build:
    name: woa-${{ matrix.config.label }}-cu134-build
    needs: prep
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The nightly's `config` list, cell for cell, including its TEMPORARY
        # narrowing to 3.13.
        config: &config
          # - { version: "3.11", label: "py311" }
          # - { version: "3.12", label: "py312" }
          - { version: "3.13", label: "py313" }
          # - { version: "3.14", label: "py314" }
          # - { version: "3.14t", label: "py314t" }
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_woa-build.yml
    with:
      runner-base: woa-arm64
      python-version: ${{ matrix.config.version }}
      python-label: ${{ matrix.config.label }}
      cuda-version: "13.4"
      cuda-arch-list: "8.9;10.3+PTX;12.0;12.1+PTX"
      build-environment: win-woa-arm64
      pytorch-ref: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.pytorch-ref }}
      nightly-date: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.nightly-date }}
      torchaudio-ref: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.torchaudio-ref }}
      torchvision-ref: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.torchvision-ref }}
      wheel-artifact: woa-${{ matrix.config.label }}-cu134-${{ github.run_id }}

  test:
    name: woa-${{ matrix.config.label }}-cu134-arm64-test
    needs: [prep, build]
    # As in the nightly: cells that built are tested even when another cell's
    # build failed.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.build.result != 'skipped' }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config: *config
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_woa-test.yml
    with:
      runner-base: woa-arm64
      python-version: ${{ matrix.config.version }}
      python-label: ${{ matrix.config.label }}
      cuda-version: "13.4"
      cuda-arch-list: "8.9;10.3+PTX;12.0;12.1+PTX"
      build-environment: win-woa-arm64
      test-config: "default"
      num-shards: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.num-shards }}
      wheel-artifact: woa-${{ matrix.config.label }}-cu134-${{ github.run_id }}

  test-summary:
    name: test-summary
    needs: test
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout this repository (for summary script)
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      - name: Aggregate failed test jobs
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh api --paginate \
            "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/attempts/${{ github.run_attempt }}/jobs" \
            -q '.jobs[]' | jq -s '.' > jobs.json
          python3 scripts/test-summary/aggregate_failures.py \
            --jobs-json jobs.json \
            --title "PyTorch WoA test summary (run ${{ github.run_id }})" \
            >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Download all shard test-reports
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: test-reports-*
          path: all-reports

      - name: Aggregate failed tests across shards
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python3 scripts/test-summary/parse_failures.py \
            --shards-root all-reports \
            --title "Aggregate failed tests - all shards (run ${{ github.run_id }})" \
            >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: _woa-test

# Reusable Windows-on-Arm (WoA) test workflow. The arm64 analog of
# `_rtx-test.yml`, but with a single install path: the wheels are always a
# producer-uploaded GitHub Actions artifact from `_woa-build.yml` (no pip-index
# path - this repo only runs the build-test flow for WoA). The built pytorch
# SHA travels with the wheels in `built_pytorch_sha.txt`, so the test checkout
# pins the exact source that produced the wheel.
#
# One invocation is a single WoA test cell for the given Python (py311..py314 or
# free-threaded py314t), CTK 13.4; the orchestrator calls it once per built
# version. Sharding is an internal fan-out: the `setup` job turns `num-shards`
# into the shard list and `strategy.matrix.shard` spawns that many parallel jobs.
# The test step exports SHARD_NUMBER / NUM_TEST_SHARDS to the vendored PowerShell
# test entrypoint, which drives test/run_test.py.
#
# Runners: the same PERSISTENT shared arm64 pool (`woa-arm64`) used for build,
# carrying only clean ARM64 interpreters (no pre-built venvs). `woa-preflight-test`
# additionally asserts a GPU is visible, `woa-create-venv` builds a FRESH throwaway
# venv for this cell from the clean interpreter (then the built wheels are installed
# into it), and `woa-strict-clean` scrubs job state (including the venv) at start + end.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner-base:
        description: "Runner label for the shared WoA build+test pool."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "woa-arm64"
      python-version:
        description: "Python version in dotted form (e.g. 3.13, or 3.14t for free-threaded)."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "3.13"
      python-label:
        description: "Python label selecting the venv (py311 | py312 | py313 | py314 | py314t)."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "py313"
      cuda-version:
        description: "CUDA toolkit version in dotted form (13.4)."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "13.4"
      cuda-arch-list:
        description: "TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST for the test step."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "8.9;10.3+PTX;12.0;12.1+PTX"
      build-environment:
        description: "Logical name passed through as BUILD_ENVIRONMENT."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "win-woa-arm64"
      test-config:
        description: "Test-config name forwarded as TEST_CONFIG."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "default"
      num-shards:
        description: "Number of parallel test shards. Drives the shard matrix (see the setup job) - the single source of truth for the count."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "4"
      wheel-artifact:
        description: "Artifact name carrying the wheels + built_pytorch_sha.txt (required)."
        type: string
        required: true

      # ---- matrix subset filter ----------------------------------------------
      python-versions:
        description: "Comma-separated allowlist of python versions; empty = no filter."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read

jobs:
  # Turn `num-shards` into the shard list [1..N] so the matrix always matches the
  # requested count (no silently-omitted or invalid shards). Cheap GitHub-hosted job.
  setup:
    name: shard plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # Token-exact match (comma-delimited) so "3.14" does not also match "3.14t".
    if: >
      inputs.python-versions == '' ||
      contains(format(',{0},', inputs.python-versions), format(',{0},', inputs.python-version))
    outputs:
      shards: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.shards }}
    steps:
      - name: Compute shard list from num-shards
        id: plan
        shell: bash
        env:
          NUM_SHARDS: ${{ inputs.num-shards }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          n="${NUM_SHARDS}"
          if ! [[ "${n}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::num-shards must be a positive integer; got '${n}'." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          shards="$(seq -s, 1 "${n}")"
          echo "shards=[${shards}]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shard plan: [${shards}]"

  test:
    name: test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ inputs.num-shards }})
    needs: setup
    # Token-exact match (comma-delimited) so "3.14" does not also match "3.14t".
    if: >
      inputs.python-versions == '' ||
      contains(format(',{0},', inputs.python-versions), format(',{0},', inputs.python-version))
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Shard list generated from `num-shards` by the setup job - the count is
        # controlled by that one input, no hardcoded shard numbers here.
        shard: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.shards) }}
    runs-on:
      - ${{ inputs.runner-base }}
    timeout-minutes: 240
    env:
      BUILD_ENVIRONMENT: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
      PYTHON_VERSION: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
      PYTHON_LABEL: ${{ inputs.python-label }}
      CUDA_VERSION: ${{ inputs.cuda-version }}
      TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: ${{ inputs.cuda-arch-list }}
      USE_CUDA: "1"
      CONTINUE_THROUGH_ERROR: "1"
      CI: "1"
      # ---- WoA preinstall contract (single-drive C: runners; docs/woa-ci-plan.md) -------
      # Expected install paths on every woa-arm64 runner (single C: drive).
      WOA_CUDA_PATH: 'C:\Program Files\NVIDIA\CUDA\v13.4'
      WOA_CUDNN_ROOT: 'C:\Program Files\NVIDIA\CUDNN\v9.26'
      PT_ROOT: 'C:\pt'
      WOA_SCRATCH: 'C:\ci\woa\scratch'
      # Fresh per-job venv + pip cache pinned inside scratch (strict-clean wipes both);
      # no cross-job wheel cache survives on these public-facing runners.
      WOA_VENV_DIR: 'C:\ci\woa\scratch\venv'
      PIP_CACHE_DIR: 'C:\ci\woa\scratch\pipcache'
      # ---- hang bounds -----------------------------------------------------
      # The vendored entrypoint owns two of the three bounds, and its versions
      # are better integrated than anything set here could be, so only their
      # values are touched - never PYTEST_ADDOPTS, which it exports itself:
      #   per test    tools/woa-build/pytorch-windows-test-shard.ps1 exports
      #               PYTEST_ADDOPTS from
      #               PYTORCH_WIN_TEST_PER_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 900,
      #               left alone: pytest-timeout fired zero times across
      #               the 1,457 invocations of a four-shard run).
      #   per shard   the same script runs run_test.py under a wall-clock
      #               watchdog from PYTORCH_WIN_TEST_RUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC,
      #               and on expiry kills the tree and synthesizes an
      #               attributed JUnit report, which a bare taskkill cannot.
      #
      # That watchdog is lowered from its 12600 default because at 210min it
      # could not fire inside the 240min job cap. It bounds the run_test.py
      # call only, so wheel download, venv, install and seed spend the cap
      # without counting against it - and on this pool those take 41-45min,
      # leaving 30min of budget for a 210min bound. A public arm64 shard was
      # cancelled 17min short of its own watchdog after run_test.py had been
      # wedged for 193min. At 180min the bound clears a 45min setup with
      # ~15min left for the kill, the JUnit synthesis, the summary and the
      # upload - which is the whole point of failing rather than being
      # cancelled.
      PYTORCH_WIN_TEST_RUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC: "10800"
      #
      # What neither covers is a single test file freezing where pytest-timeout
      # cannot see - during import, collection, or teardown after the last test
      # - because the shard watchdog's only move there is to kill the whole
      # shard. That gap is what this bound closes, enforced from inside the
      # test-file process by scripts/test-bounds/pythonpath/sitecustomize.py.
      #
      # 30min, and the floor is the per-test bound rather than the workload:
      # at 2x its 15min, pytest-timeout always gets first refusal at an in-test
      # hang, which matters because it can name the hung test where this bound
      # can only name the file. It also clears the slowest healthy invocation
      # measured with the seeded stats live - 13.9min of 1,457 - by 2.2x.
      # Earlier arm64 logs showed a 53.4min invocation, but those
      # predate the seeding: with no cost for a file run_test.py cannot
      # pytest-split it, so test_meta ran whole. Across those 17 logs zero
      # files were split; across this run's four, fourteen were.
      PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SEC: "1800"
      # Where each armed test-file process appends one JSON line, and where the
      # step after the test run reads them back from. Both need it, so it is
      # job-level; the literal repeats PT_ROOT above because a job-level `env`
      # entry cannot reference a sibling one. Extension matters -
      # parse_failures.py scans this tree for *.log / *.txt, so a .log here
      # would be fed to the failure parser.
      PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_LOG: 'C:\pt/test/test-reports/per-process-bound.jsonl'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout OOT tooling repo
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          path: oot
          show-progress: false
          # Don't retain the job token in oot/.git/config while the test workload runs.
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Strict clean (pre)
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/woa-strict-clean
        with:
          phase: pre
          pt-root: ${{ env.PT_ROOT }}
          scratch-root: ${{ env.WOA_SCRATCH }}

      - name: Preflight test toolchain + GPU
        id: preflight
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/woa-preflight-test
        with:
          python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
          python-label: ${{ inputs.python-label }}
          cuda-path: ${{ env.WOA_CUDA_PATH }}
          cudnn-root: ${{ env.WOA_CUDNN_ROOT }}

      # Build a FRESH, throwaway venv for this cell from the clean interpreter and install the
      # WoA TEST deps (woa-base.txt + woa-test.txt strict, + woa-test-extended.txt best-effort).
      # The built wheels are added on top below. Lives under scratch so strict-clean wipes it.
      - name: Create job venv
        id: venv
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/woa-create-venv
        with:
          role: test
          python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
          python-label: ${{ inputs.python-label }}
          venv-path: ${{ env.WOA_VENV_DIR }}\${{ inputs.python-label }}

      # Retried in three attempts. The action's own five retries all reuse a
      # single blob-storage redirect URL inside one attempt, so when that URL
      # goes bad mid-transfer they fail together and take the shard with them
      # before it runs a test (seen on the rtx path, same artifact shape).
      # Only a fresh attempt asks for a new redirect.
      - name: Download wheels artifact
        id: wheel_1
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.wheel-artifact }}
          path: artifact

      # Clear the half-extracted tree first: the next step reads
      # `artifact/built_pytorch_sha.txt`, and a truncated wheel would
      # otherwise resurface later as an install or import error.
      - name: Wait before wheels download retry
        if: steps.wheel_1.outcome == 'failure'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          rm -rf artifact
          sleep 60

      - name: Download wheels artifact (retry 2)
        id: wheel_2
        if: steps.wheel_1.outcome == 'failure'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.wheel-artifact }}
          path: artifact

      - name: Wait before final wheels download retry
        if: steps.wheel_1.outcome == 'failure' && steps.wheel_2.outcome == 'failure'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          rm -rf artifact
          sleep 120

      - name: Download wheels artifact (retry 3)
        if: steps.wheel_1.outcome == 'failure' && steps.wheel_2.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.wheel-artifact }}
          path: artifact

      - name: Resolve pytorch ref from artifact
        id: ref
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ref=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < artifact/built_pytorch_sha.txt)
          if ! [[ "$ref" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Invalid SHA in artifact: '$ref'" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "ref=$ref" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "checkout ref: $ref"

      - name: Enable git long paths
        shell: bash
        run: git config --global core.longpaths true

      - name: Checkout pytorch/pytorch at the built ref
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          repository: pytorch/pytorch
          ref: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.ref }}
          submodules: recursive
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false
          path: pytorch
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Relocate pytorch checkout to a short path
        shell: cmd
        run: |
          move "%GITHUB_WORKSPACE%\pytorch" "%PT_ROOT%"
          if errorlevel 1 (
            echo ::error::Failed to relocate pytorch checkout to %PT_ROOT%
            exit /b 1
          )
          echo Relocated pytorch checkout to %PT_ROOT%

      - name: Record pytorch HEAD (SHA + commit date)
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ env.PT_ROOT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          date_iso=$(git log -1 --format=%cI HEAD)
          date_ymd=$(TZ=UTC git log -1 --date=format-local:%Y%m%d --format=%cd HEAD)
          {
            echo "## pytorch checkout"
            echo ""
            echo "| field      | value |"
            echo "| ---        | --- |"
            echo "| input ref  | \`${{ steps.ref.outputs.ref }}\` |"
            echo "| HEAD sha   | \`$sha\` |"
            echo "| committed  | \`$date_iso\` |"
            echo "| dev tag    | \`dev$date_ymd\` |"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Install the built wheels into this cell's fresh venv. The cuda_embed torch wheel
      # is the distributable one (DLLs embedded), so prefer it over any vanilla
      # torch wheel that may also be present; then add the extension wheels.
      - name: Install PyTorch + extensions
        shell: powershell
        env:
          VENV_ACTIVATE: ${{ steps.venv.outputs.venv-activate }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          & $env:VENV_ACTIVATE
          $dist = Join-Path $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE "artifact"

          # $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' does NOT make a native pip nonzero exit throw,
          # so check $LASTEXITCODE after every pip call and fail explicitly.
          function Invoke-Pip { param([string[]]$PipArgs)
            python -m pip @PipArgs
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "pip $($PipArgs -join ' ') failed with exit $LASTEXITCODE" }
          }

          # torch is required. Prefer the cuda_embed wheel (DLLs embedded).
          $torch = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $dist -Filter "torch-*.whl" |
            Sort-Object { if ($_.Name -match "cuda_embed|cuda-embed") { 0 } else { 1 } } |
            Select-Object -First 1
          if (-not $torch) { Write-Host "::error::No torch wheel in artifact"; exit 1 }
          Invoke-Pip @("install", $torch.FullName)

          # Extensions are non-blocking: a missing wheel (failed build) only warns, but if a
          # wheel IS present its install must succeed (a failed install is a real error).
          $installedExts = @()
          foreach ($ext in @("torchaudio", "torchvision")) {
            $w = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $dist -Filter "$ext-*.whl" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
            if ($w) { Invoke-Pip @("install", $w.FullName); $installedExts += $ext }
            else { Write-Host "::warning::No $ext wheel in artifact (extension build may have failed; non-blocking)" }
          }

          # Smoke-test imports: torch is required (CUDA must be visible); every installed
          # extension must import too, so a broken wheel fails the shard instead of going green.
          python -c "import torch; print('torch', torch.__version__, 'cuda', torch.version.cuda); assert torch.cuda.is_available()"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "import torch smoke test failed with exit $LASTEXITCODE" }
          foreach ($ext in $installedExts) {
            python -c "import $ext; print('$ext', $ext.__version__)"
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "import $ext smoke test failed with exit $LASTEXITCODE" }
          }

      # Seed our own test-time stats into pytorch's .additional_ci_files so
      # run_test.py shards by cost instead of falling back to round robin
      # ("Failed to find test times file ... Using round robin sharding").
      # Round robin ignores cost, so one shard collects the multi-hour files
      # and sets the whole cell's critical path. All shards read the same
      # committed JSON, so the split is consistent across them.
      - name: Seed test-time stats (deterministic sharding)
        shell: powershell
        env:
          VENV_ACTIVATE: ${{ steps.venv.outputs.venv-activate }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          & $env:VENV_ACTIVATE
          python "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\oot\scripts\test-stats\seed_test_stats.py" `
            --pytorch-root $env:PT_ROOT
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "seed_test_stats.py failed with exit $LASTEXITCODE" }

      - name: Start runner diagnostics
        id: diag
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/start-runner-diagnostics

      # Run this shard via the vendored PowerShell test entrypoint (Phase 2),
      # which drives test/run_test.py with the WoA exclude args and writes JUnit
      # XML + logs into <PT_ROOT>\test\test-reports.
      - name: Run PyTorch arm64 test suite (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ inputs.num-shards }})
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          VENV_ACTIVATE: ${{ steps.venv.outputs.venv-activate }}
          SHARD_NUMBER: ${{ matrix.shard }}
          NUM_TEST_SHARDS: ${{ inputs.num-shards }}
          TEST_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.test-config }}
          # ---- per-process hang guard, covering the phases pytest-timeout
          # ---- cannot see: import, collection, and everything after the last
          # ---- test while the interpreter and CUDA context tear down. One of
          # ---- the arm64 shards lost to a hang went quiet for 61min right
          # ---- after a "Finished" line, which is exactly that gap. The
          # ---- directory holds nothing but sitecustomize.py, which `site`
          # ---- imports at interpreter startup; it arms only in processes
          # ---- whose argv[0] is a test file, so the parent is never bounded.
          # ---- Nothing in tools/woa-build touches PYTHONPATH, so this
          # ---- survives into the test processes unmodified.
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/oot/scripts/test-bounds/pythonpath
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

          # sitecustomize.py deliberately will not create this directory -
          # racing hundreds of test processes to make one is a worse failure
          # than dropping the records - so make it here. run_test.py writes its
          # own reports into the same place.
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "$env:PT_ROOT\test\test-reports" | Out-Null

          # Note [The bound's premise is cost-based sharding]
          #   30min only clears the workload because run_test.py pytest-splits
          #   its heavy files, and it can only do that with a recorded cost per
          #   file. With no costs it shards round robin and runs each file
          #   whole: test_meta takes 53min that way, test_foreach 40min, so the
          #   same bound would kill work that completes. The seed step above
          #   writes those costs, but it is younger than the workflow it sits
          #   in - `main` in both repos still has no seed step, so a shard run
          #   from there round-robins. Rather than trust that the two travel
          #   together, check for the costs and disable the bound when they are
          #   missing. Clearing the variable is the supported "off" switch:
          #   sitecustomize reads anything unparseable or <= 0 as disabled.
          $timesFile = Join-Path $env:PT_ROOT '.additional_ci_files\test-times.json'
          $costed = 0
          if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $timesFile) {
            try {
              # Shape is {"default": {"default": {<file>: <seconds>}}} - the
              # same map run_test.py reads to decide the split.
              $times = (Get-Content -LiteralPath $timesFile -Raw |
                        ConvertFrom-Json).default.default
              if ($times) { $costed = @($times.PSObject.Properties).Count }
            } catch {
              # A malformed file means run_test.py will not get costs either,
              # so treat it exactly like a missing one.
              $costed = 0
            }
          }

          # State the outcome either way, so a run where nothing hangs still
          # shows whether the bound was live. Silence alone cannot distinguish
          # "armed in every test process" from "never imported".
          $bound = "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\oot\scripts\test-bounds\pythonpath\sitecustomize.py"
          if ($costed -lt 1) {
            $env:PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SEC = ''
            Write-Host "::warning::per-process bound NOT armed - no per-file costs in '$timesFile', so this shard shards round robin and runs heavy files whole. A bound sized for split files would kill work that completes."
          } elseif (Test-Path -LiteralPath $bound) {
            Write-Host "per-process bound: $($env:PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SEC)s, armed from $bound ($costed file(s) with a recorded cost)"
          } else {
            Write-Host "::warning::per-process bound NOT armed - no sitecustomize.py at '$bound'. A hang outside a running test will cost the whole shard."
          }

          # No shard-level watchdog here: the script below already runs
          # run_test.py under one, and reports a JUnit for it. See the
          # PYTORCH_WIN_TEST_RUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC note in the job env.
          & "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\oot\tools\woa-build\pytorch-windows-test-shard.ps1" `
            -PytorchRoot $env:PT_ROOT `
            -ShardNumber ([int]$env:SHARD_NUMBER) `
            -NumShards ([int]$env:NUM_TEST_SHARDS) `
            -TestConfig $env:TEST_CONFIG `
            -VenvActivate $env:VENV_ACTIVATE
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }

      # Close the loop on the per-process bound. Without this the only thing a
      # healthy shard proves is that sitecustomize.py was on PYTHONPATH at step
      # start - not that any test process actually imported and armed it. Reads
      # the records the processes appended and states both counts.
      #
      # Read-only and never fails the shard: it reports on a guard, and a
      # broken report is not worth converting into a red shard. A zero count is
      # a warning rather than an error for the same reason - it means the bound
      # was inert, which is worth shouting about but is not itself a test
      # failure.
      - name: Report per-process bound coverage
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          rec="${PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_LOG:-}"
          if [ -z "$rec" ] || [ ! -f "$rec" ]; then
            echo "::warning::No per-process bound records at '$rec'. Either no test file ran, or sitecustomize.py was never imported - in which case a hang outside a running test would cost the whole shard."
            exit 0
          fi
          armed=$(grep -c '"event": "armed"' "$rec" || true)
          fired=$(grep -c '"event": "fired"' "$rec" || true)
          echo "per-process bound: armed in ${armed} test-file process(es), fired ${fired} time(s)"
          if [ "${armed:-0}" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::warning::per-process bound recorded no armed process; treat the bound as inert for this shard."
          fi
          if [ "${fired:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "The bound killed these process(es) - each one is a test file that hung outside a running test:"
            grep '"event": "fired"' "$rec" || true
          fi
          exit 0

      - name: Stop runner diagnostics
        if: always()
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/stop-runner-diagnostics
        with:
          output-dir: ${{ steps.diag.outputs.output-dir }}

      # Per-shard failing-test detail (read-only; never changes pass/fail). The
      # orchestrator's test-summary job renders the cross-shard aggregate.
      - name: Summarize failed tests (this shard)
        if: always()
        shell: powershell
        env:
          VENV_ACTIVATE: ${{ steps.venv.outputs.venv-activate }}
        run: |
          & $env:VENV_ACTIVATE
          python "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\oot\scripts\test-summary\parse_failures.py" `
            --reports-dir "$env:PT_ROOT\test\test-reports" `
            --title "Failed tests - $($env:BUILD_ENVIRONMENT) - $($env:PYTHON_LABEL)/cu134 - arm64 - shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ inputs.num-shards }}" `
            | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY -Append -Encoding utf8

      - name: Upload test-reports archive
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: test-reports-${{ inputs.build-environment }}-${{ inputs.python-label }}-arm64-shard${{ matrix.shard }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ env.PT_ROOT }}/test/test-reports/**
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Strict clean (post)
        if: always()
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/woa-strict-clean
        with:
          phase: post
          pt-root: ${{ env.PT_ROOT }}
          scratch-root: ${{ env.WOA_SCRATCH }}
          extra-paths: ${{ github.workspace }}/artifact

name: windows-rtx-build-test

# Source-build + test CI for pytorch/pytorch on self-hosted Windows NVIDIA
# RTX runners. Builds a wheel from source via the upstream-faithful
# `tools/pytorch-build/win-build.sh` flow (`_rtx-build.yml`), tests it
# (`_rtx-test.yml`), then rolls up failures (`test-summary`).
#
# Two triggers, and neither can be started by hand:
#
#   - `schedule`      - daily; builds/tests the full matrix against the
#                       upstream `main` commit the day's nightly was cut from.
#   - `workflow_call` - an upstream PR approved by `upstream-pull.yml`,
#                       pinned to the approved head SHA. Never HUD-eligible.
#
# There is deliberately NO `workflow_dispatch`. External-CI security guidelines
# do not allow a hand-started run to aim this repo's self-hosted RTX pool at an
# arbitrary upstream commit, which is what its `pytorch-pr` / `pytorch-ref`
# inputs did. The only way to point this workflow at a PR is the relay path,
# behind the allowlist and a maintainer's approval.
#
# There is no `repository_dispatch` arm. There used to be a parked one, whose
# `dispatch-gate` guards skipped every job when the event was a dispatch. Those
# guards outlived the trigger and then misfired: a called workflow sees the
# *caller's* event, so once `upstream-pull.yml` began calling this one over the
# relay path, `prep` and the whole fanout skipped while the parked
# inspect-dispatch job ran instead. Removed - the relay path now belongs to
# `upstream-pull.yml`, which does its own payload inspection.
#
# Shape:
#
#   prep (resolve ref)
#       |
#   build  matrix( config )            one multi-arch wheel per cell
#       |   (up to 3 cells)
#       |
#       +-> test  matrix( config x arch )   1 reusable-workflow call per
#                 up to 3 x 2 = 6 cells     cell; each call internally fans
#                                           out 5 shard runners.
#
# `config` is a paired `{python, cuda}` entry (the runner pool is allocated
# per python/cuda combination). The subset-filter inputs are forwarded to
# the reusable workflows, whose own job-level `if:` performs the per-cell
# match (GitHub forbids `matrix.*` in the `if:` of a reusable-workflow-
# calling job, so the filter lives one layer down). Empty = no filter, which
# is every scheduled run.
#
# Cell-name shape mirrors pytorch/pytorch's generated nightly:
#   build cell -> `<build_name>-build`        e.g. `wheel-py312-cu130-build`
#   test  cell -> `<build_name>-<arch>-test`  e.g. `wheel-py312-cu130-sm89-test`

on:
  schedule:
    # Sits after pytorch/pytorch has cut the day's `nightly` commit, which over
    # the 57 days to 2026-09-09 landed between 07:35 and 08:47 UTC on 55 of
    # them (median 08:00). Timing is not cosmetic here: `prep` resolves the
    # newest nightly at or before this run's start, so firing beforehand does
    # not wait for the day's commit -- it silently builds, tests and reports
    # yesterday's again. The previous 03:05 did exactly that on all 57 days
    # sampled.
    #
    # Off the hour because that is when the shared Actions scheduler is most
    # congested, and scheduled runs are only ever delivered late.
    #
    # The two stragglers in that window (2026-08-27 10:49, 2026-08-28 11:15)
    # are not covered. Chasing them would cost every other day ~2.5h of extra
    # staleness, and a nightly missed this way is not lost: the next run picks
    # it up as the newest commit at or before its own start.
    #
    # GitHub attributes a scheduled run to whoever last pushed a change to this
    # cron expression, so it must be (re)pushed by an account with a verified
    # email or every run fails at startup.
    - cron: "20 9 * * *"

  # Called by `upstream-pull.yml` to validate an approved upstream PR. A PR run
  # is started by the relay path after a maintainer approves it, never by hand,
  # and `workflow_call` puts no "Run workflow" entry in the Actions UI or API.
  # A PR is pinned to one already-resolved commit, so the only ref input is
  # that SHA - nothing here re-resolves a PR's head.
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      pytorch-ref:
        description: "Full 40-hex commit SHA to build. For a PR, its approved head."
        type: string
        required: true
      python-versions:
        description: "Comma-separated subset of 3.12 to build/test. Empty = all."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""
      cuda-versions:
        description: "Comma-separated subset of 13.0,13.2 to build/test. Empty = all."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""
      test-architectures:
        description: "Comma-separated subset of sm89,sm120 to test. Empty = all."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""

concurrency:
  group: windows-rtx-build-test-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read

jobs:
  # ===========================================================================
  # Resolve the pytorch ref to build, once, before the matrix fans out, and
  # decide whether this run is allowed to publish to the upstream HUD.
  #
  # Two paths:
  #
  #   1. `pytorch-ref` empty or `nightly` - the schedule case, which has no
  #      inputs - resolve the upstream `main` commit that nightly was cut from
  #      and build *that*. See `scripts/crcr/resolve_nightly_commits.py` for
  #      why the nightly branch tip itself is unusable as a HUD key. This is
  #      the only path that reports.
  #   2. an explicit `pytorch-ref` - a PR head passed in via `workflow_call` -
  #      build it verbatim, report nothing.
  #
  # `crcr-delivery-id` carries the decision downstream: non-empty means "this
  # is a genuine nightly of upstream main, publish it", empty means "run the
  # matrix but stay off the HUD". Keeping the policy here means the reusable
  # workflows never have to re-derive it.
  #
  # The build records the resolved SHA into built_pytorch_sha.txt; each test
  # cell pins its own checkout to it.
  # ===========================================================================
  prep:
    name: resolve pytorch ref
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      pytorch-ref: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.pytorch-ref }}
      crcr-delivery-id: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.crcr-delivery-id }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository (for CRCR scripts)
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      - name: Resolve pytorch ref
        id: ref
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REF: ${{ inputs.pytorch-ref || 'nightly' }}
          PYTHON_VERSIONS: ${{ inputs.python-versions }}
          CUDA_VERSIONS: ${{ inputs.cuda-versions }}
          TEST_ARCHITECTURES: ${{ inputs.test-architectures }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          delivery_id=""
          if [ "${REF}" = "nightly" ]; then
            # Pin resolution to when the run was *first* started, not to now.
            # The nightly tip advances every night, so resolving "the tip" on a
            # re-run would silently retarget a different main SHA: the re-run
            # would build a different commit and file its HUD row under a
            # different delivery-id, instead of replacing the row for the day
            # it was meant to repair. Attempt 1's `run_started_at` is immutable,
            # unlike the run-level field, which resets on every re-run.
            as_of=$(gh api \
              "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/attempts/1" \
              -q '.run_started_at')
            if [ -z "${as_of}" ] || [ "${as_of}" = "null" ]; then
              echo "::error::Could not read attempt 1's start time; refusing to resolve nightly against a moving tip." >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Resolving nightly as of ${as_of} (attempt 1 start)"

            # Deep enough to still contain that day's nightly when a run is
            # re-run weeks later; `resolve_nightly_commits.py` fails loudly
            # rather than guessing if the window still falls short.
            gh api "repos/pytorch/pytorch/commits?sha=nightly&per_page=100" > nightly-commits.json
            python3 scripts/crcr/resolve_nightly_commits.py \
              --commits-json nightly-commits.json \
              --as-of "${as_of}" \
              --github-output resolved.env \
              --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            ref=$(sed -n 's/^source-sha=//p' resolved.env)
            if ! [[ "${ref}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::Nightly resolution produced an invalid source SHA '${ref}'." >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Nightly resolves to upstream main ${ref}"
            delivery_id="${ref}"
          else
            ref="${REF}"
            echo "Using explicit pytorch-ref='${ref}'"
          fi

          # Belt-and-braces on top of the path selection above: only a
          # scheduled run may publish. A PR run arrives via `workflow_call`
          # carrying its caller's event, `repository_dispatch`, so it is kept
          # off the HUD here as well as by its explicit ref.
          case "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" in
            schedule) ;;
            *) delivery_id="" ;;
          esac

          echo "pytorch-ref=${ref}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "crcr-delivery-id=${delivery_id}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          if [ -n "${delivery_id}" ]; then
            hud_status="enabled -> ${delivery_id}"
          else
            hud_status="disabled"
          fi
          {
            echo "## windows-rtx-build-test config"
            echo ""
            echo "| field | value |"
            echo "| --- | --- |"
            echo "| trigger | \`${{ github.event_name }}\` |"
            echo "| pytorch-ref (resolved) | \`${ref}\` |"
            echo "| python-versions | \`${PYTHON_VERSIONS:-(all)}\` |"
            echo "| cuda-versions | \`${CUDA_VERSIONS:-(all)}\` |"
            echo "| test-architectures | \`${TEST_ARCHITECTURES:-(all)}\` |"
            echo "| HUD reporting | \`${hud_status}\` |"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  build:
    name: ${{ matrix.config.build_name }}-build
    needs: prep
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # One entry per actual runner pairing. Add/remove a line to
        # introduce/drop a (python, cuda) combination. The build job needs a
        # machine labelled `[rtx-build, <python.label>, <cuda.label>]` per entry.
        # `build_name` names the GitHub jobs; `hud_env` names the upstream HUD
        # rows. They are deliberately separate: `hud_env` mirrors pytorch's own
        # `<build-environment> / <job>` convention so our rows read natively
        # next to upstream's, and must stay stable across runs because it is
        # the identity a HUD result is filed under, so changing one orphans
        # that row's history upstream.
        config: &config
          - { python: { version: "3.12", label: "py312" }, cuda: { version: "13.0", label: "cu130" }, build_name: "wheel-py312-cu130", hud_env: "win-rtx-py312-cu130" }
          - { python: { version: "3.12", label: "py312" }, cuda: { version: "13.2", label: "cu132" }, build_name: "wheel-py312-cu132", hud_env: "win-rtx-py312-cu132" }
          # TODO: re-add Python 3.13 (py313 / cu132) to the matrix in the future.
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_rtx-build.yml
    with:
      runner-base: rtx-build
      python-version: ${{ matrix.config.python.version }}
      python-label: ${{ matrix.config.python.label }}
      cuda-version: ${{ matrix.config.cuda.version }}
      cuda-label: ${{ matrix.config.cuda.label }}
      cuda-arch-list: "8.9;12.0"
      build-environment: win-rtx-cuda
      pytorch-ref: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.pytorch-ref }}
      # Must match the `wheel-artifact:` value passed to the paired test
      # call below so the test job picks up exactly this build's wheel.
      wheel-artifact: ${{ matrix.config.build_name }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
      # Forward the caller's subset filters; the reusable workflow's
      # job-level `if:` evaluates them. Empty string = no filter.
      python-versions: ${{ inputs.python-versions }}
      cuda-versions: ${{ inputs.cuda-versions }}

  test:
    name: ${{ matrix.config.build_name }}-${{ matrix.arch.name }}-test
    needs: build
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config: *config
        arch: &arch
          - { name: sm89,  runner: rtx-40x0-test, arch_list: "8.9"  }
          - { name: sm120, runner: rtx-50x0-test, arch_list: "12.0" }
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_rtx-test.yml
    with:
      runner-base: ${{ matrix.arch.runner }}
      python-version: ${{ matrix.config.python.version }}
      python-label: ${{ matrix.config.python.label }}
      cuda-version: ${{ matrix.config.cuda.version }}
      cuda-label: ${{ matrix.config.cuda.label }}
      cuda-arch-list: ${{ matrix.arch.arch_list }}
      arch-name: ${{ matrix.arch.name }}
      build-environment: win-rtx-${{ matrix.arch.name }}
      test-config: "default"
      wheel-artifact: ${{ matrix.config.build_name }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
      # Forward the caller's subset filters; the reusable workflow's
      # job-level `if:` evaluates them. Empty string = no filter.
      python-versions: ${{ inputs.python-versions }}
      cuda-versions: ${{ inputs.cuda-versions }}
      test-architectures: ${{ inputs.test-architectures }}

  # ===========================================================================
  # Post-test rollup. Runs once after every test cell/shard settles and
  # renders a consolidated table of the test jobs that failed (with direct
  # log links) into the run's step summary. Per-test-name detail lives in
  # each shard's own summary (see `_rtx-test.yml`). Informational only:
  # `if: always()` so it runs even when tests fail, and it never reports a
  # non-zero status of its own - the test cells already carry red/green.
  # ===========================================================================
  test-summary:
    name: test-summary
    needs: test
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository (for summary script)
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      - name: Aggregate failed test jobs
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh api --paginate \
            "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/attempts/${{ github.run_attempt }}/jobs" \
            -q '.jobs[]' | jq -s '.' > jobs.json
          python3 scripts/test-summary/aggregate_failures.py \
            --jobs-json jobs.json \
            --title "PyTorch test summary (run ${{ github.run_id }})" \
            >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # The step above lists which jobs failed. This pair says which tests did.
      # It pulls every shard's uploaded test-reports tree (JUnit XML + run logs)
      # and renders one union-of-all-shards failure list, de-duplicated so a
      # test that failed in several shards - or failed and then passed on a
      # rerun - appears once, annotated with the shards it was seen in.
      #
      # Best-effort: a missing or partial artifact degrades the list rather
      # than failing the run, which is why the download cannot fail the job.
      - name: Download all shard test-reports
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: test-reports-*
          path: all-reports

      - name: Aggregate failed tests across shards
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python3 scripts/test-summary/parse_failures.py \
            --shards-root all-reports \
            --title "Aggregate failed tests - all shards (run ${{ github.run_id }})" \
            >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # ===========================================================================
  # Cross-Repo CI Relay (CRCR) HUD reporting - trust level L2.
  #
  # Publishes one HUD row per logical cell against the upstream pytorch/pytorch
  # `main` commit this run built (`prep`'s `crcr-delivery-id`). Only ever active
  # for a genuine nightly: `prep` leaves the delivery id empty for a PR run,
  # which switches both jobs off via their `if:`.
  #
  # Two properties drive the shape of these jobs:
  #
  #   * They are TERMINAL. Nothing depends on them, so a relay outage can never
  #     skip a build or a test. This is why they are not steps inside the
  #     reusable workflows: `report-build` living inside `_rtx-build.yml` would
  #     make the caller's `build` job red on a callback failure, which would in
  #     turn skip the whole `test` matrix behind it.
  #   * They are per-cell MATRIX jobs with `fail-fast: false`, so each HUD row
  #     is delivered independently and one failed callback cannot suppress the
  #     other five.
  #
  # Being terminal costs us `needs.<cell>.result` (in the caller that expression
  # collapses to one aggregate over every matrix leg), so each leg recovers its
  # own conclusion from the Jobs API via `resolve_cell_conclusion.py`.
  #
  # Neither job carries `continue-on-error`: a callback we could not deliver
  # has to be visible as a failed job rather than a missing row.
  # ===========================================================================
  report-build-crcr:
    name: report ${{ matrix.config.build_name }}-build to HUD
    needs: [prep, build]
    if: always() && needs.prep.outputs.crcr-delivery-id != '' && needs.build.result != 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      id-token: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config: *config
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository (for CRCR scripts)
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      # Mirrors the subset filter the reusable workflow applies to itself. A
      # cell the operator narrowed out of this run never produced jobs to read
      # a conclusion from, and must not be reported as anything at all.
      - name: Check cell is in this run's subset
        id: subset
        shell: bash
        env:
          PYTHON_VERSIONS: ${{ inputs.python-versions }}
          CUDA_VERSIONS: ${{ inputs.cuda-versions }}
          PY: ${{ matrix.config.python.version }}
          CU: ${{ matrix.config.cuda.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          selected=true
          if [ -n "${PYTHON_VERSIONS}" ] && [[ "${PYTHON_VERSIONS}" != *"${PY}"* ]]; then
            selected=false
          fi
          if [ -n "${CUDA_VERSIONS}" ] && [[ "${CUDA_VERSIONS}" != *"${CU}"* ]]; then
            selected=false
          fi
          echo "selected=${selected}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Resolve cell conclusion
        id: cell
        if: steps.subset.outputs.selected == 'true'
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh api --paginate \
            "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/attempts/${{ github.run_attempt }}/jobs" \
            -q '.jobs[]' | jq -s '.' > jobs.json
          python3 scripts/crcr/resolve_cell_conclusion.py \
            --jobs-json jobs.json \
            --cell "${{ matrix.config.build_name }}-build" \
            --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" \
            --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Report build result to CRCR
        if: steps.subset.outputs.selected == 'true' && steps.cell.outputs.should-report == 'true'
        uses: ./.github/actions/crcr-callback
        with:
          event-type: nightly
          delivery-id: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.crcr-delivery-id }}
          job-name: ${{ matrix.config.hud_env }} / build
          status: completed
          conclusion: ${{ steps.cell.outputs.conclusion }}
          artifact-url: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/attempts/${{ github.run_attempt }}

  report-test-crcr:
    name: report ${{ matrix.config.build_name }}-${{ matrix.arch.name }}-test to HUD
    needs: [prep, test]
    if: always() && needs.prep.outputs.crcr-delivery-id != '' && needs.test.result != 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      id-token: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config: *config
        arch: *arch
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository (for CRCR scripts)
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      - name: Check cell is in this run's subset
        id: subset
        shell: bash
        env:
          PYTHON_VERSIONS: ${{ inputs.python-versions }}
          CUDA_VERSIONS: ${{ inputs.cuda-versions }}
          TEST_ARCHITECTURES: ${{ inputs.test-architectures }}
          PY: ${{ matrix.config.python.version }}
          CU: ${{ matrix.config.cuda.version }}
          ARCH: ${{ matrix.arch.name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          selected=true
          if [ -n "${PYTHON_VERSIONS}" ] && [[ "${PYTHON_VERSIONS}" != *"${PY}"* ]]; then
            selected=false
          fi
          if [ -n "${CUDA_VERSIONS}" ] && [[ "${CUDA_VERSIONS}" != *"${CU}"* ]]; then
            selected=false
          fi
          if [ -n "${TEST_ARCHITECTURES}" ] && [[ "${TEST_ARCHITECTURES}" != *"${ARCH}"* ]]; then
            selected=false
          fi
          echo "selected=${selected}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Resolve cell conclusion
        id: cell
        if: steps.subset.outputs.selected == 'true'
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh api --paginate \
            "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/attempts/${{ github.run_attempt }}/jobs" \
            -q '.jobs[]' | jq -s '.' > jobs.json
          python3 scripts/crcr/resolve_cell_conclusion.py \
            --jobs-json jobs.json \
            --cell "${{ matrix.config.build_name }}-${{ matrix.arch.name }}-test" \
            --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" \
            --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Scoped to this cell's own five shards: the artifact name embeds the
      # build-environment, python/cuda labels, arch and run attempt, so the
      # pattern cannot pick up a sibling cell's reports.
      #
      # `continue-on-error` here does not mask an undelivered callback - that
      # rule applies to the callback step, which is left bare below. A cell whose
      # shards died before uploading anything still owes upstream a red row, so
      # a failed download has to fall through to the summariser (which reports
      # `failure` on any shortfall against `--expected-shards`) rather than
      # abort before reporting.
      - name: Download this cell's shard test-reports
        id: download
        if: steps.subset.outputs.selected == 'true' && steps.cell.outputs.should-report == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: test-reports-win-rtx-${{ matrix.arch.name }}-${{ matrix.config.python.label }}-${{ matrix.config.cuda.label }}-${{ matrix.arch.name }}-shard*-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: cell-reports

      # `--expected-shards` is the number of shard jobs the Jobs API reported
      # for this cell, so it tracks `_rtx-test.yml`'s shard matrix without a
      # second copy of the fanout to keep in sync. Any shard that left no
      # reports makes the cell `failure`: `upload-artifact` is configured
      # `if-no-files-found: warn`, so a shard that died before writing its
      # reports tree uploads nothing and still goes green - the short count is
      # the only evidence that part of the cell never ran.
      - name: Summarize cell test results
        id: results
        if: steps.subset.outputs.selected == 'true' && steps.cell.outputs.should-report == 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 scripts/crcr/build_test_results.py \
            --shards-root cell-reports \
            --expected-shards "${{ steps.cell.outputs.matched-jobs }}" \
            --title "HUD test results - ${{ matrix.config.build_name }}-${{ matrix.arch.name }}-test" \
            --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" \
            --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Two independent signals must agree before a cell is called green: the
      # shard jobs' own GitHub outcome, and the JUnit evidence they left behind.
      # Each alone has a blind spot - a shard cancelled before writing any XML
      # looks clean to the summariser, and a harness that exits 0 while
      # reporting failed cases looks clean to GitHub.
      - name: Combine conclusions
        id: conclusion
        if: steps.subset.outputs.selected == 'true' && steps.cell.outputs.should-report == 'true'
        shell: bash
        env:
          JOB_CONCLUSION: ${{ steps.cell.outputs.conclusion }}
          REPORT_CONCLUSION: ${{ steps.results.outputs.conclusion }}
          DOWNLOAD_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.download.outcome }}
          CELL: ${{ matrix.config.build_name }}-${{ matrix.arch.name }}-test
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "${JOB_CONCLUSION}" = "cancelled" ]; then
            conclusion=cancelled
          elif [ "${JOB_CONCLUSION}" = "success" ] && [ "${REPORT_CONCLUSION}" = "success" ]; then
            conclusion=success
          else
            conclusion=failure
          fi
          echo "conclusion=${conclusion}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "${DOWNLOAD_OUTCOME}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "::warning title=CRCR artifacts::Could not download shard reports for ${CELL}; test counts may be incomplete."
          fi
          {
            echo ""
            echo "| conclusion input | value |"
            echo "| --- | --- |"
            echo "| shard jobs result | \`${JOB_CONCLUSION}\` |"
            echo "| report evidence | \`${REPORT_CONCLUSION}\` |"
            echo "| artifact download | \`${DOWNLOAD_OUTCOME}\` |"
            echo "| **reported conclusion** | \`${conclusion}\` |"
            echo "| delivery-id (upstream main SHA) | \`${{ needs.prep.outputs.crcr-delivery-id }}\` |"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Report test results to CRCR
        if: steps.subset.outputs.selected == 'true' && steps.cell.outputs.should-report == 'true'
        uses: ./.github/actions/crcr-callback
        with:
          event-type: nightly
          delivery-id: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.crcr-delivery-id }}
          job-name: ${{ matrix.config.hud_env }} / test (${{ matrix.arch.name }})
          status: completed
          conclusion: ${{ steps.conclusion.outputs.conclusion }}
          test-results: ${{ steps.results.outputs.test-results }}
          artifact-url: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/attempts/${{ github.run_attempt }}

      # The HUD and GitHub conclusions have to agree. The shard
      # jobs can go green while their reports say otherwise - a harness that
      # exits 0 with failed cases, or shards that left no evidence at all - and
      # in that case the callback above has already told upstream `failure`.
      # Fail here too, so whoever opens the run sees the same answer the HUD
      # shows. Ordered after the callback deliberately: the result has to be
      # delivered before this job goes red.
      - name: Match GitHub to the reported conclusion
        if: steps.conclusion.outputs.conclusion == 'failure' && steps.cell.outputs.conclusion == 'success'
        shell: bash
        env:
          CELL: ${{ matrix.config.build_name }}-${{ matrix.arch.name }}-test
        run: |
          echo "::error title=CRCR conclusion::Shard jobs for ${CELL} all passed, but their reports show failures or missing evidence. Reported 'failure' to the HUD; failing this job so GitHub agrees."
          exit 1

name: windows-rtx-wheel-test

# Daily smoke of the *published* pytorch nightly wheel on self-hosted
# Windows NVIDIA RTX runners. No source build, no preflight, no
# artifact handoff - each test runner is told `pytorch-ref: nightly`,
# `actions/checkout@v7` resolves that against `pytorch/pytorch` to a
# concrete commit, the runner reads that commit's UTC date, then
# greps `download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/torch/` for the wheel whose
# filename carries that exact `devYYYYMMDD` tag together with the
# matrix `cu<label>` / `cp<pyshort>` tags, and `pip install`s the
# resolved absolute URL. The job fails fast if the index has no
# wheel for the checked-out commit's date (i.e. the wheel is not yet
# published) - that guarantees the wheel under test and the pytorch
# source checkout used by `.ci/pytorch/win-test.sh` come from the
# same day.
#
# Counterparts:
#   - windows-rtx-build-test.yml           -> full source build + test (scheduled; PR runs via workflow_call)
#
# Shape - one test job, 2-D matrix:
#
#   test  matrix( config x arch )       1 reusable-workflow call per cell;
#         3 x 2 = 6 cells                each call internally fans out 5
#                                        shard runners (30 runners total).
#
# `config` is a paired `{python, cuda}` entry rather than independent
# `python` and `cuda` axes - the runner pool is allocated per (python,
# cuda) combination (e.g. py312/cu130 and py312/cu132 are different
# machines), so each config is one explicit pairing. Add or remove
# pairings by editing the `config:` list directly; no `exclude`
# gymnastics needed.
#
# Sharding is NOT a top-level matrix axis here - it lives inside
# `_rtx-test.yml`'s own `strategy.matrix.shard`. Each test cell in this
# orchestrator therefore represents "this wheel x this architecture"
# (one runner per shard nested under it), matching the upstream
# `_win-rtx-test.yml` pattern in pytorch/pytorch PR #176678. The
# SHARD_NUMBER / NUM_TEST_SHARDS / TEST_CONFIG env vars consumed by
# `.ci/pytorch/win-test.sh` are populated inside the reusable workflow.
#
# Cell-name shape mirrors `pytorch/pytorch`'s generated
# `windows-binary-wheel` nightly:
#   test cell -> `<build_name>-<arch>-test`   e.g. `wheel-py312-cu130-sm89-test`
# Each `config:` entry carries its own precomputed `build_name` so the
# job-level `name:` is a one-token reference instead of a multi-piece
# template, matching upstream's `name: ${{ matrix.build_name }}-test`
# pattern. `arch` carries the runner-base label and the
# TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST value, so a single job declaration drives both
# RTX 40x0 (sm89) and RTX 50x0 (sm120).

# PARKED - this workflow has no live trigger and cannot currently start.
#
# `workflow_dispatch` was its only trigger (the nightly cron below has been
# commented out for longer), and external-CI security guidelines do not allow a
# hand-started run to aim the self-hosted RTX pool at an arbitrary upstream
# ref. Rather than delete the file - it is the worked `test`-only example the
# CI reference documents, and its wheel-resolution logic is not reproduced
# anywhere else - the trigger is reduced to `workflow_call`, which is
# schema-valid, offers no "Run workflow" in the Actions UI or API, and is
# called by nothing in this repo. Commenting out every trigger is not an
# option: an empty `on:` fails the workflow schema.
#
# To bring it back, uncomment the cron for an unattended nightly. On a
# `schedule` run every input below is empty: `pytorch-ref` and
# `wheel-index-url` already fall back to the nightly values where they are
# used, and empty subset filters select every cell.
on:
  # schedule:
  #   - cron: "0 17 * * *"
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      pytorch-ref:
        description: "pytorch/pytorch ref to test against (branch, tag, or SHA). Default: nightly."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "nightly"
      python-versions:
        description: "Comma-separated subset of 3.12,3.13 to test."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "3.12"
      cuda-versions:
        description: "Comma-separated subset of 13.0,13.2 to test."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "13.0,13.2"
      test-architectures:
        description: "Comma-separated subset of sm89,sm120 to test."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "sm89,sm120"
      wheel-index-url:
        description: "Override the nightly wheel index page (default: https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/torch/)."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""

concurrency:
  group: windows-rtx-wheel-test-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read

jobs:
  test:
    name: ${{ matrix.config.build_name }}-${{ matrix.arch.name }}-test
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # One entry per actual runner pairing. The test job needs a
        # machine labelled `[<arch.runner>, <config.python.label>,
        # <config.cuda.label>]` for each (config, arch) combination.
        # `build_name` is the canonical cell identity - the test job
        # renders as `<build_name>-<arch>-test`, matching the source-
        # build orchestrator's naming so a wheel-test row and its
        # windows-rtx-build-test counterpart sort adjacent in cross-
        # workflow dashboards. Sharding is internal to `_rtx-test.yml`
        # (its own `strategy.matrix.shard` fans out 5 runners per
        # cell), so it deliberately does NOT appear in this matrix.
        config:
          - { python: { version: "3.12", label: "py312" }, cuda: { version: "13.0", label: "cu130" }, build_name: "wheel-py312-cu130" }
          - { python: { version: "3.12", label: "py312" }, cuda: { version: "13.2", label: "cu132" }, build_name: "wheel-py312-cu132" }
        arch:
          - { name: sm89,  runner: rtx-40x0-test, arch_list: "8.9"  }
          - { name: sm120, runner: rtx-50x0-test, arch_list: "12.0" }
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_rtx-test.yml
    with:
      runner-base: ${{ matrix.arch.runner }}
      python-version: ${{ matrix.config.python.version }}
      python-label: ${{ matrix.config.python.label }}
      cuda-version: ${{ matrix.config.cuda.version }}
      cuda-label: ${{ matrix.config.cuda.label }}
      cuda-arch-list: ${{ matrix.arch.arch_list }}
      arch-name: ${{ matrix.arch.name }}
      build-environment: win-rtx-nightly-wheel-${{ matrix.arch.name }}
      test-config: "default"
      pytorch-ref: ${{ inputs.pytorch-ref || 'nightly' }}
      wheel-index-url: ${{ inputs.wheel-index-url || 'https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/torch/' }}
      # Forward the caller's subset filters; the reusable workflow's
      # job-level `if:` evaluates them. Empty string = no filter.
      python-versions: ${{ inputs.python-versions }}
      cuda-versions: ${{ inputs.cuda-versions }}
      test-architectures: ${{ inputs.test-architectures }}

  # ===========================================================================
  # Post-test rollup. Runs once after every test cell/shard settles and
  # renders a consolidated table of the test jobs that failed (with direct
  # log links) into the run's step summary. Per-test-name detail lives in
  # each shard's own summary (see `_rtx-test.yml`). Informational only:
  # `if: always()` so it runs even when tests fail, and it never reports a
  # non-zero status of its own - the test cells already carry red/green.
  # ===========================================================================
  test-summary:
    name: test-summary
    needs: test
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository (for summary script)
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      - name: Aggregate failed test jobs
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh api --paginate \
            "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/attempts/${{ github.run_attempt }}/jobs" \
            -q '.jobs[]' | jq -s '.' > jobs.json
          python3 scripts/test-summary/aggregate_failures.py \
            --jobs-json jobs.json \
            --title "PyTorch test summary (run ${{ github.run_id }})" \
            >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # The step above lists which jobs failed. This pair says which tests did.
      # It pulls every shard's uploaded test-reports tree (JUnit XML + run logs)
      # and renders one union-of-all-shards failure list, de-duplicated so a
      # test that failed in several shards - or failed and then passed on a
      # rerun - appears once, annotated with the shards it was seen in.
      #
      # Best-effort: a missing or partial artifact degrades the list rather
      # than failing the run, which is why the download cannot fail the job.
      - name: Download all shard test-reports
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: test-reports-*
          path: all-reports

      - name: Aggregate failed tests across shards
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python3 scripts/test-summary/parse_failures.py \
            --shards-root all-reports \
            --title "Aggregate failed tests - all shards (run ${{ github.run_id }})" \
            >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
