name: windows-woa-build-test

# Source-build + test CI for pytorch/pytorch on self-hosted Windows-on-Arm
# (WoA) runners. The arm64 counterpart of `windows-rtx-build-test.yml`:
# builds the full P0 wheel set from source via the vendored PowerShell library
# (`_woa-build.yml`), tests every built wheel (`_woa-test.yml`), then rolls up
# failures (`test-summary`).
#
# Scheduled (nightly) only - there is intentionally NO manual/workflow_dispatch
# trigger. Relayed upstream PRs run `_woa-pr-build-test.yml` instead: the same
# build and test jobs, with no HUD reporting and no publication.
#
# Each run additionally publishes its per-cell results to the upstream PyTorch
# HUD over the Cross-Repo CI Relay (trust level L2), keyed by the `main` commit
# the nightly was cut from. See `docs/crcr-hud-reporting.md`; the mechanism is
# identical to the one in `windows-rtx-build-test.yml`, only the matrix differs.
#
# A run can also sign and publish its own wheels: `publication` calls
# `_woa-sign-publish.yml` once the builds finish, alongside the tests, but only
# when `vars.WOA_NIGHTLY_PUBLISH` is `dry-run` or `release` - unset, or anything
# else, publishes nothing. See `docs/woa-wheel-publishing.md`.
#
# Shape:
#
#   prep (resolve ref @ nightly -> upstream main SHA)
#       |
#   build  matrix( python in 3.11/3.12/3.13/3.14/3.14t ), CTK 13.4
#       |    each: vanilla -> cuda_embed -> torchaudio -> torchvision -> upload
#       |    (3.14t is the free-threaded / no-GIL build -> cp314t wheels)
#       |
#       +-> test  matrix( same python cells, CTK 13.4 )   [needs: build]
#       |         each cell fans out 4 shards internally
#       |
#       +-> publication  sign -> GitHub Release -> Kitmaker   [needs: build, opt-in only]
#       |
#       +-> report-build-crcr / report-test-crcr   [terminal, nightly only]
#                 exactly two HUD rows for the whole matrix: every Python
#                 version is reduced into one build row and one test row
#
# Runners: one shared PERSISTENT arm64 pool tagged `woa-arm64` for build + test.
# `test` `needs: build`, so the whole build stage finishes before any test job
# starts (same mechanism as x86) - which also keeps test jobs from starving the
# build stage on the shared pool. With per-version testing the test stage fans
# out to (#python cells) x 4 shards, all on the shared pool, so the full-matrix
# nightly run serializes on the pool.

on:
  # No `workflow_call`: the PR path calls `_woa-pr-build-test.yml` instead, so
  # that it never has to grant the publication job's `contents: write`.
  schedule:
    # Nightly build + test of the full WoA matrix against pytorch `nightly`.
    # Manual/workflow_dispatch is intentionally NOT offered for this repo.
    #
    # So every run is a genuine nightly of upstream `main`, which is what makes
    # it eligible to publish to the PyTorch HUD, and why there is no opt-out
    # input.
    #
    # Timed to land after pytorch/pytorch cuts the day's `nightly` commit
    # (07:35-08:47 UTC on 55 of the 57 days to 2026-09-09); see the longer note
    # in `windows-rtx-build-test.yml`. The previous 05:00 was ahead of it on
    # every day sampled, so this matrix only ever built the day-old nightly.
    #
    # Half an hour behind the RTX cron. The two use disjoint runner pools
    # (`woa-arm64` vs `rtx-build`/`sm89`/`sm120`) so they do not contend for
    # agents; the offset just keeps the two nightlies distinguishable when
    # something upstream breaks both.
    - cron: "50 9 * * *"

# No `concurrency:` group: the shared arm64 pool runs one job per agent, and the
# only trigger is the once-a-day schedule, so runs never overlap. A run_id-keyed
# group would be unique per run and coalesce nothing anyway.

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read

env:
  # The single upstream HUD identity for this workflow. Both reporting jobs
  # file under it, so every enabled Python cell lands on one build row and one
  # test row. It is the identity a HUD result is stored against, so changing it
  # orphans that row's history.
  HUD_ENV: win-woa-arm64-cu134
  # Python labels the reporting jobs reduce into those two rows. Must list
  # exactly the cells currently enabled in the `config` matrix below - see the
  # note there before enabling or disabling one.
  PYTHON_LABELS: py313

jobs:
  # ===========================================================================
  # Resolve pytorch + the torchaudio/torchvision sources to full commit SHAs ONCE
  # (over HTTPS) and pin every build + test cell to them. The nightly run tracks
  # moving branches, so without this each build cell would independently check out
  # a moving branch and could build DIFFERENT commits mid-run. Resolving here gives
  # one integrity-checked source triple across the whole run (Git objects are
  # content-addressed, so a full SHA yields exactly that commit or fails).
  # `_woa-build.yml` additionally rejects a non-SHA pytorch ref, so the pin is
  # enforced even when the reusable workflow is called directly.
  #
  # For pytorch specifically that means resolving the upstream `main` commit
  # the nightly was cut from, and building *that* rather than the nightly
  # branch tip. The tip is a generated commit that does not exist on `main`, so
  # it cannot key a HUD row; see `scripts/crcr/resolve_nightly_commits.py`.
  #
  # `crcr-delivery-id` carries that SHA downstream and doubles as the reporting
  # switch: non-empty means "this is a genuine nightly of upstream main,
  # publish it". It is left empty if the upstream SHA cannot be resolved, which
  # runs the matrix but keeps the run off the HUD rather than filing a result
  # against a commit we are not sure we built.
  # ===========================================================================
  prep:
    name: resolve pytorch ref
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      pytorch-ref: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.pytorch-ref }}
      torchaudio-ref: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.torchaudio-ref }}
      torchvision-ref: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.torchvision-ref }}
      nightly-date: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.nightly-date }}
      crcr-delivery-id: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.crcr-delivery-id }}
      num-shards: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.num-shards }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository (for prep scripts)
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      - name: Resolve source refs to commit SHAs
        id: ref
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REF: ${{ inputs.pytorch-ref || 'nightly' }}
          AUDIO_REF: "main"
          VISION_REF: "main"
          PYTHON_VERSIONS: ""
          NUM_SHARDS: "4"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/source-refs/resolve_ref.sh
          # Two paths for pytorch. Every scheduled run takes the first. The
          # second serves an explicit `pytorch-ref`, which nothing passes today:
          # PR validation has its own pipeline, `_woa-pr-build-test.yml`.
          # `resolve_ref` stays in use for audio/vision either way.
          delivery_id=""
          if [ "${REF}" = "nightly" ]; then
            # Resolve the upstream `main` commit the nightly was cut from and
            # build *that* rather than the nightly branch tip. The tip is a
            # generated commit that does not exist on `main`, so it cannot key a
            # HUD row; see `scripts/crcr/resolve_nightly_commits.py`.
            #
            # Pin resolution to when the run was *first* started, not to now.
            # The nightly tip advances every night, so resolving "the tip" on a
            # re-run would silently retarget a different main SHA: the re-run
            # would build a different commit and file its HUD row under a
            # different delivery-id, instead of replacing the row for the day it
            # was meant to repair. Attempt 1's `run_started_at` is immutable,
            # unlike the run-level field, which resets on every re-run.
            as_of=$(gh api \
              "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/attempts/1" \
              -q '.run_started_at')
            if [ -z "${as_of}" ] || [ "${as_of}" = "null" ]; then
              echo "::error::Could not read attempt 1's start time; refusing to resolve nightly against a moving tip." >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Resolving nightly as of ${as_of} (attempt 1 start)"

            # Deep enough to still contain that day's nightly when a run is
            # re-run weeks later; `resolve_nightly_commits.py` fails loudly
            # rather than guessing if the window still falls short.
            gh api "repos/pytorch/pytorch/commits?sha=nightly&per_page=100" > nightly-commits.json
            python3 scripts/crcr/resolve_nightly_commits.py \
              --commits-json nightly-commits.json \
              --as-of "${as_of}" \
              --github-output resolved.env \
              --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            sha="$(sed -n 's/^source-sha=//p' resolved.env)"; require_sha pytorch "${sha}" "${REF}"
            # Date the wheels from the nightly release itself rather than today's
            # clock, so a re-run reproduces the same wheel version the original
            # attempt built - the same reasoning as the SHA pin above.
            nightly_date="$(sed -n 's/^nightly-date=//p' resolved.env)"
            delivery_id="${sha}"
          else
            # An explicit ref is not a nightly of upstream main, so it is never
            # HUD-eligible and has no nightly release to take a date from - fall
            # back to today's clock for the wheel version. `delivery_id` stays
            # empty, which is what switches both reporting jobs off.
            sha="$(resolve_ref "https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch" "${REF}")"; require_sha pytorch "${sha}" "${REF}"
            nightly_date="$(date -u +%Y%m%d)"
          fi
          if ! [[ "${nightly_date}" =~ ^[0-9]{8}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Could not derive a yyyyMMdd wheel date (got '${nightly_date:-<empty>}')." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          audio_sha="$(resolve_ref "https://github.com/pytorch/audio" "${AUDIO_REF}")";   require_sha torchaudio  "${audio_sha}"  "${AUDIO_REF}"
          vision_sha="$(resolve_ref "https://github.com/pytorch/vision" "${VISION_REF}")"; require_sha torchvision "${vision_sha}" "${VISION_REF}"
          echo "Resolved pytorch '${REF}' -> ${sha}, torchaudio '${AUDIO_REF}' -> ${audio_sha}, torchvision '${VISION_REF}' -> ${vision_sha}"

          # Belt-and-braces on top of the path selection above: only a
          # scheduled run may publish, so wiring up another trigger later
          # cannot start writing nightly rows unnoticed.
          case "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" in
            schedule) ;;
            *) delivery_id="" ;;
          esac
          {
            echo "pytorch-ref=${sha}"
            echo "torchaudio-ref=${audio_sha}"
            echo "torchvision-ref=${vision_sha}"
            echo "nightly-date=${nightly_date}"
            echo "crcr-delivery-id=${delivery_id}"
            # Republished so the reporting job can check the shard count it
            # expects against the one that actually drove the fanout, instead
            # of carrying its own copy of the number.
            echo "num-shards=${NUM_SHARDS}"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ -n "${delivery_id}" ]; then
            hud_status="enabled -> ${delivery_id}"
          else
            hud_status="disabled"
          fi
          {
            echo "## windows-woa-build-test config"
            echo ""
            echo "| field | value |"
            echo "| --- | --- |"
            echo "| trigger | \`${{ github.event_name }}\` |"
            echo "| pytorch-ref (input) | \`${REF}\` |"
            echo "| pytorch-ref (resolved SHA) | \`${sha}\` |"
            echo "| torchaudio-ref (resolved SHA) | \`${audio_sha}\` |"
            echo "| torchvision-ref (resolved SHA) | \`${vision_sha}\` |"
            echo "| nightly wheel date | \`${nightly_date}\` |"
            echo "| python-versions (build + test) | \`${PYTHON_VERSIONS:-(all)}\` |"
            echo "| test config | \`per-version / cu134\` |"
            echo "| shards | \`${NUM_SHARDS}\` |"
            echo "| HUD reporting | \`${hud_status}\` |"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  build:
    name: woa-${{ matrix.config.label }}-cu134-build
    needs: prep
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # One entry per Python build cell (CTK 13.4). The shared `woa-arm64`
        # runners carry every python venv, so python is NOT in the runner label.
        #
        # `label` names the GitHub jobs. It does NOT name a HUD row: however
        # many Python cells are enabled, they are reported as one build row and
        # one test row (see `report-build-crcr` below), so the row name is the
        # workflow-level `HUD_ENV` rather than anything per-cell.
        #
        # !! Re-enabling a cell below means adding its label to `PYTHON_LABELS`
        # at the top of this file, in the same commit. A commented-out matrix
        # entry produces no job at all - not even a skipped one - so the two
        # lists have to agree on exactly which cells exist. They fail in
        # opposite, both-safe directions: a label listed but not enabled fails
        # the reporting job loudly (`resolve_cell_conclusion.py` refuses to
        # guess when a cell matches no job), while a cell enabled but not
        # listed is silently left out of the HUD row it belongs in.
        config: &config
          # TEMPORARY: limited to Python 3.13 only. Re-enable the other cells
          # (3.11 / 3.12 / 3.14 / 3.14t) once they are validated (planned in a
          # few days). The list feeds BOTH the build and test matrices.
          # - { version: "3.11", label: "py311" }
          # - { version: "3.12", label: "py312" }
          - { version: "3.13", label: "py313" }
          # - { version: "3.14", label: "py314" }
          # Free-threaded (no-GIL) 3.14 -> cp314t wheels. The runner venv `py314t`
          # is backed by python3.14t.exe; the build tooling is driven by the venv,
          # so no extra build flag is needed here.
          # - { version: "3.14t", label: "py314t" }
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_woa-build.yml
    with:
      runner-base: ${{ inputs.runner-base || 'woa-arm64' }}
      python-version: ${{ matrix.config.version }}
      python-label: ${{ matrix.config.label }}
      cuda-version: "13.4"
      cuda-arch-list: "8.9;10.3+PTX;12.0;12.1+PTX"
      build-environment: win-woa-arm64
      pytorch-ref: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.pytorch-ref }}
      nightly-date: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.nightly-date }}
      # Extensions pinned to the SHAs resolved in prep so every cell builds the
      # same torchaudio/torchvision source (reproducible across the matrix).
      torchaudio-ref: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.torchaudio-ref }}
      torchvision-ref: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.torchvision-ref }}
      # Must match the paired test cell's `wheel-artifact` for the same label.
      # No run_attempt in the name: "Re-run failed jobs" bumps run_attempt but does NOT
      # re-run this already-succeeded build, so the wheel must keep a stable name (scoped
      # to run_id only) that the re-running test cell can still resolve. The build upload
      # uses overwrite:true so a full "Re-run all jobs" (build re-runs) replaces it cleanly.
      wheel-artifact: woa-${{ matrix.config.label }}-cu134-${{ github.run_id }}

  test:
    name: woa-${{ matrix.config.label }}-cu134-arm64-test
    # `prep` is here for its `num-shards` output below, not for ordering: a
    # `needs.<job>` reference outside the job's own `needs` evaluates to '' rather
    # than erroring, and an explicit '' overrides the callee's own default.
    needs: [prep, build]
    # Run the test matrix even when SOME build cells failed. With a plain `needs: build`
    # a single failed build cell marks the whole build job `failure` and GitHub auto-skips
    # every test cell - so a partial build (e.g. py311/py313 pass, py314t fails) would test
    # nothing. `!cancelled()` overrides that per-matrix auto-skip: each cell (fail-fast:false)
    # independently downloads its own wheel, so successfully-built cells get tested while a
    # failed-build cell simply errors at its wheel download (no wheel to test). The
    # `!= 'skipped'` guard keeps tests off when the build stage was wholesale skipped
    # (e.g. prep failed, or the repository_dispatch gate parked it).
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.build.result != 'skipped' }}
    # One test cell per built Python (reuses the build matrix anchor). Each cell
    # fans out 4 shards inside _woa-test.yml and consumes its own build artifact.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config: *config
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_woa-test.yml
    with:
      runner-base: ${{ inputs.runner-base || 'woa-arm64' }}
      python-version: ${{ matrix.config.version }}
      python-label: ${{ matrix.config.label }}
      cuda-version: "13.4"
      cuda-arch-list: "8.9;10.3+PTX;12.0;12.1+PTX"
      build-environment: win-woa-arm64
      test-config: "default"
      # Passed explicitly rather than left to `_woa-test.yml`'s own default, so
      # the fan-out and `report-test-crcr`'s `--expected-shards` read the same
      # number. Both happen to be 4 today; if they ever diverged the reporting
      # job would expect fewer shards than ran and stop noticing a missing one.
      num-shards: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.num-shards }}
      # Consume exactly this cell's build wheel artifact (same name as _woa-build.yml).
      # Stable across attempts (no run_attempt) so a test-only re-run still downloads the
      # wheel the build produced on the original attempt.
      wheel-artifact: woa-${{ matrix.config.label }}-cu134-${{ github.run_id }}

  # ===========================================================================
  # Sign and publish this run's wheels (`_woa-sign-publish.yml`). It needs only
  # the builds, so it runs alongside the tests rather than after them: the test
  # shards routinely fail, and publication judges each cell on its own build
  # job (`scripts/publish/build_run.py`). `!cancelled()` for the same reason as
  # `test`: the cells that built still publish when another cell's build failed.
  #
  # Opt-in through `vars.WOA_NIGHTLY_PUBLISH`, so the nightly publishes nothing
  # until Artifact Signing and the Charon tenant are in place:
  #   dry-run   nightly GitHub Release + Kitmaker upload=false requests
  #   release   the same, then the upload=true release to pypi.nvidia.com
  #
  # Holds `contents: write`, which is why the PR path calls
  # `_woa-pr-build-test.yml` rather than this file.
  # ===========================================================================
  publication:
    name: sign and publish
    needs: build
    if: >-
      ${{ !cancelled() && needs.build.result != 'skipped'
          && github.event_name == 'schedule'
          && (vars.WOA_NIGHTLY_PUBLISH == 'dry-run' || vars.WOA_NIGHTLY_PUBLISH == 'release') }}
    # The group every caller of `_woa-sign-publish.yml` holds; see its header.
    concurrency:
      group: windows-woa-publish-${{ github.run_id }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      actions: read
      attestations: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_woa-sign-publish.yml
    with:
      build-run-id: ${{ github.run_id }}
      channel: nightly
      run-kitmaker-dry-run: true
      run-kitmaker-release: ${{ vars.WOA_NIGHTLY_PUBLISH == 'release' }}
      runner-base: ${{ inputs.runner-base || 'woa-arm64' }}
    secrets:
      KITMAKER_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.KITMAKER_API_TOKEN }}

  # ===========================================================================
  # Post-test rollup. Renders which test jobs failed (with log links) plus the
  # de-duplicated cross-shard failing-test list (per-cell + overall). Runs
  # `if: always()`, informational only - never reports a status of its own.
  # ===========================================================================
  test-summary:
    name: test-summary
    needs: test
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout this repository (for summary script)
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      - name: Aggregate failed test jobs
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh api --paginate \
            "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/attempts/${{ github.run_attempt }}/jobs" \
            -q '.jobs[]' | jq -s '.' > jobs.json
          python3 scripts/test-summary/aggregate_failures.py \
            --jobs-json jobs.json \
            --title "PyTorch WoA test summary (run ${{ github.run_id }})" \
            >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Download all shard test-reports
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: test-reports-*
          path: all-reports

      - name: Aggregate failed tests across shards
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python3 scripts/test-summary/parse_failures.py \
            --shards-root all-reports \
            --title "Aggregate failed tests - all shards (run ${{ github.run_id }})" \
            >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # ===========================================================================
  # Cross-Repo CI Relay (CRCR) HUD reporting - trust level L2.
  #
  # The arm64 counterpart of the same two jobs in `windows-rtx-build-test.yml`,
  # with one deliberate difference: RTX reports one row per matrix cell, while
  # WoA reduces every Python cell into a single build row and a single test
  # row. One row per wheel per stage is more upstream surface than a small set
  # of stable logical jobs, and the Python version is recoverable from our own
  # run when a row goes red.
  #
  # Both jobs are TERMINAL - nothing depends on them, so a relay outage can
  # never skip a build or a test. That is why they are not steps inside the
  # reusable workflows: a callback failure inside `_woa-build.yml` would fail
  # the caller's `build` job and skip the whole `test` matrix behind it. Being
  # terminal costs us `needs.<cell>.result`, so the conclusion is recovered
  # from the Jobs API instead.
  #
  # Only ever active for a genuine nightly: `prep` leaves the delivery id empty
  # for runs that pinned an explicit ref, which switches both jobs off.
  # ===========================================================================
  report-build-crcr:
    name: report build to HUD
    needs: [prep, build]
    if: always() && needs.prep.outputs.crcr-delivery-id != '' && needs.build.result != 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository (for CRCR scripts)
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      # Worst outcome across every Python build cell: one version failing to
      # build is not a green build row. Versions the operator narrowed out
      # resolve to `skipped`, which loses to every real outcome, so a narrowed
      # run reports the versions that actually ran - and a run where all of
      # them were narrowed out resolves to `skipped` and reports nothing.
      - name: Resolve build conclusion across Python cells
        id: cell
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh api --paginate \
            "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/attempts/${{ github.run_attempt }}/jobs" \
            -q '.jobs[]' | jq -s '.' > jobs.json
          cells=()
          for label in ${PYTHON_LABELS}; do
            cells+=(--cell "woa-${label}-cu134-build")
          done
          python3 scripts/crcr/resolve_cell_conclusion.py \
            --jobs-json jobs.json \
            "${cells[@]}" \
            --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" \
            --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Report build result to CRCR
        if: steps.cell.outputs.should-report == 'true'
        uses: ./.github/actions/crcr-callback
        with:
          event-type: nightly
          delivery-id: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.crcr-delivery-id }}
          job-name: ${{ env.HUD_ENV }} / build
          status: completed
          conclusion: ${{ steps.cell.outputs.conclusion }}
          artifact-url: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/attempts/${{ github.run_attempt }}

  report-test-crcr:
    name: report test to HUD
    needs: [prep, test]
    if: always() && needs.prep.outputs.crcr-delivery-id != '' && needs.test.result != 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository (for CRCR scripts)
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      # How many Python cells this run should have reports from. Every run is
      # the full enabled matrix - there is no subset input - so the count is
      # just the length of `PYTHON_LABELS`. It is what tells the summariser
      # that a whole version left no reports, which the shard tally alone
      # cannot see.
      - name: Count expected Python cells
        id: selected
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          count=0
          for label in ${PYTHON_LABELS}; do
            count=$((count + 1))
          done
          echo "count=${count}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "expecting reports from ${count} Python cell(s): ${PYTHON_LABELS}"

      - name: Resolve test conclusion across Python cells
        id: cell
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh api --paginate \
            "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/attempts/${{ github.run_attempt }}/jobs" \
            -q '.jobs[]' | jq -s '.' > jobs.json
          cells=()
          for label in ${PYTHON_LABELS}; do
            cells+=(--cell "woa-${label}-cu134-arm64-test")
          done
          python3 scripts/crcr/resolve_cell_conclusion.py \
            --jobs-json jobs.json \
            "${cells[@]}" \
            --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" \
            --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Every Python version's shards, since they all feed the one row. The
      # run id and attempt keep a sibling run's reports out.
      #
      # `continue-on-error` here does not mask an undelivered callback - that
      # rule applies to the callback step, which is left bare below. Shards that died
      # before uploading anything still owe upstream a red row, so a failed
      # download has to fall through to the summariser (which fails closed on
      # any shortfall) rather than abort before reporting.
      - name: Download every cell's shard test-reports
        id: download
        if: steps.cell.outputs.should-report == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: test-reports-win-woa-arm64-*-arm64-shard*-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: cell-reports

      # `--group-regex` splits the downloaded shards back out by Python label
      # and scans each version on its own before summing. Without it the
      # versions would be unioned on test identity, and since they all run the
      # same suite, each test would collapse into one result and the totals
      # sent upstream would understate what ran by roughly the number of cells.
      # It is a no-op while only one cell is enabled, and correct the moment a
      # second one is.
      #
      # `--expected-shards` is per version and is the shard count
      # `_woa-test.yml` defaults to, rather than the Jobs API count its RTX
      # counterpart uses: `_woa-test.yml` fans out via a `setup` job
      # ("shard plan") that carries the same `<cell> / ` prefix as the shards,
      # so the API count reads one too many. `--expected-groups` catches the
      # case the shard tally cannot - an entire Python cell that left no
      # reports at all.
      - name: Summarize test results across Python cells
        id: results
        if: steps.cell.outputs.should-report == 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 scripts/crcr/build_test_results.py \
            --shards-root cell-reports \
            --group-regex 'win-woa-arm64-(?P<group>[^-]+)-arm64-shard' \
            --expected-shards "${{ needs.prep.outputs.num-shards }}" \
            --expected-groups "${{ steps.selected.outputs.count }}" \
            --title "HUD test results - ${{ env.HUD_ENV }} / test (arm64)" \
            --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" \
            --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Two independent signals must agree before the row is called green: the
      # shard jobs' own GitHub outcomes, and the JUnit evidence they left
      # behind. Each alone has a blind spot - a shard cancelled before writing
      # any XML looks clean to the summariser, and a harness that exits 0 while
      # reporting failed cases looks clean to GitHub.
      - name: Combine conclusions
        id: conclusion
        if: steps.cell.outputs.should-report == 'true'
        shell: bash
        env:
          JOB_CONCLUSION: ${{ steps.cell.outputs.conclusion }}
          REPORT_CONCLUSION: ${{ steps.results.outputs.conclusion }}
          DOWNLOAD_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.download.outcome }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "${JOB_CONCLUSION}" = "cancelled" ]; then
            conclusion=cancelled
          elif [ "${JOB_CONCLUSION}" = "success" ] && [ "${REPORT_CONCLUSION}" = "success" ]; then
            conclusion=success
          else
            conclusion=failure
          fi
          echo "conclusion=${conclusion}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "${DOWNLOAD_OUTCOME}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "::warning title=CRCR artifacts::Could not download shard reports; test counts may be incomplete."
          fi
          {
            echo ""
            echo "| conclusion input | value |"
            echo "| --- | --- |"
            echo "| shard jobs result | \`${JOB_CONCLUSION}\` |"
            echo "| report evidence | \`${REPORT_CONCLUSION}\` |"
            echo "| artifact download | \`${DOWNLOAD_OUTCOME}\` |"
            echo "| Python versions reported | \`${{ steps.results.outputs.groups }}\` of \`${{ steps.selected.outputs.count }}\` |"
            echo "| **reported conclusion** | \`${conclusion}\` |"
            echo "| delivery-id (upstream main SHA) | \`${{ needs.prep.outputs.crcr-delivery-id }}\` |"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Report test results to CRCR
        if: steps.cell.outputs.should-report == 'true'
        uses: ./.github/actions/crcr-callback
        with:
          event-type: nightly
          delivery-id: ${{ needs.prep.outputs.crcr-delivery-id }}
          job-name: ${{ env.HUD_ENV }} / test (arm64)
          status: completed
          conclusion: ${{ steps.conclusion.outputs.conclusion }}
          test-results: ${{ steps.results.outputs.test-results }}
          artifact-url: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/attempts/${{ github.run_attempt }}

      # The HUD and GitHub conclusions have to agree. The shard
      # jobs can go green while their reports say otherwise - a harness that
      # exits 0 with failed cases, or shards that left no evidence at all - and
      # in that case the callback above has already told upstream `failure`.
      # Fail here too, so whoever opens the run sees the same answer the HUD
      # shows. Ordered after the callback deliberately: the result has to be
      # delivered before this job goes red.
      - name: Match GitHub to the reported conclusion
        if: steps.conclusion.outputs.conclusion == 'failure' && steps.cell.outputs.conclusion == 'success'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::error title=CRCR conclusion::Every WoA test shard passed, but their reports show failures or missing evidence. Reported 'failure' to the HUD; failing this job so GitHub agrees."
          exit 1
