name: _rtx-test

# Reusable Windows RTX test workflow. Two install paths, one set of
# downstream steps:
#
#   A) artifact path  - the wheel is a producer-uploaded artifact from
#                       `_rtx-build.yml`; SHA travels alongside the
#                       wheel in `built_pytorch_sha.txt`. Used by
#                       `windows-rtx-build-test.yml`.
#   B) pip-index path - the wheel is already on a public pip index
#                       (download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/torch/). The
#                       orchestrator passes a `pytorch-ref` (typically
#                       a branch like `nightly`); `actions/checkout@v7`
#                       resolves it to a concrete commit, this workflow
#                       reads the commit's UTC date, greps the index
#                       for a wheel whose filename carries that exact
#                       `devYYYYMMDD` tag together with the matrix
#                       `cu<label>` / `cp<pyshort>` tags, and installs
#                       the resolved URL directly. The job fails fast
#                       if the index has no wheel for that date
#                       (i.e. the wheel for the source we just checked
#                       out is not yet published). Used by
#                       `windows-rtx-wheel-test.yml`.
#
# Exactly one path must be selected per call: set `wheel-artifact`
# (path A) or `pytorch-ref` (path B).
#
# Each invocation is one (config x arch) test cell. Sharding is an
# internal fanout: `strategy.matrix.shard` below spawns 5 parallel
# runners under this single workflow call, and the test step exports
# `SHARD_NUMBER` (per-cell) / `NUM_TEST_SHARDS` (constant 5) /
# `TEST_CONFIG` so `.ci/pytorch/win-test.sh` (which delegates to
# `test/run_test.py`) runs only its slice. The orchestrator therefore
# sees one cell per (config x arch), not one cell per shard - matching
# the upstream `_win-rtx-test.yml` pattern in pytorch/pytorch PR
# #176678 where the test job's `test-matrix` JSON carries the shard
# fanout internally.
#
# A lightweight runner-diagnostics monitor samples host + GPU metrics
# in the background while the test step runs in the foreground, so OOT
# failures can be triaged against an accurate picture of the machine.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner-base:
        description: "Base runner label for the test pool (e.g. rtx-40x0-test)."
        type: string
        required: true
      python-version:
        description: "Python version in dotted form (e.g. 3.12)."
        type: string
        required: true
      python-label:
        description: "Python label used in runner labels (e.g. py312)."
        type: string
        required: true
      cuda-version:
        description: "CUDA toolkit version in dotted form (e.g. 13.0)."
        type: string
        required: true
      cuda-label:
        description: "CUDA label used in runner labels (e.g. cu130)."
        type: string
        required: true
      cuda-arch-list:
        description: >
          Target SM for TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST in the test step (e.g. '8.9'
          for sm89 / RTX 40x0, '12.0' for sm120 / RTX 50x0). The wheel
          itself may be multi-arch; this just tells the test runner which
          arch to exercise.
        type: string
        required: true
      arch-name:
        description: "Architecture token (e.g. 'sm89', 'sm120'); used for the test-architectures filter."
        type: string
        required: true
      build-environment:
        description: "Logical name passed through as BUILD_ENVIRONMENT."
        type: string
        required: true

      # ---- Sharding (matches pytorch/pytorch PR #176678) --------------
      # The shard fanout is internal to this workflow: each invocation
      # spawns 5 parallel shard runners via `strategy.matrix.shard`
      # below. The caller does NOT see shards in its own matrix - one
      # call to this reusable workflow == one (config x arch) test
      # cell, period. To change the shard count, edit both the
      # `shard:` list under `strategy.matrix` and the `NUM_TEST_SHARDS`
      # env in the test step. The caller's `report-test-crcr` job needs
      # no update: it counts this cell's shard jobs via the Jobs API.
      test-config:
        description: "Test-config name forwarded as TEST_CONFIG (e.g. 'default')."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "default"

      # ---- Path A: artifact-driven (source build) ---------------------
      wheel-artifact:
        description: "Artifact name carrying wheel + built_pytorch_sha.txt. Mutually exclusive with pytorch-ref."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""

      # ---- Path B: pip-index-driven (nightly wheel) -------------------
      pytorch-ref:
        description: "pytorch/pytorch ref to checkout (branch, tag, or SHA). Required when wheel-artifact is empty."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""
      wheel-index-url:
        description: "Nightly wheel index page (PEP 503 simple index). The resolver greps this for a wheel whose filename matches the checked-out commit's date and the matrix cuda + python tags."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/torch/"

      # ---- matrix subset filters -------------------------------------
      # The caller cannot reference `matrix.*` in its own job-level
      # `if:` (GitHub Actions restricts that context for reusable-
      # workflow-calling jobs), so the per-cell filter is evaluated
      # here instead, against this invocation's own `python-version` /
      # `cuda-version` / `arch-name` inputs. Empty string disables the
      # corresponding filter dimension.
      python-versions:
        description: "Comma-separated allowlist of python versions; empty = no filter."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""
      cuda-versions:
        description: "Comma-separated allowlist of CUDA toolkit versions; empty = no filter."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""
      test-architectures:
        description: "Comma-separated allowlist of arch tokens (e.g. 'sm89,sm120'); empty = no filter."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read

jobs:
  test:
    name: test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/5)
    if: >
      (inputs.python-versions == '' || contains(inputs.python-versions, inputs.python-version))
      && (inputs.cuda-versions == '' || contains(inputs.cuda-versions, inputs.cuda-version))
      && (inputs.test-architectures == '' || contains(inputs.test-architectures, inputs.arch-name))
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    runs-on:
      - ${{ inputs.runner-base }}
      - ${{ inputs.python-label }}
      - ${{ inputs.cuda-label }}
    # Raised from 210 so that the in-step watchdog (RUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC
    # below), not this cap, is always what stops a hung shard. A job-level
    # timeout is a bad way to catch a hang: GitHub *cancels* the job, so the
    # shard summary never renders, the test-reports upload races the
    # cancellation, and the log just stops with no indication of what wedged.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    env:
      # ---- carried from the matrix cell -------------------------------
      BUILD_ENVIRONMENT: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
      PYTHON_VERSION: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
      CUDA_VERSION: ${{ inputs.cuda-version }}
      TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: ${{ inputs.cuda-arch-list }}
      # ---- pytorch CI knobs (subset of pytorch/pytorch PR #176678) ----
      USE_CUDA: "1"
      # Runner image already carries the Windows SDK and VS BuildTools;
      # tell win-test.sh not to re-install them.
      INSTALL_WINDOWS_SDK: "0"
      # Don't stop the whole shard on the first test failure - we want
      # the full pass/fail picture per shard.
      CONTINUE_THROUGH_ERROR: "1"
      VC_PRODUCT: "BuildTools"
      VC_YEAR: "2022"
      VS_VERSION: "17.4.1"
      VC_VERSION: ""
      PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW: "0"
      # Only instantiate CUDA variants for PyTorch device-generic tests.
      # This prevents generated CPU cases from running in the RTX test jobs.
      PYTORCH_TESTING_DEVICE_ONLY_FOR: "cuda"
      CI: "1"
      # `CI` above is what switches on run_test.py's S3 telemetry upload:
      # --upload-artifacts-while-running defaults to IS_CI and has no negating
      # flag, so after every test file handle_complete() calls
      # parse_xml_and_upload_json(), which puts the report into pytorch's own
      # `gha-artifacts` bucket via boto3. We hold no credentials for someone
      # else's bucket, so it can only ever fail - but on a non-AWS host boto3
      # first probes the EC2 instance-metadata service at 169.254.169.254
      # looking for them, and that probe can stall for minutes. It runs once
      # per test file, so a single stall wedges the shard with no output. The
      # WoA path hit exactly this (3h+ before the watchdog killed it) and
      # guards it the same way - see Set-RunTestTelemetryGuardEnv in
      # tools/woa-build/shared/test/TestShardRunner.ps1.
      #
      # Disabling the probe makes the doomed upload raise NoCredentialsError
      # immediately instead of hanging. run_test.py's only other network step,
      # the disabled/slow-test download, is an anonymous public HTTPS GET and
      # is unaffected.
      AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED: "true"
      # Harden every pip invocation in the job against transient index /
      # CDN failures - including the ones we do not call ourselves, i.e.
      # the `pip install -r .ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt` buried in
      # pytorch's own setup_pytorch_env.bat. pip reads these from the
      # environment, so they apply to nested batch scripts too. pip's
      # default 15s socket timeout is far too tight for this pool: a
      # single slow index response returns an empty candidate list, pip
      # reports "No matching distribution found" for a package that
      # plainly exists, and the whole requirements resolve is abandoned.
      PIP_RETRIES: "8"
      PIP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: "60"
      # Wall-clock cap for the whole win-test.sh run, enforced in-step - and,
      # per the watchdog comment below, the only bound that reliably fires on
      # Windows for a hang outside a running test. Sized from the 19 measurable
      # shards of a full run: the slowest guarded step was 112min, and that one
      # included a 15min per-test timeout plus its retry; the slowest without a
      # hang was 106min. 165min is 1.47x the worst observed, leaving room for
      # pytorch's test count to grow and for the unresolved 1.5-1.8x shard
      # imbalance, while staying far enough under `timeout-minutes` that the
      # watchdog always wins the race against the job cap.
      #
      # Lowered from 195min, which was sized against a "~168min of run_test
      # time" observation from before the seeding balanced the shards - so it
      # was costing an extra 45min on every shard it had to kill.
      RUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC: "9900"
      # Per-test cap handed to pytest-timeout, sized from the JUnit reports of
      # a real run : across 278,992 test cases the slowest single test was
      # test_multiprocessing::test_fs_sharing at 7.8min, only two exceeded 5min,
      # none reached 10min, and p99.99 was 68s. 15min is ~2x the observed worst
      # case - enough headroom for a slower runner or a loaded machine, while
      # still cutting the time a wedged test can burn. When it trips it dumps
      # every thread's stack, which is the evidence a silent hang otherwise
      # denies us. Also matches PerTestTimeoutSec in the WoA path's
      # tools/woa-build/shared/env/defaults/test-runtime.psd1, so both arches
      # fail a wedged test on the same clock.
      PER_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC: "900"
      # Wall-clock cap on a single test-file process, enforced from inside it
      # by scripts/test-bounds/pythonpath/sitecustomize.py. This is the bound
      # that covers the phases pytest-timeout cannot (import, collection, and
      # teardown after the last test) without costing the whole shard the way
      # RUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC does.
      #
      # Sized per *invocation*, not per file: run_test.py runs each file twice
      # (serial tests, then the rest) and pytest-shards the big ones, so the
      # figure to clear is the slowest single invocation. Across 10,331
      # measured invocations that was 26.6min (export/test_sparse; 23.0min for
      # test_foreach 2/6 on this path). 45min is 1.69x that. Note the whole
      # file can legitimately far exceed this - test_meta totals ~142min across
      # 15 pieces - so this must never be compared against a per-file total.
      PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SEC: "2700"
      # Short physical path the pytorch checkout is relocated to right after
      # checkout. The runner workspace lives at
      #   C:\actions-runner\_work\pytorch-windows-ci\pytorch-windows-ci\pytorch
      # (the repo name is doubled), so test-time cpp_extension builds write
      # object/dep files ~290 chars deep and blow past Windows MAX_PATH (260).
      # Relocating to C:\pt strips ~60 chars off every derived path. See the
      # "Relocate pytorch checkout" step for the full rationale.
      PT_ROOT: 'C:\pt'
      # Where each armed test-file process appends one JSON line, and where the
      # step after the test run reads them back from. Both need it, so it is
      # job-level; the literal repeats PT_ROOT above because a job-level `env`
      # entry cannot reference a sibling one. Extension matters -
      # parse_failures.py scans this tree for *.log / *.txt, so a .log here
      # would be fed to the failure parser.
      PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_LOG: 'C:\pt/test/test-reports/per-process-bound.jsonl'
    steps:
      - name: Validate install-path inputs
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.wheel-artifact }}" ]; then
            echo "install path: artifact (${{ inputs.wheel-artifact }})"
          elif [ -n "${{ inputs.pytorch-ref }}" ]; then
            echo "install path: pip-index"
            echo "  pytorch-ref:     ${{ inputs.pytorch-ref }}"
            echo "  wheel-index-url: ${{ inputs.wheel-index-url }}"
          else
            echo "::error::Either 'wheel-artifact' or 'pytorch-ref' must be set." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # Let git use the \\?\ extended-length prefix so the deep recursive
      # submodule checkout of pytorch/pytorch (third_party/.../pybind11/...)
      # never trips the 260-char MAX_PATH during `git checkout`. No admin
      # needed (--global writes the runner user's gitconfig), unlike the
      # registry LongPathsEnabled flag. This covers `git` itself; the
      # MAX_PATH that the test-time compilers (cl/nvcc) hit is handled
      # separately by relocating the checkout to C:\pt (see that step).
      - name: Enable git long paths
        shell: bash
        run: git config --global core.longpaths true

      # Retried in three explicit attempts. actions/checkout only retries
      # the git fetch internally (3 tries, ~90s total) and then fails the
      # step, which on this pool is shorter than an observed github.com
      # connectivity blip. Losing THIS checkout is disproportionately
      # expensive: every later `uses: ./oot/...` local action and the
      # summary script live in this tree, so a single missed clone turns
      # one network error into a pile of misleading "Can't find action.yml"
      # / "can't open file parse_failures.py" failures.
      - name: Checkout repository (runner-diagnostics actions)
        id: oot_checkout_1
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          path: oot
          show-progress: false
          # The pytorch checkout below already does this; these need it for the
          # same reason. The test harness runs the PR's own test code on this
          # runner, so a token in any `.git/config` on the filesystem is
          # readable by it. Nothing here pushes.
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Wait before OOT checkout retry
        if: steps.oot_checkout_1.outcome == 'failure'
        shell: bash
        run: sleep 60

      - name: Checkout repository (retry 2)
        id: oot_checkout_2
        if: steps.oot_checkout_1.outcome == 'failure'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          path: oot
          show-progress: false
          # The pytorch checkout below already does this; these need it for the
          # same reason. The test harness runs the PR's own test code on this
          # runner, so a token in any `.git/config` on the filesystem is
          # readable by it. Nothing here pushes.
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Wait before final OOT checkout retry
        if: steps.oot_checkout_1.outcome == 'failure' && steps.oot_checkout_2.outcome == 'failure'
        shell: bash
        run: sleep 120

      - name: Checkout repository (retry 3)
        if: steps.oot_checkout_1.outcome == 'failure' && steps.oot_checkout_2.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          path: oot
          show-progress: false
          # The pytorch checkout below already does this; these need it for the
          # same reason. The test harness runs the PR's own test code on this
          # runner, so a token in any `.git/config` on the filesystem is
          # readable by it. Nothing here pushes.
          persist-credentials: false

      # Pull the wheel + SHA produced by the paired build job from GitHub
      # Actions artifact storage. Lands files under `artifact/...`.
      #
      # Retried in three attempts like the checkout above, and for the same
      # reason. The action does retry internally, but all five of its tries
      # live inside one attempt against one blob-storage redirect URL: when
      # that URL went bad mid-transfer on this 1.7GB artifact, the five tries
      # burned 13 minutes and the step failed with "Artifact download failed
      # after 5 retries", losing a whole shard before it ran a single test.
      # A fresh attempt asks for a new redirect, which is the part the
      # internal retries never repeat.
      - name: Download wheel artifact
        id: wheel_1
        if: inputs.wheel-artifact != ''
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.wheel-artifact }}
          path: artifact

      # Clear the half-extracted tree first. A truncated wheel here would
      # otherwise surface much later as an install or import error, and
      # `artifact/built_pytorch_sha.txt` is read by the very next step.
      - name: Wait before wheel download retry
        if: inputs.wheel-artifact != '' && steps.wheel_1.outcome == 'failure'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          rm -rf artifact
          sleep 60

      - name: Download wheel artifact (retry 2)
        id: wheel_2
        if: inputs.wheel-artifact != '' && steps.wheel_1.outcome == 'failure'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.wheel-artifact }}
          path: artifact

      - name: Wait before final wheel download retry
        if: inputs.wheel-artifact != '' && steps.wheel_1.outcome == 'failure' && steps.wheel_2.outcome == 'failure'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          rm -rf artifact
          sleep 120

      - name: Download wheel artifact (retry 3)
        if: inputs.wheel-artifact != '' && steps.wheel_1.outcome == 'failure' && steps.wheel_2.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.wheel-artifact }}
          path: artifact

      - name: Resolve pytorch ref to check out
        id: ref
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.wheel-artifact }}" ]; then
            ref=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < artifact/built_pytorch_sha.txt)
            if ! [[ "$ref" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::Invalid SHA in artifact: '$ref'" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          else
            ref="${{ inputs.pytorch-ref }}"
          fi
          echo "ref=$ref" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "checkout ref: $ref"

      - name: Checkout pytorch/pytorch at the resolved ref
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          repository: pytorch/pytorch
          ref: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.ref }}
          path: pytorch
          # Submodules are deliberately NOT fetched by this action - the
          # retried step below does it instead. actions/checkout aborts the
          # entire step on the first submodule fetch error and exposes no
          # retry for that phase, and pytorch's recursive tree reaches deep
          # third-party hosts (third_party/flash-attention -> aiter ->
          # ROCm/composable_kernel) where one transient connect failure was
          # killing shards ~55 minutes into checkout, after the main clone
          # had already succeeded.
          submodules: false
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: true
          # This checkout is read-only (the tree is relocated to C:\pt and
          # only built/tested, never pushed), so it does not need a GitHub
          # token persisted in .git/config.
          persist-credentials: false

      # `--jobs 4` also cuts a large chunk off the serial ~55min recursive
      # clone this replaces.
      - name: Fetch pytorch submodules (retried)
        shell: bash
        working-directory: pytorch
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if git submodule update --init --recursive --depth 1 --jobs 4; then
              echo "pytorch submodules ready (attempt ${attempt})"
              exit 0
            fi
            delay=$((attempt * 60))
            echo "::warning::Submodule fetch attempt ${attempt} failed; retrying in ${delay}s."
            sleep "${delay}"
          done
          echo "::error::pytorch submodule fetch failed after 3 attempts." >&2
          exit 1

      # Windows MAX_PATH (260) mitigation, root cause fix. The runner image
      # already sets the LongPathsEnabled registry flag (packer
      # win_build_setup/tools.ps1), but that does NOT help the test-time
      # cpp_extension builds (test_libtorch_agnostic, test_python_agnostic,
      # ...): nvcc does not support paths over MAX_PATH at all (per the CUDA
      # docs), and cl's long-path opt-in does not cover every output path the
      # ninja/setuptools build constructs. setuptools writes each object to
      #   <ext>\build\temp.win-amd64-cpython-312\Release\<ABSOLUTE-SOURCE-PATH>
      # i.e. the already-deep workspace path doubled, so cl fails "C1083:
      # Cannot open compiler generated file" and nvcc "Could not open output
      # file ...obj.d". The only reliable fix is a genuinely SHORTER physical
      # path - not a `subst` alias, which setuptools' os.path.realpath()
      # canonicalises straight back to the long physical path.
      #
      # So move the whole checkout out of the doubled-name workspace into
      # C:\pt. Same-volume `move` is an atomic rename (no per-file MAX_PATH
      # traversal), pytorch's submodule .git links are relative so they stay
      # valid, and win-test.sh derives PROJECT_DIR/TMP_DIR/TEST_DIR purely
      # from $PWD (it never reads $GITHUB_WORKSPACE), so running the harness
      # from C:\pt shortens every downstream object/dep path for real. C:\pt
      # lives outside the workspace, so clear any leftover from a previous job
      # on this persistent runner first (robocopy /MIR empties deep trees
      # without itself hitting MAX_PATH).
      - name: Relocate pytorch checkout to a short path (MAX_PATH mitigation)
        shell: cmd
        run: |
          if exist "%PT_ROOT%" (
            mkdir "%PT_ROOT%_empty" 2>nul
            robocopy "%PT_ROOT%_empty" "%PT_ROOT%" /MIR /NFL /NDL /NJH /NJS /NP >nul
            rmdir /s /q "%PT_ROOT%"
            rmdir /s /q "%PT_ROOT%_empty"
          )
          move "%GITHUB_WORKSPACE%\pytorch" "%PT_ROOT%"
          if errorlevel 1 (
            echo ::error::Failed to relocate pytorch checkout to %PT_ROOT%
            exit /b 1
          )
          echo Relocated pytorch checkout to %PT_ROOT%

      - name: Record pytorch HEAD (SHA + commit date)
        id: head
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ env.PT_ROOT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          date_iso=$(git log -1 --format=%cI HEAD)
          # Force UTC so the YYYYMMDD matches the wheel's `devYYYYMMDD` tag,
          # which pytorch CI mints from the UTC build date.
          date_ymd=$(TZ=UTC git log -1 --date=format-local:%Y%m%d --format=%cd HEAD)
          {
            echo "## pytorch checkout"
            echo ""
            echo "| field      | value |"
            echo "| ---        | --- |"
            echo "| input ref  | \`${{ steps.ref.outputs.ref }}\` |"
            echo "| HEAD sha   | \`$sha\` |"
            echo "| committed  | \`$date_iso\` |"
            echo "| dev tag    | \`dev$date_ymd\` |"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "date_ymd=$date_ymd" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "pytorch HEAD: $sha @ $date_iso (dev$date_ymd)"

      - name: Resolve nightly wheel URL for this cell
        if: inputs.wheel-artifact == ''
        id: wheel
        shell: bash
        env:
          CUDA_LABEL: ${{ inputs.cuda-label }}
          PY_VERSION: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
          WHEEL_INDEX_URL: ${{ inputs.wheel-index-url }}
          HEAD_DATE: ${{ steps.head.outputs.date_ymd }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # TODO: Add a sleep timer to check & pull the wheel with max timeout of 6 hours
          py_short="${PY_VERSION//./}"
          # PEP 503 simple-index hrefs encode '+' as '%2B':
          #   torch-<ver>.dev<YYYYMMDD>%2B<cu>-cp<py>-cp<py>-win_amd64.whl
          pattern="torch-[^/\"]+\.dev${HEAD_DATE}%2B${CUDA_LABEL}-cp${py_short}-cp${py_short}-win_amd64\.whl"
          url=$(curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 120 "$WHEEL_INDEX_URL" \
            | grep -oE 'href="[^"]+"' \
            | sed -E 's/^href="(.+)"$/\1/' \
            | grep -E "${pattern}(#|$)" \
            | head -n1 || true)
          # download.pytorch.org's simple index always emits absolute hrefs,
          # so no path normalisation is needed - just strip the PEP 503
          # `#sha256=...` fragment.
          url="${url%%#*}"
          if [ -z "$url" ]; then
            echo "::error::No nightly wheel for date=${HEAD_DATE} cuda=${CUDA_LABEL} cp=${py_short} at ${WHEEL_INDEX_URL}. The wheel for the checked-out pytorch commit is not yet published." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Resolved wheel: $url"

      - name: Install PyTorch
        shell: bash
        env:
          WHEEL_URL: ${{ steps.wheel.outputs.url }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$WHEEL_URL" ]; then
            echo "pip install $WHEEL_URL"
            python -m pip install "$WHEEL_URL"
          else
            wheel=$(ls -1 artifact/*.whl | head -n1)
            echo "pip install $wheel"
            python -m pip install "$wheel"
          fi
          python -c "import torch; print('torch', torch.__version__, 'cuda', torch.version.cuda); assert torch.cuda.is_available()"

      # pytorch's setup_pytorch_env.bat (called from win-test.sh, deep inside
      # the single test step below) installs .ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt
      # and then IGNORES the exit code. pip resolves a requirements file
      # atomically, so one unavailable pin takes the whole set down with it:
      # a transient index failure on `onnx==1.21.0` left expecttest, numpy
      # and hypothesis uninstalled, and the shard then died ~400 log lines
      # later on `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'expecttest'` - a
      # symptom that points nowhere near the cause.
      #
      # So install the same requirements here first, with real retries. The
      # nested install afterwards becomes a fast "already satisfied" no-op,
      # and even if it does hiccup the environment is already complete.
      #
      # Deliberately NOT gated on pip's exit code: this Linux-oriented
      # requirements file may legitimately fail on a package with no
      # win_amd64 wheel, which must not fail the shard. The import check
      # below is the real gate - it fails fast, and names what is missing.
      - name: Install test-harness dependencies (retried)
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ env.PT_ROOT }}
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            echo "--- requirements-ci.txt install, attempt ${attempt}"
            if python -m pip install -r .ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "${attempt}" -lt 3 ]; then
              delay=$((attempt * 30))
              echo "::warning::requirements-ci.txt install attempt ${attempt} failed; retrying in ${delay}s."
              sleep "${delay}"
            fi
          done

          # Not in requirements-ci.txt, but PYTEST_ADDOPTS below passes
          # --timeout to every pytest invocation, and an unrecognised
          # argument would fail every single test file. So this install is
          # load-bearing and the import check must cover it.
          python -m pip install "pytest-timeout==2.3.1"

          python - <<'PY'
          import importlib.util
          import sys

          # Modules that run_test.py / common_utils.py import before they can
          # report anything useful themselves. Scoped to what
          # requirements-ci.txt actually pins - pytest-shard and nvidia-ml-py
          # come from win-test.sh's own pip line, which has not run yet -
          # plus pytest_timeout, installed just above.
          required = ("expecttest", "numpy", "hypothesis", "psutil", "pytest", "pytest_timeout")
          missing = [m for m in required if importlib.util.find_spec(m) is None]
          if missing:
              print(
                  "::error::Test harness dependencies missing after 3 install attempts: "
                  + ", ".join(missing)
                  + ". The requirements-ci.txt resolve failed (usually a transient index "
                  "error on an unrelated pin) - re-run the shard.",
                  file=sys.stderr,
              )
              sys.exit(1)
          print("test-harness imports present:", ", ".join(required))
          PY

      # Seed our own test-time stats into pytorch's .additional_ci_files so
      # run_test.py shards deterministically from data we control instead of
      # downloading test-infra stats (or falling back to round-robin). All 5
      # shards read the same committed JSON, so the sharding is consistent.
      #
      # A file with no recorded time is also placed badly, not just costed
      # badly: calculate_shards gives up on cost entirely for it and hands it
      # out by index (`_get_min_sharded_job` round-robins when `test.time is
      # None`). So the script backfills a time for every test file in the
      # checkout, and prints how many it had to invent - a number that climbing
      # steadily is the signal to regenerate the committed stats
      # (docs/ci-details.md).
      #
      # A recorded time is also what arms run_test.py's own 30min per-file
      # subprocess timeout - but do not count on that bound, because it cannot
      # kill anything on Windows. See the watchdog comment below.
      - name: Seed test-time stats (deterministic sharding)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/oot/scripts/test-stats/seed_test_stats.py" \
            --pytorch-root "${{ env.PT_ROOT }}"

      - name: Start runner diagnostics
        id: diag
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/start-runner-diagnostics

      - name: Run PyTorch Windows test suite
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ env.PT_ROOT }}
        env:
          # ---- sharding (consumed by .ci/pytorch/win-test.sh -> test/run_test.py)
          SHARD_NUMBER: ${{ matrix.shard }}
          NUM_TEST_SHARDS: "5"
          TEST_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.test-config }}
          # ---- where the wheel lives on this runner (path A) or
          # ----   a placeholder dir for path B (pip-index install
          # ----   already happened in `Install PyTorch`).
          PYTORCH_FINAL_PACKAGE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/artifact
          # ---- GH context useful for log correlation + stats hooks
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.client_payload.pr_number || '' }}
          SHA1: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.event.client_payload.head_sha || github.sha }}
          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
          GITHUB_WORKFLOW: ${{ github.workflow }}
          GITHUB_JOB: ${{ github.job }}
          GITHUB_RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}
          # ---- per-test hang guard. run_test.py hands every test file to
          # ---- pytest, and pytest reads PYTEST_ADDOPTS itself, so this
          # ---- reaches all of them without patching upstream's args. The
          # ---- `thread` method is the only one that works on Windows
          # ---- (signal-based alarms are POSIX-only); it dumps all thread
          # ---- stacks and then hard-exits the process, which is what lets
          # ---- run_test.py record the file as failed and move on instead
          # ---- of blocking its worker pool forever.
          PYTEST_ADDOPTS: "--timeout=${{ env.PER_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC }} --timeout-method=thread"
          # ---- per-process hang guard, covering the phases pytest-timeout
          # ---- cannot see: import, collection, and everything after the last
          # ---- test while the interpreter and CUDA context tear down. Two of
          # ---- the shards lost to a hang froze in exactly those phases. This
          # ---- directory holds nothing but sitecustomize.py, which `site`
          # ---- imports at interpreter startup; it arms only in processes whose
          # ---- argv[0] is a test file, so run_test.py itself is never bounded.
          # ---- See scripts/test-bounds/pythonpath/sitecustomize.py.
          # PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SEC and PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_LOG are both
          # job-level, so they are already in this step's environment; only
          # PYTHONPATH needs setting, and it is scoped to this step so no other
          # step's python sees it.
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/oot/scripts/test-bounds/pythonpath
        # Tee the harness output into the test-reports tree so the summary
        # parser can recover failures that never make it into JUnit XML
        # (hard crashes, collection/import errors, whole-file aborts). The
        # log rides along in the uploaded test-reports artifact too.
        # `pipefail` keeps the test step's real exit code despite the pipe.
        #
        # `test-reports/` must be created up front: win-test.sh / run_test.py
        # only create it once tests start, so without this mkdir `tee` fails
        # with "No such file or directory", silently writes nothing, and the
        # parent run_test.py output (including the `<file> N/M failed!`
        # markers and the final failed-tests summary) never reaches the
        # scanned/uploaded tree - making whole-file failures invisible to the
        # summary even though the job correctly goes red.
        #
        # The checkout was relocated to C:\pt (see "Relocate pytorch checkout")
        # so this working directory - and every object/dep path win-test.sh
        # derives from $PWD - stays well under MAX_PATH. No subst/drive aliasing
        # is needed (and would not work: setuptools' realpath() canonicalises
        # aliases back to the long physical path).
        #
        # Backstop watchdog. Seven shards across four runs were lost to the job
        # cap, every one the same way: a single CUDA test deadlocked
        # (TestMemPool::test_graph_capture_pre_capture_stream_use in test_cuda,
        # _foreach_minimum and max_unpool1d in test_meta), its file never
        # returned to run_test.py's pool, the parent blocked in pool.join(), and
        # the orphaned process tree held this step's stdout pipe open so the
        # step could not even end. GitHub cancelled 70-120 minutes later with no
        # failure recorded and no stack: the parent sits in Process.join() ->
        # WaitForSingleObject(INFINITE), which on Windows ignores Ctrl-C, so
        # only the idle pool workers ever printed a traceback.
        #
        # Nothing bounded any of it. run_test.py does arm a 30min timeout on the
        # subprocess it runs each file in, but only when it knows that file's
        # expected duration (`test_module.time is not None`) - and the seeded
        # stats were empty, so it knew none of them.
        #
        # Supplying times re-arms that bound, but it is inert on Windows and
        # must not be relied on. This is an upstream defect in pytorch, not
        # something we configure: torch.testing._internal.common_utils's
        # wait_for_process handles its own timeout with
        # `p.send_signal(signal.SIGINT)` ("send SIGINT to give pytest a chance
        # to make xml" - sound on POSIX), and the function carries no platform
        # branch at all. Popen.send_signal on Windows accepts only SIGTERM /
        # CTRL_C_EVENT / CTRL_BREAK_EVENT, so SIGINT (2) raises ValueError. That
        # escapes before the `p.kill()` below it, and the handler's
        # `finally: p.wait()` then waits forever on a child that is still
        # running - turning a hung child into a permanently blocked parent,
        # which is the exact symptom above. Nothing we can set fixes it from
        # outside; it needs a patch upstream (or to the installed torch).
        # Confirmed by absence: retry_shell's "Command took >Nmin, returning
        # 124" does not appear in any of the ~9800 shard logs collected so far.
        # The bound is also armed only for the serial pytest invocation, since
        # `should_retry` is false once `-n` is in the command.
        #
        # Three bounds do work, because none of them needs a signal.
        # PYTEST_ADDOPTS above caps a single test at 15min: its timer thread
        # runs inside the child, dumps every thread's stack and hard-exits, so
        # run_test.py sees an ordinary exit code, records the failure and
        # carries on. PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SEC caps the whole test-file process
        # at 45min from inside it, which is what covers the phases
        # pytest-timeout cannot see - import, collection, and teardown after
        # the last test - at the cost of one file rather than the shard. And
        # this watchdog, which uses taskkill.
        #
        # So this watchdog is now the last resort proper: a hang in
        # run_test.py's own process, or in a non-python step, where nothing
        # inside a test-file interpreter can help.
        #
        # Killing python.exe rather than just the win-test.sh child is
        # deliberate: the grandchildren hold the write end of the pipe into
        # `tee`, so killing only the shell would leave `tee` blocked and the
        # step hung anyway. Killing repeatedly is deliberate too - win-test.sh
        # is a long sequence of python invocations and a single sweep can
        # leave it limping on to the next one instead of unwinding.
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          mkdir -p test/test-reports

          # sitecustomize.py stays silent when it arms - it is imported by every
          # python process in the job, so announcing itself there would be
          # hundreds of lines per shard. State it once here instead, and prove
          # the file is actually on the path rather than merely configured.
          if [ -f "${PYTHONPATH}/sitecustomize.py" ]; then
            echo "per-process bound: ${PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SEC}s, armed from ${PYTHONPATH}/sitecustomize.py"
          else
            echo "::warning::per-process bound NOT armed - no sitecustomize.py under '${PYTHONPATH}'. A hang outside a running test will now cost the whole shard."
          fi

          watchdog_marker="${RUNNER_TEMP}/win-test-watchdog-fired"
          rm -f "$watchdog_marker"
          (
            sleep "${RUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC}"
            : > "$watchdog_marker"
            echo "::error::Watchdog: win-test.sh made no progress within ${RUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC}s; killing test processes so the shard fails cleanly."
            while true; do
              taskkill //F //T //IM python.exe >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
              sleep 20
            done
          ) &
          watchdog_pid=$!

          # AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED stops the doomed S3 telemetry upload from
          # stalling, but it still runs and still narrates itself once per test
          # file. That was 1010 lines - 2.2% of the output - in a measured shard
          # log, for work that cannot ever succeed, so drop just those lines.
          # Matching is fixed-string and pins the "Unable to locate credentials"
          # reason, so an upload failing for any other reason is still printed
          # rather than swallowed.
          #
          # `set +e` around the pipeline so a red shard still reaches the
          # watchdog teardown below. PIPESTATUS[0] is win-test.sh's own exit
          # code, unmasked by the later stages. `--line-buffered` keeps the live
          # job log streaming instead of arriving in grep-sized blocks.
          set +e
          bash .ci/pytorch/win-test.sh 2>&1 \
            | grep -v --line-buffered -F \
                -e 'Failed to parse and upload json test reports: Unable to locate credentials' \
                -e 'Parsing testcases for test report:' \
                -e 'Found job id:' \
                -e 'GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT, or ARTIFACTS_FILE_SUFFIX not set, not uploading' \
                -e 'Uploading artifacts took' \
                -e 'SCRIBE_GRAPHQL_ACCESS_TOKEN is NOT set' \
            | tee "test/test-reports/run_test_shard${SHARD_NUMBER}.log"
          rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          set -e

          kill "$watchdog_pid" 2>/dev/null || true

          if [ -f "$watchdog_marker" ]; then
            echo "::error::Shard timed out after ${RUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC}s. The tail of the log above is where it stopped making progress."
            exit 1
          fi
          exit "$rc"

      # Close the loop on the per-process bound. Without this the only thing a
      # healthy shard proves is that sitecustomize.py was on PYTHONPATH at step
      # start - not that any test process actually imported and armed it. Reads
      # the records the processes appended and states both counts.
      #
      # Read-only and never fails the shard: it reports on a guard, and a
      # broken report is not worth converting into a red shard. A zero count is
      # a warning rather than an error for the same reason - it means the bound
      # was inert, which is worth shouting about but is not itself a test
      # failure. Hence `-u` off and `:-` on the read: the first version of this
      # step had the path step-scoped to the test step and died on `unbound
      # variable` in all 20 shards, before printing anything.
      - name: Report per-process bound coverage
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          rec="${PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_LOG:-}"
          if [ -z "$rec" ] || [ ! -f "$rec" ]; then
            echo "::warning::No per-process bound records at '$rec'. Either no test file ran, or sitecustomize.py was never imported - in which case a hang outside a running test would cost the whole shard."
            exit 0
          fi
          armed=$(grep -c '"event": "armed"' "$rec" || true)
          fired=$(grep -c '"event": "fired"' "$rec" || true)
          echo "per-process bound: armed in ${armed} test-file process(es), fired ${fired} time(s)"
          if [ "${armed:-0}" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::warning::per-process bound recorded no armed process; treat the bound as inert for this shard."
          fi
          if [ "${fired:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "The bound killed these process(es) - each one is a test file that hung outside a running test:"
            grep '"event": "fired"' "$rec" || true
          fi
          exit 0

      # The output-dir guard doubles as an "OOT tree is present" check: when
      # the monitor never started there is no local action to run either, and
      # attempting it only adds a bogus "Can't find action.yml" error on top
      # of the real failure.
      - name: Stop runner diagnostics
        if: always() && steps.diag.outputs.output-dir != ''
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/stop-runner-diagnostics
        with:
          output-dir: ${{ steps.diag.outputs.output-dir }}

      # Parse this shard's JUnit reports and render the failing test names
      # straight into the shard's own step summary. Read-only and best-
      # effort: it never changes the shard's pass/fail status (the test
      # step above already owns that), so it runs even when the test step
      # errored. The orchestrator-level `test-summary` job aggregates which
      # cells/shards failed; this gives the per-shard test-name detail.
      - name: Summarize failed tests (this shard)
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          parser="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/oot/scripts/test-summary/parse_failures.py"
          # If the shard died before/inside the OOT checkout there is nothing
          # to parse with. Say so once instead of failing this step too and
          # burying the real error under a `can't open file` traceback.
          if [ ! -f "$parser" ]; then
            echo "::warning::$parser missing (OOT checkout did not complete); skipping shard summary."
            exit 0
          fi
          python "$parser" \
            --reports-dir "${{ env.PT_ROOT }}/test/test-reports" \
            --title "Failed tests - ${{ inputs.build-environment }} - ${{ inputs.python-label }}/${{ inputs.cuda-label }} - ${{ inputs.arch-name }} - shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/5" \
            >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Enabled deliberately, despite the build job's copy being disabled.
      # Diagnosing the seven lost shards meant reconstructing host state from
      # test logs alone, because these samples - ~12KB of memory, CPU and GPU
      # timeseries per shard - were the one artifact the test jobs never kept.
      # They are what distinguishes "one test deadlocked" from "the box was
      # thrashing", and the answer changes the fix.
      - name: Upload runner diagnostics
        if: always() && steps.diag.outputs.output-dir != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: runner-diagnostics-${{ inputs.build-environment }}-${{ inputs.python-label }}-${{ inputs.cuda-label }}-shard${{ matrix.shard }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ steps.diag.outputs.output-dir }}/**
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

      # Archive the raw test-reports tree (JUnit XML plus any crash / log
      # files the harness drops there). upload-artifact stores the folder and
      # serves it as a single `<name>.zip` on download. The name is unique
      # per cell+shard+run+attempt so the 5 parallel shards never collide
      # (v4 and later forbid two jobs uploading the same artifact name).
      - name: Upload test-reports archive
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: test-reports-${{ inputs.build-environment }}-${{ inputs.python-label }}-${{ inputs.cuda-label }}-${{ inputs.arch-name }}-shard${{ matrix.shard }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ env.PT_ROOT }}/test/test-reports/**
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

# PyTorch OOT Windows CI — Architecture & Reference

Detailed reference for the workflows in this repository. For a high-level
overview and quick start, see the top-level [README](../README.md).

This repository provides NVIDIA PyTorch out-of-tree (OOT) CI on
self-hosted **Windows + NVIDIA RTX** (x86-64) and **Windows-on-Arm**
(arm64) runners. The workflows here implement
the downstream half of [RFC-0050: Cross-Repository CI Relay for PyTorch
Out-of-Tree Backends](https://github.com/pytorch/rfcs/blob/master/RFC-0050-Cross-Repository-CI-Relay-for-PyTorch-Out-of-Tree-Backends.md)
and mirror the in-tree shape of `pytorch/pytorch` PR
[#176678 - \[CI\]\[Windows\] Add NVIDIA RTX workflow](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/176678).
Upstream covers a single configuration (Python 3.12, CUDA 12.8); this
repository expands the matrix so it can catch regressions
across multiple Python and CUDA toolkit combinations before they show up
upstream. Build/test logic itself comes entirely from PyTorch's in-tree
`.ci/pytorch/*.sh` scripts; this repo holds only the workflow wiring.

Build and test jobs run on self-hosted runners provided by NVIDIA
infrastructure. The lightweight jobs — lint, prep/ref-resolution, and
test-summary — run on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`.

## Windows-on-Arm

Alongside the RTX x86_64 flow, `windows-woa-build-test.yml` drives the reusable
`_woa-build.yml` and `_woa-test.yml` workflows on the `woa-arm64` runner pool.
See the [WoA operator guide](woa-ci.md) and
[WoA design and runner contract](woa-ci-plan.md) for the matrix, preinstalled
toolchain, persistent-runner cleanup, and operational details.

## Triggering workflows

> **Nothing in this repo can be started by hand.** No workflow has a
> `workflow_dispatch` trigger: external-CI security guidelines do not allow a
> hand-started run to aim the self-hosted pools at an arbitrary upstream
> commit. A finished run can still be repeated with **Re-run jobs**, which
> re-resolves the same commit (see [HUD reporting](crcr-hud-reporting.md)).

There are three top-level workflows. Two of them run automatically on a
nightly `schedule`; the third is parked:

- **`windows-rtx-build-test.yml`** — full source build + test, nightly at
  `20 9 * * *` (14:50 IST).
- **`windows-woa-build-test.yml`** — WoA (arm64) source build + test, nightly
  at `50 9 * * *` (15:20 IST). It can also sign and publish the wheels it
  built, opt-in through `vars.WOA_NIGHTLY_PUBLISH`; see
  [WoA wheel signing and publication](woa-wheel-publishing.md).
- **`windows-rtx-wheel-test.yml`** — published-wheel test. Its nightly cron
  (`0 17 * * *` / 22:30 IST) is commented out and its only other trigger is a
  `workflow_call` that nothing calls, so it cannot currently start. Uncomment
  the cron to bring it back.

Both active schedules sit after `pytorch/pytorch` cuts the day's `nightly`
commit, which over the 57 days to 2026-09-09 landed between 07:35 and 08:47
UTC. This matters because `prep` resolves the newest nightly at or before the
run's start — a cron that fires earlier does not wait for the day's commit, it
builds, tests and reports the previous day's again.

The reusable workflows (`_rtx-build.yml`, `_rtx-test.yml`, `_woa-build.yml`,
`_woa-test.yml`, `_woa-pr-build-test.yml`, `_woa-sign-publish.yml` and the
`_woa-sign.yml` / `_woa-publish.yml` / `_woa-verify.yml` stages it calls) are
called by the orchestrators and are not run directly.

Separate from those three, **`upstream-pull.yml`** is driven by the upstream
relay rather than by anyone here: it validates a `pytorch/pytorch` pull request
whenever the relay dispatches one. Whether a given PR runs is decided by a
maintainer-controlled allowlist plus an explicit approval, after which it calls
a build/test pipeline per platform as a reusable workflow, pinned to the
approved commit — see
[per-PR CI: the allowlist and maintainer approval](per-pr-ci-triggering.md).
For RTX that is `windows-rtx-build-test.yml` itself, which is why it carries a
`workflow_call` trigger; it adds no way to start it by hand. For WoA it is
`_woa-pr-build-test.yml`, the nightly's build and test jobs without the
nightly's wheel publication, which a PR must never be able to reach.

## Workflows

| Workflow | Purpose | Triggers | Compute |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `windows-rtx-wheel-test.yml`           | Each test cell checks out `pytorch/pytorch` at `pytorch-ref` (default `nightly`) via `actions/checkout@v7` (which resolves the branch to a concrete commit), records the actual HEAD SHA + commit date into the cell's job summary, then greps `download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/torch/` for the wheel whose filename carries that exact `devYYYYMMDD` tag together with the matrix `cu<label>` / `cp<pyshort>` tags and `pip install`s the resolved absolute URL before running `.ci/pytorch/win-test.sh`. Fails fast if no matching wheel exists, so the wheel under test always shares its commit date with the pytorch source on disk. No preflight job, no artifact transit. | Parked: `workflow_call` only (nothing calls it); the nightly cron is commented out | `_rtx-test.yml` (sm89 + sm120 in one matrix) |
| `windows-rtx-build-test.yml`            | Full source build (multi-arch wheel) + test. A PR run, called by `upstream-pull.yml`, is pinned to the approved head SHA and may narrow the matrix via subset filters. | `schedule` (`20 9 * * *` = 14:50 IST), `workflow_call` (from `upstream-pull.yml`); no manual trigger | `prep` -> `_rtx-build.yml` -> `_rtx-test.yml` (sm89 + sm120 in one matrix); `report-*-crcr` |
| `windows-woa-build-test.yml` | Builds and tests the WoA wheel matrix from source on the shared arm64 pool, and can sign and publish the wheels it built (opt-in; see [WoA wheel signing and publication](woa-wheel-publishing.md)). PR runs use `_woa-pr-build-test.yml`, the same build and test jobs without publication or HUD reporting. | `schedule` (`50 9 * * *` = 15:20 IST); no manual trigger | `prep` -> `_woa-build.yml` -> `_woa-test.yml` -> `test-summary`; `publication` -> `_woa-sign-publish.yml`; `report-*-crcr` |

Both build/test orchestrators end in two terminal `report-*-crcr` jobs that
publish the nightly's results to the upstream PyTorch HUD. They hang off the
matrix rather than feeding it, so a reporting failure can never skip a build or
a test. See [HUD reporting](crcr-hud-reporting.md) for the row names, how a
conclusion is decided, and why re-runs must resolve the same upstream SHA.

Both RTX workflows fan out across `(config)` for builds and
`(config x arch)` for tests. **Sharding is not a top-level axis on
either orchestrator** - it lives inside `_rtx-test.yml`'s own
`strategy.matrix.shard`, so one call to the reusable workflow ==
one `(config, arch)` test cell, and each call internally spawns the
5 shard runners nested underneath it. This matches upstream
`_win-rtx-test.yml` (PR #176678) where the `test-matrix` JSON drives
sharding inside the reusable workflow rather than on the caller.

`config` is a paired `{python, cuda}` entry rather than independent
`python` and `cuda` axes, because the runner pool is allocated per
(python, cuda) combination - py312/cu130 and py312/cu132 are
different machines, so the matrix enumerates the actual pairings
rather than blindly cross-multiplying.

Cell names mirror `pytorch/pytorch`'s generated
`windows-binary-wheel` nightly (`wheel-py3_10-cuda13_0-build` /
`wheel-py3_10-cuda13_0-test`). Each `config:` entry carries a
precomputed `build_name` (`wheel-py312-cu130`, etc.) so the
job-level `name:` collapses to a one-token reference exactly like
upstream's `name: ${{ matrix.build_name }}-build`:

| Job | Cell name template | Example cell |
| --- | --- | --- |
| orchestrator `build`            | `<build_name>-build`        | `wheel-py312-cu130-build` |
| orchestrator `test`             | `<build_name>-<arch>-test`  | `wheel-py312-cu130-sm89-test` |
| `_rtx-test.yml`'s inner shards  | `test (shard <N>/5)`        | nested under each `*-test` cell |

GitHub groups matrix cells alphabetically by name, so leading with
`wheel-<py>-<cu>` keeps each wheel's two arch fanouts adjacent and
also lines up a wheel-test row alongside its windows-rtx-build-test
counterpart in cross-workflow dashboards.

`.ci/pytorch/win-test.sh` (via `test/run_test.py`) honours the
`SHARD_NUMBER` / `NUM_TEST_SHARDS` / `TEST_CONFIG` env vars set
inside `_rtx-test.yml` to run just its slice.

```
windows-rtx-build-test.yml:                          windows-rtx-wheel-test.yml:

  build  matrix( config )                         (no preflight job)
      |   (3 cells)                                test  matrix( config x arch )
      |   multi-arch wheel + SHA sidecar                  (3 x 2 = 6 cells)
      |   uploaded as one artifact per cell
      |                                                  each cell calls
      +-> test  matrix( config x arch )                  _rtx-test.yml, which
                (3 x 2 = 6 cells)                        internally fans out
                  each cell calls _rtx-test.yml,         5 shard runners.
                  which internally fans out 5
                  shard runners (30 runners total).      Inside each runner:
                                                           - checkout pytorch@nightly
                  Inside each runner:                      - grep public index for the
                    - pip install the build's wheel          matching devYYYYMMDD wheel
                      artifact                             - pip install URL
                    - run shard N of 5                     - run shard N of 5

UI grouping in both workflows (orchestrator level):
  wheel-py312-cu130-build                  (windows-rtx-build-test only)
  wheel-py312-cu130-sm89-test              ... drill in for 5 shard cells
  wheel-py312-cu130-sm120-test             ... drill in for 5 shard cells
  wheel-py312-cu132-build                  (windows-rtx-build-test only)
  wheel-py312-cu132-sm89-test
  ...
```

`_rtx-test.yml` accepts two install paths and routes between them based
on which inputs the orchestrator provided:

| Install path | When | Required inputs | Checkout ref from | Install source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **artifact** (path A) | source build | `wheel-artifact` | SHA in `built_pytorch_sha.txt` inside the artifact | `pip install ./artifact/*.whl` |
| **pip-index** (path B) | nightly wheel | `pytorch-ref` (+ optional `wheel-index-url`, default `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/torch/`) | `pytorch-ref` passed verbatim (typically `nightly`); `actions/checkout@v7` resolves it | Wheel URL grepped from the index by checked-out commit's `devYYYYMMDD` + matrix `cu<label>` / `cp<pyshort>` tags |

In both paths the test job records the actual `git rev-parse HEAD` +
commit date of the checkout into its Step Summary, so each cell logs
"what nightly did I test" without needing a centralized preflight.
This keeps `_rtx-build.yml` as the only producer that needs to ship a
wheel through GitHub artifact storage. The nightly path avoids the
fetch/upload/download round-trip entirely - the test runner that
resolves the ref is the same runner that pip-installs and tests.

The path-B resolver fails fast if the index has no wheel for the
checked-out commit's date - that is the signal that the nightly wheel
for the source just pulled is not yet published, and any install
would otherwise silently fall back to an older wheel that disagrees
with the source tree on disk.

## Default matrix

`config` (paired entries — each one corresponds to a real allocated
runner; add/remove entries to match the runner pool):

| python | cuda toolkit | python-label | cuda-label |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.12 | 13.0 | `py312` | `cu130` |
| 3.12 | 13.2 | `py312` | `cu132` |
| 3.13 | 13.2 | `py313` | `cu132` |

Plus `arch: [sm89, sm120]` on the orchestrator's test job, with the
5-shard fanout living inside `_rtx-test.yml`
(`strategy.matrix.shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`, `NUM_TEST_SHARDS: "5"`),
matching PR #176678.

Per source-build run that's **3 build jobs + 6 orchestrator-level
test cells** (3 configs x 2 archs); each test cell expands to 5
nested shard runners, so the actual runner count is `3 + 6 * 5 = 33`
GH Actions runner jobs. The wheel-test run is **6 orchestrator-
level test cells** (30 runners after the internal shard fanout) - no
preflight, no per-cell wheel producer.

`TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` is set per `arch` matrix entry (`8.9` for sm89,
`12.0` for sm120), and `runner-base` likewise (`rtx-40x0-test` vs
`rtx-50x0-test`). The build wheel itself is multi-arch (`8.9;12.0`) so
a single producer feeds both architectures.

## Runner model

Runners are **ephemeral, pre-prepped images**. The image has the right
Python, CUDA toolkit, MSVC build tools, sccache, magma, cmake, ninja, and
the standard PyTorch test runtime pre-installed and on `PATH`. The
workflows perform **zero** in-job environment setup. Each matrix cell is
routed to its image via the runner-label set:

| Job kind | Label set |
| --- | --- |
| `build` (source-build wheel producer)           | `[rtx-build, <python-label>, <cuda-label>]` |
| `test` cells where `matrix.arch.name == sm89`   | `[rtx-40x0-test, <python-label>, <cuda-label>]` |
| `test` cells where `matrix.arch.name == sm120`  | `[rtx-50x0-test, <python-label>, <cuda-label>]` |
| `inspect-dispatch` (parked RFC-0050 arm)        | `[rtx-build]` (any free build runner) |
| `prep`, `test-summary`, `lint`                  | `ubuntu-latest` (GitHub-hosted) |

The narrow labels (`rtx-build`, `rtx-40x0-test`, `rtx-50x0-test`,
`py3xx`, `cu1xx`) are unique to the self-hosted Windows pool, so the
GitHub auto-tags (`self-hosted`, `Windows`, `X64`) that the runner
agent applies are redundant in the AND filter and are deliberately
left off `runs-on:` everywhere.

For example, the sm120 test cell for Python 3.13 + CUDA 13.0 needs an
image registered as `[rtx-50x0-test, py313, cu130]` (plus whatever
auto-tags the runner agent adds).

## What the runner image must already contain

Because there is no in-job setup, the pre-prepped image carries everything the
PyTorch CI scripts (`.ci/pytorch/win-build.sh`, `.ci/pytorch/win-test.sh`,
`.ci/pytorch/win-test-helpers/**`) expect to find. Concretely:

- Python (matching matrix cell, on `PATH` as `python`)
- CUDA toolkit (matching matrix cell) and a recent enough GPU driver
- cuDNN, NCCL (where applicable) bundled with the toolkit
- Visual Studio Build Tools / MSVC (`cl.exe` reachable through `vcvarsall.bat`)
- Git for Windows (provides `bash`, `git`, `curl`)
- ninja, cmake, sccache, magma binaries
- All Python deps from `pytorch/.ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt` for the
  matching Python version (numba 0.64.0+, pytest, expecttest, hypothesis,
  numpy, ...; see `pytorch/pytorch` PR #176678 review thread for the
  current pin set)
- `nvidia-smi` on `PATH`
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the in-box `powershell.exe`) is sufficient
  for the runner-diagnostics composite actions. PowerShell 7+ (`pwsh`) is
  NOT required on the RTX pool - every script those actions invoke sticks
  to cmdlets and language features available in 5.1.

PyTorch's in-tree CI scripts cover build, install, and test end-to-end on
the RTX pool. The repo-local helpers around them are the runner-diagnostics
monitor described [below](#runner-diagnostics), the test-summary and
test-stats scripts, and the vendored WoA build/test library under
`tools/woa-build/`.

## Customising the matrix

The matrix work in each orchestrator lives in at most two jobs - `build`
and `test` (`windows-rtx-wheel-test.yml` has only `test`, since it
installs a published wheel instead of producing one). The surrounding
`prep`, `test-summary`, and `inspect-dispatch` jobs are single cells and
carry no matrix. The orchestrator's test matrix is 2-dimensional
(`config x arch`); the shard fanout lives one layer down in
`_rtx-test.yml`:

```yaml
# Orchestrator (windows-rtx-build-test.yml / windows-rtx-wheel-test.yml)
matrix:
  config:                      # paired {python, cuda} entries; each one
    - { python: { version: "3.12", label: "py312" },  #   corresponds to an actual allocated
        cuda:   { version: "13.0", label: "cu130" },  #   runner. Add/remove lines freely.
        build_name: "wheel-py312-cu130" }
    - { python: { version: "3.12", label: "py312" },
        cuda:   { version: "13.2", label: "cu132" },
        build_name: "wheel-py312-cu132" }
    # ... etc
  arch:                        # 2 entries, each carries runner-base
    - { name: sm89,  runner: rtx-40x0-test, arch_list: "8.9"  }
    - { name: sm120, runner: rtx-50x0-test, arch_list: "12.0" }

# _rtx-test.yml (reusable; one call per orchestrator test cell)
strategy:
  matrix:
    shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]     # 5 shards per (config, arch); NUM_TEST_SHARDS env is "5"
```

In `windows-rtx-build-test.yml`, the `config` list is declared on
the `build` job (`&config` anchor) and re-used on the `test` job
(`*config`). In `windows-rtx-wheel-test.yml` the list lives directly on
the `test` job since there is no build to share it with.

To add or remove cells:
- **config axis** (a python+cuda pairing): edit the `config:` list in
  one place per orchestrator. Each entry is `{ python: {version,
  label}, cuda: {version, label}, build_name: ... }`. Because the
  matrix enumerates only the pairings you put in, dropping an
  unsupported combination (say `py313` + `cu130` if no machine for it
  exists) is just a line delete - no `exclude:` clause needed.
- **arch axis**: edit the `arch:` list on the `test` job. Each entry
  is a `{ name, runner, arch_list }` triple - `runner` becomes the
  fourth runner label, `arch_list` becomes `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` for
  that cell.
- **shard count**: edit `_rtx-test.yml` in two places - the
  `strategy.matrix.shard` list and the `NUM_TEST_SHARDS` env literal.
  Orchestrators are agnostic to the shard count.
- **per-run matrix filters** (`workflow_call` only): both RTX
  orchestrators accept three comma-separated subset inputs from their
  caller and forward them verbatim via `with:` to the called reusable
  workflows (`_rtx-build.yml` / `_rtx-test.yml`), whose own job-level
  `if:` performs the match against the cell's own `python-version`,
  `cuda-version`, and `arch-name` inputs. The filter lives one layer
  down because GitHub Actions disallows `matrix.*` in the `if:` of a
  job that calls a reusable workflow. Scheduled runs always cover
  every cell (their inputs are empty, which disables the corresponding
  filter dimension in the reusable workflow), and `upstream-pull.yml`
  passes no filters today, so a PR run covers every cell as well.

  | Input | Filters |
  | --- | --- |
  | `python-versions`    | `build` + `test` (matches the cell's `python-version`) |
  | `cuda-versions`      | `build` + `test` (matches the cell's `cuda-version`)   |
  | `test-architectures` | `test` only (matches the cell's `arch-name`)           |

  Cells dropped by the filter show up in the GitHub UI with their
  inner reusable-workflow job in the "skipped" state, so a narrowed run
  that only covered py3.12 / cu13.0 still leaves an audit trail of
  every other slot as "this cell exists, was deliberately not
  exercised".

## Test environment variables

`_rtx-test.yml` exports the subset of PR #176678's test env block that
applies here (no AWS, no `filter-test-configs`,
no `get-workflow-job-id`):

| Scope | Variable | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| job  | `BUILD_ENVIRONMENT`, `PYTHON_VERSION`, `CUDA_VERSION`, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` | matrix cell |
| job  | `USE_CUDA=1`, `INSTALL_WINDOWS_SDK=0`, `CONTINUE_THROUGH_ERROR=1`, `PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=0`, `PYTORCH_TESTING_DEVICE_ONLY_FOR=cuda`, `CI=1` | static |
| job  | `VC_PRODUCT=BuildTools`, `VC_YEAR=2022`, `VS_VERSION=17.4.1`, `VC_VERSION=""` | MSVC tooling info |
| job  | `PIP_RETRIES=8`, `PIP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=60` | pip resilience for the test-harness install |
| job  | `PER_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC=900`, `PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SEC=2700`, `RUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC=9900` | the bounds that hold a hung shard - see [Timeout bounds](#timeout-bounds) |
| job  | `PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_LOG` | `test/test-reports/per-process-bound.jsonl`; unset disables the records |
| job  | `AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true` | suppresses a dead S3 telemetry probe - see below |
| step | `SHARD_NUMBER` | `_rtx-test.yml`'s internal `matrix.shard` |
| step | `NUM_TEST_SHARDS` | static (`"5"`, matches the shard list length) |
| step | `TEST_CONFIG` | `inputs.test-config` (default `"default"`) |
| step | `PYTORCH_FINAL_PACKAGE_DIR` | `${{ github.workspace }}/artifact` |
| step | `PYTHONPATH` | `scripts/test-bounds/pythonpath`, so `site` picks up our `sitecustomize.py` |
| step | `PR_NUMBER`, `SHA1` | `repository_dispatch` payload or PR context |
| step | `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` / `_WORKFLOW` / `_JOB` / `_RUN_ID` / `_RUN_NUMBER` / `_RUN_ATTEMPT` | `github.*` context |

`AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED` is there because `run_test.py` tries to upload each
batch of test reports to pytorch's S3 bucket. There are no credentials on these
runners, so the upload cannot succeed and does not need to - nothing reads it.
But `boto3`, finding no credentials, next asks the EC2 instance metadata
service for them, and on a host that is not an EC2 instance there is nothing
listening on `169.254.169.254` to refuse the connection. It waits for the
connect to time out instead, once per batch. Setting this makes `boto3` skip
that probe and give up at once. The test step also filters the resulting
`Failed to parse and upload json test reports: Unable to locate credentials`
line out of the log, since the upload is expected to fail.

## Test sharding

`test/run_test.py` assigns test files to the 5 shards itself, using per-file
timings it reads from `<pytorch>/.additional_ci_files/test-times.json`. Upstream
that file is downloaded from test-infra, which has no data for an out-of-tree
build env - hence the benign warning every shard logs:

```
Gathered no stats from artifacts for win-rtx-sm89 build env and default
test config. Using default job name and default test config instead.
```

The fallback to `default`/`default` is the intended path here: the
`Seed test-time stats` step runs `scripts/test-stats/seed_test_stats.py`, which
copies our committed `scripts/test-stats/data/*.json` into that folder under
exactly those keys. Every shard reads the same committed JSON, so all 5 agree on
the split without coordinating.

Timings do two things beyond balance. `calculate_shards` bin-packs by cost only
for a file whose time is known; an unknown file falls back to round-robin
(`_get_min_sharded_job` in `tools/testing/test_selections.py`), which ignores
cost. And any file over the 10-minute `THRESHOLD` is split into
`ceil(duration / 600)` pytest shards spread across jobs, so `test_meta` runs as
15 pieces of ~9.5 min rather than one atomic 2.4-hour file.

So that no file drops out of cost-based packing, `seed_test_stats.py` backfills
an entry for every `test_*.py` in the checkout that our data has never measured,
at the median of the times we do have. `--no-backfill` disables the backfill.
Each run states the outcome:

```
sharding coverage: 1271 test file(s) in the checkout, 633 backfilled at 15.6s,
0 left without a time
```

The last number should always be `0`. The middle one counts the whole `test/`
tree, most of which this CI never selects, so it is a poor drift signal - for
that, compare the files a run actually executed against the committed data.

### Timeout bounds

Four bounds apply to an x86 test shard, at descending granularity. The arm64
shards carry the same set at different values, and take their per-test and
per-shard bounds from the vendored harness rather than from the workflow - see
[WoA timeout bounds](woa-ci.md#timeout-bounds).

| Bound | Where | Value | On expiry |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| per test | `PYTEST_ADDOPTS=--timeout=... --timeout-method=thread` | 15 min | fails that test; the shard carries on |
| per test-file process | `PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SEC`, armed by `scripts/test-bounds/pythonpath/sitecustomize.py` | 45 min | dumps all thread stacks, kills that file's process tree; the shard carries on |
| per test file | `run_test.py`'s own subprocess timeout (`THRESHOLD * 3`) | 30 min | **nothing - inert on Windows, see below** |
| per shard | in-step watchdog (`RUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC`) | 165 min | `taskkill`s the test processes and fails the shard |

Do not rely on the per-file bound. It is armed only when `run_test.py` knows the
file's expected duration and only for the serial pytest invocation, and on
Windows it cannot kill anything even then: its expiry path calls
`Popen.send_signal(signal.SIGINT)`, which Windows rejects with `ValueError`
before reaching the `p.kill()` below it, leaving the handler blocked in
`finally: p.wait()` on a live child. That turns a timeout into a permanent hang.
It is an upstream pytorch defect with no environment-variable workaround, so
treat the bound as absent.

`PYTEST_ADDOPTS` only covers a test that is running, so the per-process bound is
what covers the rest of a test file's life:

| Window | per test | per process | per file | per shard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| inside a test (setup, call, teardown) | yes | yes | inert | yes |
| import and collection, before the first test | no | yes | inert | yes |
| session teardown, interpreter exit, CUDA context destruction | no | yes | inert | yes |
| between the serial and parallel invocations | n/a | yes | inert | yes |
| in `run_test.py` itself, or a non-Python step | no | no | no | yes |

The per-process bound lives in a `sitecustomize.py`, which `site` imports at
interpreter startup - hence the coverage of import, collection and teardown. It
is on `PYTHONPATH` in the test step only, and arms only in a process whose
`argv[0]` is a `test_*.py` file, so `run_test.py` itself is never bounded. Each
shard logs `per-process bound: <n>s, armed from <path>` once, or a `::warning::`
if the file is not on the path. Setting `PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SEC` to `0` or
leaving it unset disables it.

Because the bound is silent while armed, a run in which nothing hangs cannot
otherwise be told apart from one where the module was never imported. So each
armed process appends a line to `PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_LOG`, and a second one if
it fires; the `Report per-process bound coverage` step turns those into
`per-process bound: armed in <n> test-file process(es), fired <m> time(s)` and
warns if `<n>` is `0`. The file rides along in the `test-reports` artifact. It
is `.jsonl` rather than `.log` because `parse_failures.py` scans that tree for
`*.log` / `*.txt` when hunting failures.

Both bounds are sized from measured runs. `RUN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC` is 165 min
against a slowest clean shard of 106 min and a slowest guarded one of 112 min.
`PER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SEC` is 45 min against a slowest single invocation of
26.6 min - compare it per *invocation*, not per file, since `run_test.py` runs
each file twice and pytest-shards the big ones, so a file's total can exceed it
legitimately (`test_meta` totals ~142 min).

### Refreshing the stats

The data is a snapshot and drifts as the upstream suite changes. Drift costs
balance, not safety - an unmeasured file is backfilled, so it is still packed on
cost, just from a guess rather than a measurement. To regenerate from a
completed run:

1. Download each shard's log for one `(config, arch)` cell - either
   `gh api repos/NVIDIA/pytorch-windows-ci/actions/jobs/<job-id>/logs`, or the
   `run_test_shard<N>.log` inside that shard's `test-reports-*` artifact.
2. Optionally extract the `test-reports-*` artifacts too; they are the only
   source of per-class times.
3. Run the generator, passing **every** shard of the run so that pytest-sharded
   files are seen whole:

```bash
python scripts/test-stats/gen_test_stats.py \
  --log-dir ./logs --report-dir ./reports/shard1 ... --report-dir ./reports/shard5
```

4. Commit the regenerated `scripts/test-stats/data/*.json`.

Use a run whose shards all completed: a cancelled shard truncates its log, and
the generator can only scale a partially-observed file back up to an estimate.

## Runner diagnostics

Each test job spawns `scripts/runner-diagnostics/monitor.ps1` (resolved
by `start-runner-diagnostics` from `$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH`) in the
background while
`.ci/pytorch/win-test.sh` runs in the foreground. It writes one
artifact per cell, `runner-diagnostics-<env>-<py>-<cu>-<run_id>-<attempt>`,
14-day retention, containing:

```
spec-snapshot.json   host / CPU / RAM / disk / driver / GPU / Python / nvcc
system.jsonl         CPU %, mem MiB, disk free / used GB, top 5 procs by WS
gpu.jsonl            per-GPU util, mem, temp, power, SM / mem clocks
monitor.log          start / stop bookends + sample count
```

Pipe the JSONL files through `jq` / `pandas` to plot pressure around a
failure. To tune the interval or relocate the output dir, edit the
`with:` block in `_rtx-test.yml` (`start-runner-diagnostics` accepts
`interval-seconds` and `output-dir` inputs).

## Test summaries

The RTX and WoA orchestrators run a final `test-summary` job on
`ubuntu-latest` after all test cells settle. It uses
`scripts/test-summary/aggregate_failures.py` to summarize failed jobs and
`scripts/test-summary/parse_failures.py` to combine failures from downloaded
shard reports. The summary job is informational; the individual test jobs
remain responsible for the workflow result.

## RFC-0050 mapping

| RFC concept | This repo |
| --- | --- |
| Downstream CI on real PR-time events | `upstream-pull.yml` subscribes to `repository_dispatch` (`pull_request`, plus the legacy `pytorch-pr-trigger`). An allowlisted author's PR waits for a maintainer's approval, then `windows-rtx-build-test.yml` and `_woa-pr-build-test.yml` are called pinned to the approved head SHA; see [per-PR CI](per-pr-ci-triggering.md). |
| `concurrency: upstream-pr-<pr_number>` | `upstream-pull.yml` keys `concurrency.group` on the PR number with `cancel-in-progress`, so a newer push to a PR cancels its older run |
| `pytorch/actions/checkout-pr@v1` (RFC Action #1) | Not used. `_rtx-build.yml` checks out `pytorch/pytorch` at the resolved SHA with `actions/checkout@v7` alone; a fork PR's head is fetchable by SHA from `pytorch/pytorch` |
| `pytorch/actions/report-ci-result@v1` (RFC Action #2) | Not yet wired — result acknowledgement is pending publication of the upstream action |

## Local workflow validation

```bash
python -m pip install "PyYAML>=6" "check-jsonschema>=0.29"
check-jsonschema --builtin-schema vendor.github-workflows .github/workflows/*.yml
```

The same checks run automatically in `lint.yml` on every PR.
