name: _rtx-build

# Reusable Windows RTX build workflow. Mirrors the role of
# pytorch/pytorch's `_win-build.yml` (see PR #176678) but kept standalone
# in this repo so it works before that PR lands upstream. The actual
# build is driven by THIS repo's `tools/pytorch-build/win-build.sh` flow
# (an upstream-faithful, no-S3 replica of `.ci/pytorch/win-build.sh`).
#
# Each invocation builds ONE multi-architecture CUDA wheel (one wheel that
# serves sm89, sm120, ... whatever `cuda-arch-list` covers). The caller
# drives Python and CUDA toolkit variations via its own matrix and passes
# the cell's values in as `python-{version,label}` and `cuda-{version,label}`.
#
# Every caller gets the same checkout: `pytorch-ref`, which the caller has
# already resolved to a commit. A PR head needs nothing special - see the note
# on the checkout step. It used to branch on the event name instead, which is
# what made the relay path check out nothing at all.
#
# After checkout, the resolved commit SHA is recorded into
# `built_pytorch_sha.txt` and shipped in the same artifact as the wheel,
# so the paired test job can pin its own checkout to the exact same source
# tree without any cross-matrix output plumbing.
#
# Runners are ephemeral pre-prepped images selected by the label set
#   [<runner-base>, <python-label>, <cuda-label>]
# (e.g. [rtx-build, py312, cu130]). The narrow labels are unique to
# our self-hosted Windows pool, so the GitHub auto-tags (`self-hosted`,
# `Windows`, `X64`) are redundant and intentionally omitted. The image
# has the right Python, CUDA toolkit, MSVC, sccache, magma, ninja,
# cmake, and all PyTorch CI dependencies pre-installed - this workflow
# performs no in-job environment setup.
#
# A lightweight runner-diagnostics monitor samples host + GPU metrics in
# the background for the whole job (it starts before the long
# `pytorch/pytorch` checkout), so build-time failures - including a host
# that disappears mid-job - can be triaged against an accurate picture of
# the machine. NOTE: on a true runner shutdown the runner skips the
# `if: always()` cleanup, so the upload won't fire for that case - the
# host's Windows Event Log remains the source of truth there; this
# capture covers the soft-failure / timeout / OOM / disk-full cases.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner-base:
        description: "Base runner label for the build pool (e.g. rtx-build)."
        type: string
        required: true
      python-version:
        description: "Python version in dotted form (e.g. 3.12). Exposed as PYTHON_VERSION."
        type: string
        required: true
      python-label:
        description: "Python label used in runner labels and artifact names (e.g. py312)."
        type: string
        required: true
      cuda-version:
        description: "CUDA toolkit version in dotted form (e.g. 13.0). Exposed as CUDA_VERSION."
        type: string
        required: true
      cuda-label:
        description: "CUDA label used in runner labels and artifact names (e.g. cu130)."
        type: string
        required: true
      cuda-arch-list:
        description: >
          Semicolon-separated SM list for TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST. Use one value
          (e.g. '12.0') for an arch-specific wheel, or multiple (e.g.
          '8.9;12.0') for one wheel that fans out across architectures.
        type: string
        required: true
      build-environment:
        description: "Logical name used in BUILD_ENVIRONMENT env and the artifact name."
        type: string
        required: true
      pytorch-ref:
        description: "pytorch/pytorch ref to build (branch / tag / SHA)."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "nightly"
      wheel-artifact:
        description: >
          Artifact name to publish the built wheel + built_pytorch_sha.txt
          under. Pass the same value as `wheel-artifact` on the paired
          `_rtx-test.yml` call so the downstream test job downloads
          exactly this wheel. Empty = skip publication entirely.
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""

      # ---- matrix subset filters -------------------------------------
      # The caller cannot reference `matrix.*` in its own job-level
      # `if:` (GitHub Actions restricts that context for reusable-
      # workflow-calling jobs), so the per-cell filter is evaluated
      # here instead, against this invocation's own `python-version` /
      # `cuda-version` inputs. Empty string disables the filter.
      python-versions:
        description: "Comma-separated allowlist of python versions; empty = no filter."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""
      cuda-versions:
        description: "Comma-separated allowlist of CUDA toolkit versions; empty = no filter."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    name: build
    if: >
      (inputs.python-versions == '' || contains(inputs.python-versions, inputs.python-version))
      && (inputs.cuda-versions == '' || contains(inputs.cuda-versions, inputs.cuda-version))
    runs-on:
      - ${{ inputs.runner-base }}
      - ${{ inputs.python-label }}
      - ${{ inputs.cuda-label }}
    timeout-minutes: 300
    env:
      BUILD_ENVIRONMENT: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
      TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: ${{ inputs.cuda-arch-list }}
      PYTHON_VERSION: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
      CUDA_VERSION: ${{ inputs.cuda-version }}
      # BUILD_TEST is always on across every build config - the C++ test
      # binaries are built unconditionally and must never be disabled.
      BUILD_TEST: "1"
      # MSVC env hint and machine-specific parallelism tuning.
      DISTUTILS_USE_SDK: "1"
      MAX_JOBS: "8"
    steps:
      # This (OOT) repo carries `tools/pytorch-build/win-build.sh` and its
      # helpers (the upstream-faithful build flow). Keep it in `oot/` so the
      # parallel pytorch checkout below doesn't trample it.
      # Retried in three explicit attempts: actions/checkout gives up after
      # ~90s of internal git-fetch retries, which is shorter than an
      # observed github.com connectivity blip on this pool, and every later
      # `uses: ./oot/...` local action plus the whole build flow lives in
      # this tree.
      - name: Checkout OOT tooling repo
        id: oot_checkout_1
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          path: oot
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Wait before OOT checkout retry
        if: steps.oot_checkout_1.outcome == 'failure'
        shell: bash
        run: sleep 60

      - name: Checkout OOT tooling repo (retry 2)
        id: oot_checkout_2
        if: steps.oot_checkout_1.outcome == 'failure'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          path: oot
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Wait before final OOT checkout retry
        if: steps.oot_checkout_1.outcome == 'failure' && steps.oot_checkout_2.outcome == 'failure'
        shell: bash
        run: sleep 120

      - name: Checkout OOT tooling repo (retry 3)
        if: steps.oot_checkout_1.outcome == 'failure' && steps.oot_checkout_2.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          path: oot
          persist-credentials: false

      # Start sampling host + GPU metrics before the heavy checkout/build
      # steps so the time-series covers the exact window where the runner
      # has been observed to vanish (mid `pytorch/pytorch` fetch).
      - name: Start runner diagnostics
        id: diag
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/start-runner-diagnostics

      # One checkout for every caller, guarded by nothing.
      #
      # It used to branch on `github.event_name != 'repository_dispatch'` and
      # call `pytorch/actions/checkout-pr@v1` on the other arm. That action was
      # removed - a third-party `uses:` the org policy does not permit, see the
      # long note in `.github/actions/crcr-callback/action.yml` - but its guards
      # were left behind, so a dispatched run checked out no pytorch source at
      # all and died on the next step's `git -C pytorch rev-parse HEAD`.
      #
      # Note [A PR head needs no special checkout]
      #     The obvious replacement was a second arm fetching
      #     refs/pull/<n>/head, on the assumption that a fork's head commit is
      #     not reachable from pytorch/pytorch by SHA alone. It is: GitHub
      #     republishes PR heads in the base repo, and `git fetch <fork-PR-sha>`
      #     against pytorch/pytorch succeeds - checked directly against a live
      #     fork PR. So the caller resolving the PR to a SHA and passing it as
      #     `pytorch-ref` is all that is needed, and one unguarded path is
      #     better than two where only one is ever taken.
      - name: Checkout pytorch/pytorch
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          repository: pytorch/pytorch
          ref: ${{ inputs.pytorch-ref }}
          # Fetched by the retried step below instead - actions/checkout
          # aborts the whole step on the first submodule error with no retry
          # for that phase, and pytorch's recursive tree reaches deep
          # third-party hosts (third_party/flash-attention -> aiter ->
          # ROCm/composable_kernel) where one transient connect failure
          # discards an otherwise good clone.
          submodules: false
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false
          path: pytorch
          # Every checkout in this job sets this, because the next step runs
          # the checked-out PR's own build scripts on a self-hosted runner. A
          # token left in any `.git/config` on that filesystem - this tree or
          # the `oot` one beside it - is readable by the thing being built.
          # Nothing here pushes, so nothing needs the credential.
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Fetch pytorch submodules (retried)
        shell: bash
        working-directory: pytorch
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if git submodule update --init --recursive --depth 1 --jobs 4; then
              echo "pytorch submodules ready (attempt ${attempt})"
              exit 0
            fi
            delay=$((attempt * 60))
            echo "::warning::Submodule fetch attempt ${attempt} failed; retrying in ${delay}s."
            sleep "${delay}"
          done
          echo "::error::pytorch submodule fetch failed after 3 attempts." >&2
          exit 1

      - name: Record built SHA
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sha=$(git -C pytorch rev-parse HEAD)
          echo "$sha" > built_pytorch_sha.txt
          echo "Built from pytorch/pytorch @ $sha"

      # Upstream-faithful flow: tools/pytorch-build/win-build.sh -> build_pytorch.bat
      # -> install_magma / install_sccache / activate_miniconda3. It is env-driven
      # (no CLI args) and must run from the pytorch root, so VC tooling and CUDA
      # selection are supplied via env here. Mirrors pytorch/pytorch's in-tree
      # .ci/pytorch/win-build.sh. BUILD_TEST is on (job env), so the C++ test
      # binaries are always built.
      - name: Build PyTorch wheel (win-build.sh upstream flow)
        shell: bash
        working-directory: pytorch
        env:
          USE_CUDA: "1"
          VC_PRODUCT: "BuildTools"
          VC_YEAR: "2022"
          VC_VERSION: ""
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bash "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/oot/tools/pytorch-build/win-build.sh"

      - name: Stage wheel + sha into artifact dir
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          wheel=$(ls -1 pytorch/dist/*.whl 2>/dev/null | head -n1)
          if [ -z "$wheel" ]; then
            echo "::error::No wheel produced under pytorch/dist." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p artifact
          cp "$wheel" built_pytorch_sha.txt artifact/
          ls -la artifact

      # Publish the wheel + SHA as a GitHub Actions artifact so the paired
      # test job can download exactly this build's output.
      - name: Publish wheel + sha artifact
        if: inputs.wheel-artifact != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.wheel-artifact }}
          path: artifact
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Stop runner diagnostics
        if: always()
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/stop-runner-diagnostics
        with:
          output-dir: ${{ steps.diag.outputs.output-dir }}

      # Upload is ENABLED here (unlike `_rtx-test.yml`, which disables it):
      # the build matrix is at most ~3 cells so the artifact volume is
      # small, and these captures are the whole reason this monitor was
      # added to the build job. Skipped only when the runner is hard-killed
      # (runner shutdown bypasses `if: always()`).
      - name: Upload runner diagnostics
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: runner-diagnostics-build-${{ inputs.build-environment }}-${{ inputs.python-label }}-${{ inputs.cuda-label }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ steps.diag.outputs.output-dir }}/**
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

name: upstream-pull

# Per-PR validation of `pytorch/pytorch` pull requests, driven by the upstream
# Relay Server (RFC-0050).
#
# This workflow builds nothing itself. It receives the relay's dispatch,
# decides whether the PR is worth a maintainer's attention, asks for approval,
# and then calls both Windows pipelines pinned to the approved commit:
#
#   gate ---- author on allowlist ----> approval ----> authorize --+--> windows-rtx-build-test
#      \                              (a maintainer)   (records    |
#       `-- anyone else -> nothing                       who)      `--> _woa-pr-build-test
#                          at all
#
# The pipelines are *called*, not dispatched, so a PR validation shows up as
# one run with the build and test jobs nested inside it - the approval, the
# audit record and every job it authorised share a single page. It also means
# this workflow needs no `actions: write`, and no manual trigger has to exist
# on either pipeline for the PR path to work.
#
# Three rules, and the first two are easy to read backwards:
#
#   * Approval is always required. The allowlist decides whether a maintainer
#     is *asked* about a PR; it never lets one skip approval.
#   * Not being on the allowlist is silent - no request, no notification, no
#     run. That is what keeps the volume survivable: the relay forwards every
#     upstream PR event, on the order of one every few minutes.
#   * An approved PR runs everything. There is no per-PR choice of pipeline;
#     the decision is whether this PR gets CI, not which CI it gets.
#
# Note [Why there is no per-pipeline selection]
#     Routing on a label on the upstream PR was considered and does not work:
#     a label has to exist in `pytorch/pytorch` before it can be applied, which
#     needs write access there, and applying one needs triage permission - which
#     the contributors whose PRs this validates do not have. Creating and
#     governing such a label is upstream's call; their `.github/allowlist.yml`
#     documents `ciflow/oot/<name>` for trust level L3.
#
#     Capacity is therefore controlled by who is on the allowlist and by
#     approval being mandatory, and - if that needs to be tighter - by the
#     subset inputs passed to each pipeline below.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PR_CI_MODE - the switch that decides whether any of this is live
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Repository variable (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions):
#
#   unset / `off`  Nothing happens. Every job is skipped, so a dispatch costs
#                  nothing and appears in the Actions tab as a skipped run.
#                  This is the default, and the kill switch.
#   `live`         The allowlist applies and an approved run starts both
#                  pipelines.
#
# Anything else fails `gate` loudly, so a typo'd value cannot read as
# "quietly do nothing".
#
# It must be a *repository* variable, not an environment one: the mode is read
# in `gate`'s job-level `if:`, and `gate` declares no environment because it
# runs before the approval. An environment-scoped value resolves only for jobs
# that reference that environment, so it would read as empty and skip every
# dispatch while looking correctly configured. `UPSTREAM_PR_ALLOWLIST` is
# repository-scoped for the same reason.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dispatch payload
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two shapes are accepted, because the relay's schema moved and this has to
# keep working across the change:
#
#   nested (current, matches `inspect-dispatch-event`):
#     client_payload.payload.pull_request.number / .head.sha / .user.login
#   flat (legacy RFC-0050):
#     client_payload.pr_number / client_payload.head_sha
#
# The flat shape carries no author, so it can never satisfy the allowlist.
# That is intended, not a gap: a payload that cannot say who opened the PR is
# not one to build unattended.
#
# Both dispatch *types* are listened for, because the relay has used
# `pytorch-pr-trigger` and `pull_request`. Listening for one and being sent
# the other is indistinguishable from the relay being down.

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [pytorch-pr-trigger, pull_request]

# Every dispatch looks identical in the Actions list otherwise - GitHub titles
# a `repository_dispatch` run after its action type, so a page of them all read
# "pull_request", with no way to tell which PR each one was or whether several
# are one PR firing repeatedly.
run-name: >-
  PR #${{ github.event.client_payload.payload.pull_request.number
  || github.event.client_payload.pr_number || '?' }}
  -> ${{ github.event.client_payload.payload.pull_request.base.ref
  || github.event.client_payload.base_ref || '?' }}
  (${{ github.event.client_payload.payload.action || github.event.action }})

# One group per PR, so PRs are independent: several can await approval at once
# and several can build at once. Rate control is the allowlist's job, not the
# scheduler's.
#
# Deliberately *not* one shared group. That would serialize every PR behind one
# approval, and GitHub keeps at most one pending run per group - so a third
# dispatch cancels the second rather than joining a queue.
#
# `cancel-in-progress` supersedes a run when its own PR is pushed to again,
# which is what makes accepting `synchronize` safe rather than noisy: approval
# is granted against the head SHA shown in the run, so once that PR moves on,
# the thing that was approved is gone. A ghstack push can fire two events a
# second apart; the last one wins and nothing accumulates.
concurrency:
  group: >-
    upstream-pr-${{ github.event.client_payload.payload.pull_request.number
    || github.event.client_payload.pr_number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  # `authorize` reads this run's review history to record who approved it.
  actions: read

env:
  # Recorded in the audit line as what this approval started. Must list the
  # reusable-workflow jobs at the bottom of this file;
  # `scripts/pr-gate/tests/test_workflow_contract.py` asserts that it does, so
  # adding a pipeline without updating this is caught in lint rather than by a
  # misleading audit record.
  PIPELINES: windows-rtx-build-test.yml _woa-pr-build-test.yml

jobs:
  # ===========================================================================
  # Decide whether to ask a maintainer about this PR.
  #
  # Skipped entirely when `PR_CI_MODE` is unset or `off`, which is what makes
  # the default state free: the run is created by the dispatch, every job
  # skips, and nothing else in the file is reachable.
  #
  # Always green when it does run. "Not worth raising" is not an error, and a
  # red gate would be indistinguishable from the gate being broken. The one
  # exception is a payload it cannot parse, which is a real fault.
  # ===========================================================================
  gate:
    name: triage PR dispatch
    if: vars.PR_CI_MODE != '' && vars.PR_CI_MODE != 'off'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      proceed: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.proceed }}
      author: ${{ steps.check.outputs.author }}
      allowed: ${{ steps.check.outputs.allowed }}
      pr-number: ${{ steps.payload.outputs.pr-number }}
      # From `verify`, not `payload`: everything downstream acts on what
      # upstream says, not on what the relay claimed.
      head-sha: ${{ steps.verify.outputs.head-sha }}
      base-ref: ${{ steps.verify.outputs.base-ref }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve mode
        shell: bash
        env:
          MODE: ${{ vars.PR_CI_MODE }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "${MODE}" != "live" ]; then
            echo "::error title=PR gate::PR_CI_MODE is '${MODE}', which is not one of off / live. Fix the repository variable; refusing to guess what was meant." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "PR_CI_MODE=${MODE}"

      - name: Checkout repository (for the gate scripts)
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      # Read the payload for its *shape* only. The PR number is the one field
      # taken forward at face value, because it is what the upstream lookup
      # below is keyed on; the author, head SHA and base branch it carries are
      # kept solely to be compared against upstream's answer.
      #
      # A malformed payload is a hard error, unlike an author we do not follow:
      # a maintainer approves a specific head SHA, so a run that cannot name a
      # PR has nothing meaningful to approve.
      - name: Extract and validate the relay payload
        id: payload
        shell: bash
        env:
          NESTED_PR: ${{ github.event.client_payload.payload.pull_request.number }}
          NESTED_SHA: ${{ github.event.client_payload.payload.pull_request.head.sha }}
          NESTED_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.client_payload.payload.pull_request.user.login }}
          NESTED_BASE: ${{ github.event.client_payload.payload.pull_request.base.ref }}
          NESTED_ACTION: ${{ github.event.client_payload.payload.action }}
          FLAT_PR: ${{ github.event.client_payload.pr_number }}
          FLAT_SHA: ${{ github.event.client_payload.head_sha }}
          FLAT_BASE: ${{ github.event.client_payload.base_ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          pr="${NESTED_PR:-${FLAT_PR:-}}"
          sha="${NESTED_SHA:-${FLAT_SHA:-}}"
          author="${NESTED_AUTHOR:-}"
          base="${NESTED_BASE:-${FLAT_BASE:-}}"
          action="${NESTED_ACTION:-}"

          if ! [[ "${pr}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [ "${pr}" -le 0 ]; then
            echo "::error title=PR gate::Dispatch payload has no usable PR number (got '${pr}'). Neither client_payload.payload.pull_request.number nor client_payload.pr_number was set. The inspect-dispatch job prints what actually arrived." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! [[ "${sha}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error title=PR gate::Dispatch payload has no usable head SHA (got '${sha}'). Refusing to guess a ref to build." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

          {
            echo "pr-number=${pr}"
            echo "head-sha=${sha}"
            echo "author=${author}"
            echo "base-ref=${base}"
            echo "action=${action}"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "pytorch PR #${pr} @ ${sha}"
          echo "  author: ${author:-<none in payload>}"
          echo "  base:   ${base:-<none in payload>}"
          echo "  action: ${action:-<none in payload>}"

      # Re-derive the PR's facts from upstream rather than believing the relay.
      #
      # The summary a maintainer reads before approving is rendered from these
      # fields, so a payload that misreports them would have the approval click
      # authorise something other than what was displayed. Forgery is not the
      # concern - sending a dispatch needs write access here - but a relay that
      # is buggy, mid-schema-change or compromised is, and this costs one public
      # API call against a 5000/hour limit.
      #
      # Fails the gate if the lookup does not answer. Waving a dispatch through
      # on the payload's word when verification failed would put the gate back
      # where it started, so an unverifiable dispatch is a fault, not a skip.
      - name: Look up the PR upstream
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.payload.outputs.pr-number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if ! gh api "repos/pytorch/pytorch/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}" > pr.json; then
            echo "::error title=PR gate::Could not read pytorch/pytorch PR #${PR_NUMBER} from the API; refusing to act on the relay payload alone." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Verify the payload against upstream
        id: verify
        shell: bash
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.payload.outputs.pr-number }}
          CLAIMED_AUTHOR: ${{ steps.payload.outputs.author }}
          CLAIMED_SHA: ${{ steps.payload.outputs.head-sha }}
          CLAIMED_BASE: ${{ steps.payload.outputs.base-ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 scripts/pr-gate/verify_pr.py \
            --pr-json pr.json \
            --expect-pr "${PR_NUMBER}" \
            --payload-author "${CLAIMED_AUTHOR}" \
            --payload-head-sha "${CLAIMED_SHA}" \
            --payload-base-ref "${CLAIMED_BASE}" \
            --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" \
            --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Check PR author against allowlist
        id: check
        shell: bash
        env:
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ steps.verify.outputs.author }}
          ALLOWLIST: ${{ vars.UPSTREAM_PR_ALLOWLIST }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 scripts/pr-gate/evaluate_allowlist.py \
            --author "${PR_AUTHOR}" \
            --allowlist "${ALLOWLIST:-}" \
            --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" \
            --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Two filters run ahead of the allowlist, because they are about whether
      # the event describes a PR worth looking at rather than about who may run
      # one:
      #
      #   * Base branch. Roughly a third of upstream's open PRs target
      #     `gh/<user>/<n>/base` rather than `main` - those are ghstack
      #     intermediates, the internal plumbing of someone's stacked PR, where
      #     testing the intermediate means nothing. Release branches are
      #     excluded on the same grounds: this validates changes headed for
      #     main.
      #
      #   * Event action: `opened` or `synchronize`, the two that mean there is
      #     code to test. The relay forwards the whole `pull_request` webhook
      #     family; `closed`, `reopened`, `edited`, `assigned` and the rest are
      #     ignored.
      #
      #     Note [Why `labeled` is not accepted]
      #         Upstream's bots and maintainers apply several labels to a PR
      #         over its life (`open source`, `triaged`, `release notes: ...`).
      #         Since no label selects anything here, accepting `labeled` would
      #         raise a fresh approval request for a commit that had already
      #         been approved, every time one was added.
      #
      #     `synchronize` fires only when the head SHA changes: commits pushed,
      #     a force-push, or the head being updated from its base. It does not
      #     fire for comments, reviews, title edits or labels, and re-targeting
      #     a PR is `edited`. So every accepted one means different code.
      #
      # An absent value passes. Only the legacy flat payload omits these, and it
      # is already inert because it carries no author - blocking on absence
      # would make it invisible rather than safe.
      - name: Decide whether to raise a request
        id: decide
        shell: bash
        env:
          ALLOWED: ${{ steps.check.outputs.allowed }}
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.verify.outputs.base-ref }}
          IS_OPEN: ${{ steps.verify.outputs.is-open }}
          ACTION: ${{ steps.payload.outputs.action }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          proceed=false
          if [ "${IS_OPEN}" != "true" ]; then
            why="PR is not open upstream"
          elif [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && [ "${BASE_REF}" != "main" ]; then
            why="PR targets '${BASE_REF}', not main (ghstack intermediate or release branch)"
          elif [ -n "${ACTION}" ] && ! grep -qwF -- "${ACTION}" <<< "opened synchronize"; then
            why="event action '${ACTION}' does not introduce code to test"
          elif [ "${ALLOWED}" != "true" ]; then
            why="author is not on the allowlist"
          else
            proceed=true
            why="allowlisted author"
          fi
          echo "proceed=${proceed}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "proceed=${proceed} (${why})"
          {
            echo ""
            echo "| triage | value |"
            echo "| --- | --- |"
            echo "| base branch | \`${BASE_REF}\` |"
            echo "| open upstream | \`${IS_OPEN}\` |"
            echo "| event action | \`${ACTION:-(none in payload)}\` |"
            echo ""
            echo "**Approval request: $([ "${proceed}" = true ] && echo "raised" || echo "not raised")** - ${why}."
            if [ "${proceed}" = true ]; then
              echo ""
              echo "Approving will start: $(for p in ${PIPELINES}; do printf '`%s` ' "$p"; done)"
            fi
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # ===========================================================================
  # The approval itself. Gating is GitHub's own: this job declares
  # `environment: pr-ci-approval`, and that environment carries the required
  # reviewers (Settings -> Environments). The run parks in `waiting`, GitHub
  # notifies them, and the job only starts once one approves - so the rule is
  # enforced by the platform rather than by anything in this file, and the
  # decision lands in the run's own timeline.
  #
  # Deliberately not on a self-hosted runner: nothing has been approved at the
  # point this is queued, so it must not occupy a build pool while it waits.
  # `timeout-minutes` covers only the trivial execution after approval; the
  # wait is bounded by GitHub's 30-day cap on a pending deployment.
  # ===========================================================================
  approval:
    name: await maintainer approval
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.proceed == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    environment: pr-ci-approval
    steps:
      - name: Note that approval was granted
        shell: bash
        env:
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.author }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.pr-number }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.head-sha }}
        run: |
          echo "Approved: pytorch PR #${PR_NUMBER} @ ${HEAD_SHA} by '${PR_AUTHOR:-<none in payload>}'."
          echo "Pipelines: ${PIPELINES}."
          echo "The approver is recorded by the 'authorize' job."

  # ===========================================================================
  # The audit record. Ordered before the pipelines so no run starts without one.
  #
  # GitHub enforces the approval but does not pass the approver into the run,
  # so the review history is the only in-run source. Best-effort: the approval
  # has already happened by now, so a failure to read it is a hole in the
  # record, not a hole in the gate, and must not fail an approved run.
  # ===========================================================================
  authorize:
    name: record authorization
    needs: [gate, approval]
    if: needs.approval.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      approver: ${{ steps.record.outputs.approver }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository (for the audit script)
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      - name: Fetch this run's review history
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          if ! gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/approvals" > approvals.json; then
            echo "::warning title=PR CI authorization::Could not read this run's review history; the approver will be recorded as 'unknown'."
            printf '[]' > approvals.json
          fi

      - name: Record the authorization
        id: record
        shell: bash
        env:
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.author }}
          ALLOWLISTED: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.allowed }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.pr-number }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.head-sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 scripts/pr-gate/summarize_authorization.py \
            --author "${PR_AUTHOR}" \
            --allowlisted "${ALLOWLISTED}" \
            --approvals-json approvals.json \
            --environment pr-ci-approval \
            --pr-number "${PR_NUMBER}" \
            --head-sha "${HEAD_SHA}" \
            --targets "${PIPELINES}" \
            --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" \
            --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # ===========================================================================
  # The pipelines. Both run for every approved PR - see Note [Why there is no
  # per-pipeline selection].
  #
  # `pytorch-ref` is the head SHA the gate validated and the maintainer
  # approved, not the PR number: both pipelines pass a full SHA straight
  # through to their build workflow, and a fork PR's head commit is fetchable
  # from `pytorch/pytorch` because GitHub republishes it under `refs/pull/*`.
  # Pinning the SHA tests exactly what was approved, rather than re-resolving
  # the PR head and possibly building a commit that landed afterwards.
  #
  # Neither call opts out of HUD reporting, because neither can reach it. The
  # RTX `prep` leaves `crcr-delivery-id` empty for an explicit non-nightly
  # `pytorch-ref`, and also clears it for any event that is not `schedule`.
  # The WoA PR pipeline, `_woa-pr-build-test.yml`, has no reporting jobs at
  # all - nor the nightly's publication job, whose `contents: write` this path
  # would otherwise have to grant. A PR run cannot file a row against an
  # upstream commit, or publish a wheel.
  #
  # Both are named in `PIPELINES` above, which the audit record reports and a
  # contract test keeps in step with these jobs.
  #
  # Note [Why rtx grants id-token: write when nothing here mints a token]
  #     The RTX pipeline's two CRCR reporting jobs declare `id-token: write` for
  #     the OIDC handshake, and GitHub validates a called workflow's permission
  #     requests against the caller *at parse time, for every nested job,
  #     before any `if:` is evaluated*. So a caller that grants less is rejected
  #     with "The nested job 'report-build-crcr' is requesting 'id-token:
  #     write', but is only allowed 'id-token: none'" - a startup failure that
  #     takes out the whole run, not a skipped job.
  #
  #     Granting it does not let a PR run reach the HUD. Those jobs are still
  #     gated on a non-empty `crcr-delivery-id`, which `prep` leaves empty for a
  #     non-nightly ref, so they skip and no token is ever minted. The grant
  #     satisfies a static check; it is not a capability this path exercises.
  #
  #     Granted per job rather than workflow-wide so `gate`, `approval` and
  #     `authorize` keep the smaller token they actually need.
  #     `test_upstream_pull_contract.py` asserts these stay a superset of what
  #     the called workflows ask for.
  # ===========================================================================
  rtx:
    name: windows-rtx-build-test
    needs: [gate, authorize]
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      id-token: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/windows-rtx-build-test.yml
    with:
      pytorch-ref: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.head-sha }}

  # Named for the nightly it mirrors, so its jobs read the same as the nightly's.
  woa:
    name: windows-woa-build-test
    needs: [gate, authorize]
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_woa-pr-build-test.yml
    with:
      pytorch-ref: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.head-sha }}

  # ===========================================================================
  # Observability: render the relay payload (table + full event JSON) into the
  # run's step summary, so the exact shape and dispatch type that arrived is
  # visible. Independent of the gate's decision, so a payload that failed
  # validation or an author we do not follow still leaves a record.
  #
  # Carries the same mode guard as `gate`: in the default `off` state a dispatch
  # should cost nothing at all, and this would otherwise run a job for every
  # upstream PR event.
  # ===========================================================================
  inspect-dispatch:
    name: inspect upstream PR dispatch
    if: vars.PR_CI_MODE != '' && vars.PR_CI_MODE != 'off'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository (for composite actions)
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false

      - name: Inspect repository_dispatch event
        uses: ./.github/actions/inspect-dispatch-event

name: lint

# Cheap PR-time check:
#   * `yaml`       - every workflow YAML in `.github/workflows` is syntactically
#                    valid, matches the GitHub Actions schema, and offers no
#                    manual (`workflow_dispatch`) trigger.
#   * `powershell` - the vendored WoA build/test library under `tools/woa-build`
#                    parses and passes PSScriptAnalyzer (errors fail the job).
#   * `scripts`    - unit tests for the python helpers under `scripts/` that the
#                    workflows call (test summarisation, CRCR HUD reporting).
# Catches broken workflows / scripts before they reach a real build/test runner.
# All jobs run on ubuntu-latest (has python + pwsh preinstalled).

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - ".github/**"
      - "tools/woa-build/**"
      - "scripts/**"
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - ".github/**"
      - "tools/woa-build/**"
      - "scripts/**"
  # No `workflow_dispatch`: no workflow in this repo can be started by hand. A
  # lint run can still be repeated with "Re-run jobs" on the PR or push that
  # started it.


concurrency:
  group: lint-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  yaml:
    name: validate workflow YAML
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          show-progress: false

      - name: Install validators
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python -m pip install --user --quiet "PyYAML>=6" "check-jsonschema>=0.29"

      - name: YAML syntax check
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python - <<'PY'
          import sys, pathlib, yaml
          bad = 0
          for p in pathlib.Path(".github").rglob("*.yml"):
              try:
                  yaml.safe_load(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                  print(f"OK   {p}")
              except yaml.YAMLError as e:
                  print(f"FAIL {p}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
                  bad += 1
          sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
          PY

      - name: Validate workflow schema
        shell: bash
        run: |
          check-jsonschema --builtin-schema vendor.github-workflows \
            .github/workflows/*.yml

      # External-CI security guidelines do not allow a hand-started run, so no
      # workflow here may offer `workflow_dispatch`. Enforced rather than only
      # documented, because re-adding the trigger is a two-line change that
      # nothing else would flag.
      - name: No manual triggers
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python - <<'PY'
          import pathlib, sys, yaml
          bad = []
          for p in sorted(pathlib.Path(".github/workflows").glob("*.y*ml")):
              # `on` parses as the boolean True in YAML 1.1.
              on = yaml.safe_load(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get(True)
              events = on if isinstance(on, (dict, list)) else [on]
              if "workflow_dispatch" in events:
                  bad.append(p)
          for p in bad:
              print(f"::error file={p}::{p.name} offers workflow_dispatch; manual triggers are not allowed in this repo")
          sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
          PY

  # The workflows above call these helpers to decide what gets reported as a
  # pass or a failure - including, for `scripts/crcr`, what gets published to
  # the upstream PyTorch HUD. Their fail-closed behaviour is only worth
  # anything if it is actually enforced, so run their tests on every change.
  #
  # Runs on Linux because that is where these helpers run in production: the
  # reporting and summary jobs are all `ubuntu-latest`. The exception is
  # `scripts/test-bounds`, which bounds a hung test *on the Windows shards*;
  # the handful of its cases that assert the `taskkill` path are marked
  # Windows-only and report as skipped here.
  scripts:
    name: unit-test CI scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          show-progress: false

      - name: Install pytest
        shell: bash
        run: python -m pip install --user --quiet "pytest>=7"

      - name: Run script unit tests
        shell: bash
        run: python -m pytest scripts -q

  powershell:
    name: lint PowerShell (woa-build)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          show-progress: false

      # Syntax gate: parse every .ps1 with the PowerShell parser. Guaranteed to
      # catch a broken re-vendor or a bad entrypoint edit regardless of platform.
      - name: Parse-check all .ps1
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $bad = 0
          Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter *.ps1 tools/woa-build | ForEach-Object {
            $errors = $null
            [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile($_.FullName, [ref]$null, [ref]$errors) | Out-Null
            if ($errors -and $errors.Count -gt 0) {
              $bad++
              Write-Host "::error file=$($_.FullName)::$($errors.Count) parse error(s)"
              $errors | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  $($_.Extent.StartLineNumber): $($_.Message)" }
            }
          }
          if ($bad -gt 0) { throw "$bad file(s) with parse errors" }

      # Style/quality gate: PSScriptAnalyzer. Errors fail the job; warnings are
      # surfaced as PR annotations but do not block (the vendored code is authored
      # against PSSA and carries targeted suppressions).
      - name: PSScriptAnalyzer
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          Set-PSRepository -Name PSGallery -InstallationPolicy Trusted
          Install-Module PSScriptAnalyzer -Scope CurrentUser -Force
          $res = @(Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Path tools/woa-build -Recurse `
            -Settings tools/woa-build/PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1)
          if ($res.Count -gt 0) {
            $res | Sort-Object Severity, ScriptName, Line |
              Format-Table Severity, RuleName, ScriptName, Line, Message -AutoSize |
              Out-String -Width 240 | Write-Host
          }
          foreach ($w in @($res | Where-Object Severity -eq 'Warning')) {
            Write-Host "::warning file=$($w.ScriptPath),line=$($w.Line)::[$($w.RuleName)] $($w.Message)"
          }
          $errs = @($res | Where-Object Severity -eq 'Error')
          foreach ($e in $errs) {
            Write-Host "::error file=$($e.ScriptPath),line=$($e.Line)::[$($e.RuleName)] $($e.Message)"
          }
          if ($errs.Count -gt 0) { throw "PSScriptAnalyzer reported $($errs.Count) error(s)" }
          Write-Host "PSScriptAnalyzer: no errors ($($res.Count) finding(s) total)."

name: _woa-build

# Reusable Windows-on-Arm (WoA) build workflow. The arm64 analog of
# `_rtx-build.yml`, driven by the PowerShell build library under
# `tools/woa-build/**`.
#
# One invocation builds ONE Python cell for CTK 13.4 and produces the full P0
# set of wheels:
#     torch (vanilla) -> torch (cuda_embed, DLLs embedded)
#       -> torchaudio -> torchvision
# The two extensions are P0 but non-blocking: `continue-on-error: true` lets a
# failed extension keep the run going (build the sibling extension + upload the
# torch wheel), and a final gate step then reflects any extension failure as a RED
# build job. So an extension failure SHOWS as a failed job (like a failing test
# shard) yet never blocks the torch wheel or the other python cells (fail-fast:false).
#
# Runners: a single PERSISTENT, shared arm64 pool tagged `woa-arm64` (no runner
# image, no per-pipeline CTK update). Every runner has MSVC arm64, CUDA 13.4 +
# cuDNN and the clean ARM64 CPython interpreters (py311..py314 plus free-threaded
# py314t) preinstalled - but NO pre-built venvs. `woa-preflight-build` verifies the
# toolchain paths, `woa-create-venv` builds a FRESH throwaway venv for this job from
# the clean interpreter (public-facing runners: nothing a job installs persists), and
# `woa-strict-clean` scrubs job-produced state (including that venv) at start and end.
#
# The resolved pytorch commit SHA is recorded into `built_pytorch_sha.txt` and
# shipped in the wheel artifact so the paired test cell pins the exact source.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner-base:
        description: "Runner label for the shared WoA build+test pool."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "woa-arm64"
      python-version:
        description: "Python version in dotted form (e.g. 3.13). Exposed as PYTHON_VERSION."
        type: string
        required: true
      python-label:
        description: "Python label (py311 | py312 | py313 | py314 | py314t); selects the venv + names the artifact."
        type: string
        required: true
      cuda-version:
        description: "CUDA toolkit version in dotted form (13.4). Exposed as CUDA_VERSION."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "13.4"
      cuda-arch-list:
        description: "TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST for the arm64 wheel."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "8.9;10.3+PTX;12.0;12.1+PTX"
      build-environment:
        description: "Logical name used in BUILD_ENVIRONMENT and the artifact name."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "win-woa-arm64"
      pytorch-ref:
        description: "pytorch/pytorch commit to build. MUST be a full 40-hex commit SHA (enforced below). The orchestrator prep resolves branches/tags to a SHA; direct callers must pass a SHA (required, no default, so a symbolic ref cannot slip past the guard)."
        type: string
        required: true
      nightly-date:
        description: "Nightly wheel version date in yyyyMMdd format."
        type: string
        required: true
      torchaudio-ref:
        description: "torchaudio (pytorch/audio) commit to build. Resolved to a SHA by the orchestrator prep; empty = clone the remote default branch (direct-caller fallback)."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""
      torchvision-ref:
        description: "torchvision (pytorch/vision) commit to build. Resolved to a SHA by the orchestrator prep; empty = clone the remote default branch (direct-caller fallback)."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""
      wheel-artifact:
        description: >
          Artifact name to publish the wheels + built_pytorch_sha.txt under.
          Pass the same value on the paired `_woa-test.yml` call. Empty = skip.
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""

      # ---- matrix subset filter (see _rtx-build.yml rationale) ---------------
      python-versions:
        description: "Comma-separated allowlist of python versions; empty = no filter."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: ""

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    name: build
    # Token-exact match (comma-delimited) so "3.14" does not also match "3.14t".
    if: >
      inputs.python-versions == '' ||
      contains(format(',{0},', inputs.python-versions), format(',{0},', inputs.python-version))
    runs-on:
      - ${{ inputs.runner-base }}
    timeout-minutes: 360
    env:
      BUILD_ENVIRONMENT: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
      TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: ${{ inputs.cuda-arch-list }}
      # Extension (torchaudio/torchvision) arch for the ctk134_py313 build variant.
      # The cpp_extension arch allowlist rejects the 'f' family suffix, so
      # the torch list stays suffix-free (explicit 12.1, not 12.0f); the CMAKE arch
      # list uses the compact family form (89 Ada, 103a, 120f covers 12.0/12.1).
      # Read directly by the vendored ExtensionBuildPipeline via Resolve-CiEnv.
      EXT_WIN_CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES: "89;103a;120f"
      EXT_WIN_TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: ${{ inputs.cuda-arch-list }}
      PYTHON_VERSION: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
      PYTHON_LABEL: ${{ inputs.python-label }}
      CUDA_VERSION: ${{ inputs.cuda-version }}
      NIGHTLY_DATE: ${{ inputs.nightly-date }}
      BUILD_TEST: "1"
      DISTUTILS_USE_SDK: "1"
      # Pinned extension source commits (resolved by the orchestrator prep); empty
      # falls back to the remote default branch. Read by the vendored extension
      # pipeline via Resolve-CiEnv.
      TORCHAUDIO_WIN_GIT_REF: ${{ inputs.torchaudio-ref }}
      TORCHVISION_WIN_GIT_REF: ${{ inputs.torchvision-ref }}
      # ---- WoA preinstall contract (single-drive C: runners; see docs/woa-ci-plan.md) ----
      # Expected install paths on every woa-arm64 runner: CTK/cuDNN under
      # C:\Program Files\NVIDIA, tools/vcpkg/APL under C:\DevToolKit.
      WOA_CUDA_PATH: 'C:\Program Files\NVIDIA\CUDA\v13.4'
      WOA_CUDNN_ROOT: 'C:\Program Files\NVIDIA\CUDNN\v9.26'
      # arm64 MSVC entry point verified by woa-preflight-build (fail fast if absent).
      # VS 2026 BuildTools: install root is major version 18, outside the '(x86)' prefix.
      WOA_VCVARS_BAT: 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvarsarm64.bat'
      # Short relocated checkout root + job scratch on C: (MAX_PATH + space; runners are C: only).
      PT_ROOT: 'C:\pt'
      WOA_SCRATCH: 'C:\ci\woa\scratch'
      # The per-job venv is built fresh here (under scratch, so strict-clean wipes it) and
      # the pip cache is pinned inside scratch too - no cross-job wheel cache survives on
      # these public-facing runners (avoids a shared-cache poisoning vector).
      WOA_VENV_DIR: 'C:\ci\woa\scratch\venv'
      PIP_CACHE_DIR: 'C:\ci\woa\scratch\pipcache'
    steps:
      # Keep the OOT tooling in oot/ so the parallel pytorch checkout can't
      # trample it, and so the composite actions resolve at ./oot/.github/...
      - name: Checkout OOT tooling repo
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          path: oot
          show-progress: false
          # Don't leave the job token in oot/.git/config while the build (and any
          # third-party build code) runs; this checkout only needs read access now.
          persist-credentials: false

      # Persistent shared runner -> scrub any leftover job state BEFORE work.
      - name: Strict clean (pre)
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/woa-strict-clean
        with:
          phase: pre
          pt-root: ${{ env.PT_ROOT }}
          scratch-root: ${{ env.WOA_SCRATCH }}

      # Verify the preinstalled toolchain + a clean ARM64 interpreter for this python
      # label (NO install, NO CTK update). Fails fast on a misprovisioned runner.
      - name: Preflight build toolchain
        id: preflight
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/woa-preflight-build
        with:
          python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
          python-label: ${{ inputs.python-label }}
          cuda-path: ${{ env.WOA_CUDA_PATH }}
          cudnn-root: ${{ env.WOA_CUDNN_ROOT }}
          vcvars-bat: ${{ env.WOA_VCVARS_BAT }}

      # Build a FRESH, throwaway venv for this job from the clean interpreter and install the
      # WoA BUILD deps (woa-base.txt + woa-build.txt, strict - no test harness/domain stack).
      # It lives under scratch so strict-clean wipes it at job end - the runner keeps only
      # clean interpreters.
      - name: Create job venv
        id: venv
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/woa-create-venv
        with:
          role: build
          python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
          python-label: ${{ inputs.python-label }}
          venv-path: ${{ env.WOA_VENV_DIR }}\${{ inputs.python-label }}

      - name: Start runner diagnostics
        id: diag
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/start-runner-diagnostics

      - name: Enable git long paths
        shell: bash
        run: git config --global core.longpaths true

      # Enforce commit SHA pinning: the source checkout MUST be a full 40-hex
      # commit SHA (not a moving branch/tag). The orchestrator resolves the ref in
      # prep; this guard also protects direct reusable-workflow callers. A full SHA
      # makes the checkout deterministic and integrity-checked (Git objects are
      # content-addressed) across every build cell.
      - name: Enforce commit SHA pinning
        shell: bash
        env:
          PYTORCH_REF: ${{ inputs.pytorch-ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if ! [[ "${PYTORCH_REF}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error title=Unpinned pytorch source::pytorch-ref must be a full 40-hex commit SHA for a pinned, integrity-checked checkout; got '${PYTORCH_REF}'. The orchestrator prep resolves branches/tags to a SHA before calling this workflow." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "pytorch source is SHA-pinned: ${PYTORCH_REF}"

      # actions/checkout clones over HTTPS/TLS (no SSH; credentials not persisted).
      # `ref` is a full commit SHA (see the guard above), so the fetch is pinned.
      - name: Checkout pytorch/pytorch
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          repository: pytorch/pytorch
          ref: ${{ inputs.pytorch-ref }}
          submodules: recursive
          fetch-depth: 1
          show-progress: false
          path: pytorch
          persist-credentials: false

      # MAX_PATH mitigation: relocate the deep pytorch tree to the short root
      # PT_ROOT (C:\pt). Same-volume move is an atomic rename; the strict-clean
      # above already emptied C:\pt.
      - name: Relocate pytorch checkout to a short path
        shell: cmd
        run: |
          move "%GITHUB_WORKSPACE%\pytorch" "%PT_ROOT%"
          if errorlevel 1 (
            echo ::error::Failed to relocate pytorch checkout to %PT_ROOT%
            exit /b 1
          )
          echo Relocated pytorch checkout to %PT_ROOT%

      - name: Record built SHA
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sha=$(git -C "${PT_ROOT}" rev-parse HEAD)
          echo "$sha" > built_pytorch_sha.txt
          echo "Built from pytorch/pytorch @ $sha"

      - name: Set nightly torch wheel version
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          if ($env:NIGHTLY_DATE -notmatch '^\d{8}$') {
            throw "nightly-date must use yyyyMMdd format; got '$env:NIGHTLY_DATE'"
          }
          $versionFile = "$env:PT_ROOT\version.txt"
          if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $versionFile)) {
            throw "version.txt not found at '$versionFile'; cannot derive the nightly wheel version"
          }
          $base = (Get-Content $versionFile -Raw).Trim() -replace 'a0$', ''
          if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($base)) {
            throw "version.txt at '$versionFile' is empty; cannot derive the nightly wheel version"
          }
          $cuda = $env:CUDA_VERSION -replace '\.', ''
          $version = "${base}.dev$env:NIGHTLY_DATE+cu$cuda"
          "PYTORCH_BUILD_VERSION=$version" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV
          "PYTORCH_BUILD_NUMBER=1" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV
          Write-Host "Building torch $version"

      # ---- P0 build chain (PowerShell library vendored in Phase 2) -----------
      # Each step activates the fresh per-job venv built by `woa-create-venv`, then calls
      # the vendored entrypoint. Wheels are written into WOA_SCRATCH\dist.
      - name: Build torch wheel (vanilla + cuda_embed)
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          VENV_ACTIVATE: ${{ steps.venv.outputs.venv-activate }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $out = Join-Path $env:WOA_SCRATCH "dist"
          & "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\oot\tools\woa-build\torch-build-flow.ps1" `
            -PytorchRoot $env:PT_ROOT -OutputDir $out -VenvActivate $env:VENV_ACTIVATE
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }

      # Extensions are P0 but NON-BLOCKING: continue-on-error lets a failed extension
      # keep the run going (build the sibling + upload the torch wheel); the
      # "Reflect extension build status" gate below turns any extension failure into a
      # RED build job afterwards, so the failure SHOWS without blocking the torch wheel
      # or other cells. The step ids feed that gate's outcome check.
      - name: Build torchaudio (extension)
        id: torchaudio
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          VENV_ACTIVATE: ${{ steps.venv.outputs.venv-activate }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $out = Join-Path $env:WOA_SCRATCH "dist"
          & "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\oot\tools\woa-build\torchaudio\build-pipeline.ps1" `
            -OutputDir $out -VenvActivate $env:VENV_ACTIVATE
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }

      - name: Build torchvision (extension)
        id: torchvision
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          VENV_ACTIVATE: ${{ steps.venv.outputs.venv-activate }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $out = Join-Path $env:WOA_SCRATCH "dist"
          & "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\oot\tools\woa-build\torchvision\build-pipeline.ps1" `
            -OutputDir $out -VenvActivate $env:VENV_ACTIVATE
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }

      - name: Stage wheels + sha into artifact dir
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          dist="${WOA_SCRATCH}/dist"
          mkdir -p artifact
          shopt -s nullglob
          wheels=("$dist"/*.whl)
          if [ ${#wheels[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::No wheels produced under ${dist}." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          expected=".dev${NIGHTLY_DATE}+cu${CUDA_VERSION//./}"
          for wheel in "${wheels[@]}"; do
            if [[ "$(basename "$wheel")" != *"${expected}-"* ]]; then
              echo "::error::Wheel does not use nightly naming '${expected}': $(basename "$wheel")" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          cp "${wheels[@]}" built_pytorch_sha.txt artifact/
          ls -la artifact

      - name: Publish wheels + sha artifact
        if: inputs.wheel-artifact != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.wheel-artifact }}
          path: artifact
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14
          # The name is stable across run attempts (run_id only, no run_attempt) so a
          # test-only "Re-run failed jobs" can still find it. overwrite lets a full
          # "Re-run all jobs" (which re-runs this build) replace the prior attempt's
          # artifact instead of failing with a 409 name collision.
          overwrite: true

      # Reflect extension build status: the extensions ran with continue-on-error so a
      # failure did NOT skip the sibling extension or the wheel upload above. Now that the
      # torch wheel is published, fail the build job if either extension failed, so the
      # status SHOWS the failure (same principle as a failing test shard). This is still
      # non-blocking: fail-fast:false on the build matrix keeps the other python cells
      # running, and the torch wheel + artifact are already uploaded. Runs on always() so
      # the outcome is surfaced even if a later always() step misbehaves; a skipped
      # extension (e.g. torch build failed earlier) is not a failure.
      - name: Reflect extension build status
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        env:
          TORCHAUDIO_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.torchaudio.outcome }}
          TORCHVISION_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.torchvision.outcome }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          failed=""
          [ "${TORCHAUDIO_OUTCOME}" = "failure" ]  && failed="${failed} torchaudio"
          [ "${TORCHVISION_OUTCOME}" = "failure" ] && failed="${failed} torchvision"
          if [ -n "${failed}" ]; then
            echo "::error title=Extension build failed::P0 extension(s) failed:${failed}. The torch wheel was still built + uploaded and the other python cells are unaffected (non-blocking); failing this build job so its status reflects the extension failure." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "extensions ok (or skipped): torchaudio=${TORCHAUDIO_OUTCOME}, torchvision=${TORCHVISION_OUTCOME}"

      - name: Stop runner diagnostics
        if: always()
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/stop-runner-diagnostics
        with:
          output-dir: ${{ steps.diag.outputs.output-dir }}

      - name: Upload runner diagnostics
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: runner-diagnostics-woa-build-${{ inputs.python-label }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ steps.diag.outputs.output-dir }}/**
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

      # Detailed build transcripts (pip-wheel / delvewheel per stage + the WHEEL_OUT_ROOT
      # marker) that the flow writes under $CI_PROJECT_DIR/logs (== workspace/logs). These
      # are the same lines now streamed live to the job log via Invoke-CmdLogged|Out-Host,
      # but a durable artifact lets you download them post-run for triage even if the job
      # log is truncated or the runner rebooted mid-build. Runs on success AND failure.
      - name: Upload build logs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: build-logs-woa-${{ inputs.python-label }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/logs/**
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

      # Post-job strict scrub of everything this job produced/downloaded. Runs
      # even on failure; skipped only on a hard runner shutdown (bypasses always()).
      - name: Strict clean (post)
        if: always()
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/woa-strict-clean
        with:
          phase: post
          pt-root: ${{ env.PT_ROOT }}
          scratch-root: ${{ env.WOA_SCRATCH }}
          extra-paths: ${{ github.workspace }}/artifact

name: _woa-sign

# Sign one python cell's WoA wheel set with Azure Artifact Signing, then prove the
# signed wheels still install and run on WoA hardware.
#
# TWO JOBS ON TWO MACHINES, ON PURPOSE.
#   sign      GitHub-hosted `windows-2025`. The signing identity is a GitHub OIDC token
#             federated to Entra, scoped to the `woa-signing` environment, so no signing
#             credential ever exists on the persistent self-hosted WoA runners - the
#             risk this design accepts for everything else. x64 signtool signs ARM64
#             PE files fine; what it cannot do is run them.
#   validate  The WoA runner pool, because only WoA hardware with a GPU can import the
#             signed win_arm64 wheels and run CUDA. It holds no credentials at all.
#
# Keeping build, signing and publication in separate jobs means the build job never
# gains signing authority, and neither of these gains publication authority.
# Publication lives in `_woa-publish.yml`, and it only accepts wheels this workflow
# validated.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner-base:
        description: "Runner label for the WoA validation job (the WoA runner pool). Signing always runs on GitHub-hosted windows-2025."
        type: string
        required: false
        default: "woa-arm64"
      python-version:
        description: "Dotted Python version of the cell (3.11 | 3.12 | 3.13 | 3.14 | 3.14t)."
        type: string
        required: true
      python-label:
        description: "Python label of the cell (py311 | ... | py314t)."
        type: string
        required: true
      build-run-id:
        description: "The windows-woa-build-test run that built the wheels (vetted by scripts/publish/build_run.py)."
        type: string
        required: true
      unsigned-artifact-id:
        description: "Id of the build cell's wheel artifact in that run, as scripts/publish/build_run.py vetted it: the one its build job uploaded."
        type: string
        required: true
      unsigned-files:
        description: "JSON {path: sha256} of every file in that artifact, as the resolve job hashed it. Nothing else is signed."
        type: string
        required: true
      signed-artifact:
        description: "Artifact name for the signed wheels, manifest and signature report."
        type: string
        required: true
      validation-artifact:
        description: "Artifact name for the WoA validation report."
        type: string
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  sign:
    name: sign
    runs-on: windows-2025
    # The Entra federated credential is bound to this environment name, so it is part
    # of the signing identity: renaming it means a new federated credential.
    environment: woa-signing
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      # The unsigned wheels live in the build run, not this one.
      actions: read
      # Provenance for what this job signed; see scripts/publish/attestations.py.
      attestations: write
    timeout-minutes: 90
    outputs:
      signed-artifact-id: ${{ steps.upload.outputs.artifact-id }}
      signed-files: ${{ steps.signed-files.outputs.files }}
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: pwsh
    steps:
      - name: Checkout OOT tooling repo
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          path: oot
          show-progress: false
          persist-credentials: false

      # Fail in seconds, with a pointer to the fix, until the Artifact Signing account,
      # certificate profile and federated credential are provisioned.
      - name: Require Azure Artifact Signing configuration
        env:
          AZURE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          AZURE_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ vars.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
          AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_ENDPOINT: ${{ vars.AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_ENDPOINT }}
          AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_ACCOUNT: ${{ vars.AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_ACCOUNT }}
          AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_PROFILE: ${{ vars.AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_PROFILE }}
          WOA_EXPECTED_SIGNER_SUBJECT: ${{ vars.WOA_EXPECTED_SIGNER_SUBJECT }}
        run: |
          $names = 'AZURE_CLIENT_ID', 'AZURE_TENANT_ID', 'AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID',
            'AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_ENDPOINT', 'AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_ACCOUNT', 'AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_PROFILE',
            'WOA_EXPECTED_SIGNER_SUBJECT'
          $missing = @($names | Where-Object { [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable($_)) })
          if ($missing.Count -gt 0) {
            Write-Host "::error title=Azure Artifact Signing is not configured::Missing repository variables: $($missing -join ', '). See docs/woa-wheel-publishing.md."
            exit 1
          }

      # By id, not name: see Note [Sign the build job's own upload, by id] in build_run.py.
      - name: Download unsigned wheels from the build run
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          artifact-ids: ${{ inputs.unsigned-artifact-id }}
          merge-multiple: true
          digest-mismatch: error
          run-id: ${{ inputs.build-run-id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          path: incoming

      # Before any signing token exists: see Note [The unsigned files are hashed before
      # signing, on a hosted runner] in build_run.py.
      - name: Check the unsigned files against the resolve job's hashes
        env:
          UNSIGNED_FILES: ${{ inputs.unsigned-files }}
        run: python oot/scripts/publish/digests.py check --dir incoming --expected-env UNSIGNED_FILES

      - name: Unpack wheels for signing
        run: python oot/scripts/publish/wheel_repack.py unpack --wheel-dir incoming --work-dir "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\sign"

      - name: Authenticate to Azure with GitHub OIDC
        uses: azure/login@a641126d1b8aa4d1fa005f4f92df94a3a4c4c906 # v3.1.0
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}

      # .pyd and .node are PE DLLs under another name and carry most of the file count;
      # the example filter (exe,dll,msix) would leave them unsigned, which repack refuses.
      # timeout bounds each signtool batch, not the step: a torch batch is about 150 files
      # at roughly 2.3 s each, so the 300 s default kills it partway through.
      - name: Sign native binaries with Azure Artifact Signing
        uses: azure/artifact-signing-action@c7ab2a863ab5f9a846ddb8265964877ef296ee82 # v2
        with:
          endpoint: ${{ vars.AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_ENDPOINT }}
          signing-account-name: ${{ vars.AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_ACCOUNT }}
          certificate-profile-name: ${{ vars.AZURE_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_PROFILE }}
          files-folder: ${{ runner.temp }}\sign\unpacked
          files-folder-filter: dll,pyd,exe,node
          files-folder-recurse: true
          file-digest: SHA256
          timestamp-rfc3161: http://timestamp.acs.microsoft.com
          timestamp-digest: SHA256
          timeout: 1800

      - name: Repack signed wheels
        run: |
          python oot/scripts/publish/wheel_repack.py repack `
            --work-dir "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\sign" --out-dir signed `
            --manifest "signed/release-manifest-${{ inputs.python-label }}.json" `
            --cell "${{ inputs.python-label }}" --pytorch-sha-file incoming/built_pytorch_sha.txt `
            --build-run-id "${{ inputs.build-run-id }}"

      - name: Verify signatures in the repacked wheels
        env:
          EXPECTED_SUBJECT: ${{ vars.WOA_EXPECTED_SIGNER_SUBJECT }}
        run: |
          ./oot/tools/woa-build/verify-wheel-signatures.ps1 -WheelDir signed `
            -ReportPath "signed/signature-report-${{ inputs.python-label }}.json" `
            -ExpectedSubject "$env:EXPECTED_SUBJECT"

      # Nothing in this job installs from PyPI: it runs with the signing session and
      # before the attestation, so it could rewrite what gets attested. `twine check`
      # runs in validate, which holds no credentials.

      # The release job accepts only files carrying this job's attestation: other jobs
      # in the run, including the self-hosted ones, can replace the artifact uploaded below.
      - name: Attest the signed wheels and their evidence
        uses: actions/attest@1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: |
            signed/*.whl
            signed/release-manifest-${{ inputs.python-label }}.json
            signed/signature-report-${{ inputs.python-label }}.json

      # validate trusts these job outputs, not the artifact's name, which any job can reuse.
      - name: Record the signed files' SHA-256
        id: signed-files
        run: python oot/scripts/publish/digests.py hash --dir signed --github-output "$env:GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Upload signed wheels + evidence
        id: upload
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.signed-artifact }}
          path: signed
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14
          overwrite: true

      - name: Upload signing diagnostics
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: woa-${{ inputs.python-label }}-sign-diagnostics-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: signed/*.json
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 14

  validate:
    name: validate
    needs: sign
    runs-on:
      - ${{ inputs.runner-base }}
    timeout-minutes: 90
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: pwsh
    env:
      WOA_CUDA_PATH: 'C:\Program Files\NVIDIA\CUDA\v13.4'
      WOA_CUDNN_ROOT: 'C:\Program Files\NVIDIA\CUDNN\v9.26'
      PT_ROOT: 'C:\pt'
      WOA_SCRATCH: 'C:\ci\woa\scratch'
      WOA_VENV_DIR: 'C:\ci\woa\scratch\venv'
      PIP_CACHE_DIR: 'C:\ci\woa\scratch\pipcache'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout OOT tooling repo
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7
        with:
          path: oot
          show-progress: false
          persist-credentials: false

      # The workspace root survives between jobs on these persistent runners, and the
      # validator checks every wheel under signed/, so a previous run's must be gone.
      - name: Strict clean (pre)
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/woa-strict-clean
        with:
          phase: pre
          pt-root: ${{ env.PT_ROOT }}
          scratch-root: ${{ env.WOA_SCRATCH }}
          extra-paths: |
            ${{ github.workspace }}/signed
            ${{ github.workspace }}/validation

      - name: Preflight test toolchain + GPU
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/woa-preflight-test
        with:
          python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
          python-label: ${{ inputs.python-label }}
          cuda-path: ${{ env.WOA_CUDA_PATH }}
          cudnn-root: ${{ env.WOA_CUDNN_ROOT }}

      - name: Create job venv
        id: venv
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/woa-create-venv
        with:
          role: test
          python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
          python-label: ${{ inputs.python-label }}
          venv-path: ${{ env.WOA_VENV_DIR }}\validate-${{ inputs.python-label }}

      # By the id and hashes the sign job published, so a replacement uploaded under the
      # same name by another job in the run is never what gets validated.
      - name: Download signed wheels
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          artifact-ids: ${{ needs.sign.outputs.signed-artifact-id }}
          merge-multiple: true
          digest-mismatch: error
          path: signed

      - name: Check the signed files against the sign job's hashes
        env:
          SIGNED_FILES: ${{ needs.sign.outputs.signed-files }}
        run: |
          $python = Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent "${{ steps.venv.outputs.venv-activate }}") 'python.exe'
          & $python oot/scripts/publish/digests.py check --dir signed --expected-env SIGNED_FILES
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }

      - name: Check package metadata
        run: |
          $python = Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent "${{ steps.venv.outputs.venv-activate }}") 'python.exe'
          & $python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --quiet twine==7.0.0
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
          $wheels = @(Get-ChildItem signed -Filter '*.whl' | ForEach-Object FullName)
          & $python -m twine check @wheels
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }

      - name: Validate signed wheels on WoA hardware
        env:
          EXPECTED_SUBJECT: ${{ vars.WOA_EXPECTED_SIGNER_SUBJECT }}
        run: |
          ./oot/tools/woa-build/validate-signed-wheels.ps1 -WheelDir signed `
            -VenvActivate "${{ steps.venv.outputs.venv-activate }}" `
            -ReportPath "validation/validation-${{ inputs.python-label }}.json" `
            -ExpectedSubject "$env:EXPECTED_SUBJECT"

      # Uploaded on failure too: the publish job reads `status`, so a failed report can
      # never be mistaken for a pass, and it is the record of why the cell was held back.
      - name: Upload validation report
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.validation-artifact }}
          path: validation
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14
          overwrite: true

      - name: Strict clean (post)
        if: always()
        uses: ./oot/.github/actions/woa-strict-clean
        with:
          phase: post
          pt-root: ${{ env.PT_ROOT }}
          scratch-root: ${{ env.WOA_SCRATCH }}
          extra-paths: |
            ${{ github.workspace }}/signed
            ${{ github.workspace }}/validation
